key: Each zone (Central, Western, Southern
name: ch06_railway_zone_offices
alt: A map of India split into railway zones, each with its own booking office holding only its own trains' bookings.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a large stylised map of India laid flat like a board game, divided by bold dotted borders into four coloured regions. On each region sits a small, separate railway booking office building with a red tiled roof, a ticket window and a clerk inside. Left to right: a western office with a clerk in a white shirt stamping tickets, a central office with an older clerk in spectacles flipping a thick ledger, a southern office with a young woman clerk in a green saree typing at a computer, and an eastern office with a clerk sipping tea between customers. Each office has its own short queue of passengers holding tickets, and each ledger on each desk is a different colour matching its region. Thin toy trains run only inside their own coloured region, and a dotted arrow from each train points to its own office, never to a neighbour's. In the bottom corner a new, freshly painted fifth office is being opened with a ribbon, a few passengers already walking towards it, to show that adding an office adds capacity. Bright midday light, orderly and calm mood. Labels: "ONE ZONE = ONE PARTITION" across the top edge of the map, and "NEW OFFICE" on a small banner over the ribboned building.

key: 4 subjects (partitions) and 4 teachers
name: ch06_teachers_mark_registers
alt: Four teachers in a staff room, each the main marker for one subject and holding photocopied registers of two others.
scene: A cosy Indian school staff room seen from the front, a long wooden table with four teachers seated side by side. From left to right: a middle-aged man in a grey sweater vest, a young woman in a yellow salwar kameez, an older woman with grey hair in a bun and reading glasses, and a cheerful young man in a sky-blue shirt. In front of each teacher lies one large hardbound register with a bright coloured cover (red for Maths, blue for Science, green for English, orange for Hindi) which that teacher is writing marks in with a fountain pen, a small gold crown sticker on the cover. Beside each teacher also lie two thinner photocopied registers in the colours of two other subjects, stapled at the corner, which they only read. Curved arrows run from each crowned register to its two photocopies on other teachers' desks. In the far right, one chair is empty with a coat on it (the absent teacher), yet the red and blue registers still appear elsewhere on the table, so nothing is lost. Afternoon sun through a barred window, a wall calendar and a steel water jug on the table. Labels: "LEADER" on a small tag beside one crowned register, and "FOLLOWER" beside one photocopy.

key: Exam-hall seating by roll-number range
name: ch06_exam_hall_roll_ranges
alt: Two exam halls with roll-number ranges; late admissions crowd only into the last hall while the first stays calm.
scene: A cutaway view of a school corridor with two exam halls side by side, their doors open so we can see inside. Above the left door a painted board reads "1-60", above the right door "61-120". The left hall is calm: neat rows of students in white uniforms writing quietly, an invigilator in a cardigan strolling with hands behind her back, and a small group of seats in the middle highlighted by a soft bracket marked "30-45" to show students who sit together for a range lookup. The right hall is overflowing: every bench full, extra plastic chairs crammed into the aisles, students sitting on the window sill, and a long line of new students with fresh admission slips walking down the corridor straight towards this last hall only, while the left door has nobody waiting. A flustered invigilator in the right hall holds up both hands. In a small inset bubble at the top right, the same new students are instead spread across several halls labelled by section letters, each hall getting just one or two, with a little magnifying-glass icon showing a teacher who now has to visit every hall to find them all. Bright morning light, slightly chaotic mood on the right. Labels: "HOT PARTITION" over the crowded right hall.

key: students to four houses (Red, Blue
name: ch06_school_houses_hash
alt: A school assembly where a scrambled code sends students evenly into four coloured houses, and one family stays together in date order.
scene: A school assembly ground seen from slightly above, with four neat queues standing behind four coloured flags: red, blue, green and yellow, each queue almost exactly the same length. In the foreground a teacher in a white kurta sits at a small table with a hand-cranked machine like a lottery drum that turns each child's admission slip into a jumbled number; the last digit of that number is circled and decides the flag. A line of June admissions, all holding slips dated in June, approaches the drum and comes out scattered among all four queues, shown by curving arrows going in four different directions. On the right, a worried clerk with a clipboard reading "first week of June" is having to walk to all four queues one by one, with footprints showing his long route. In the lower left corner, a small inset shows the yellow house with one family group (parents and three children with the same surname badge) standing together in a single row, their record cards clipped in date order on a string like bunting, which a teacher reads in one glance. Cheerful morning sun, dusty ground, marigold decorations on the stage. Labels: "HASH" on the side of the drum, and "SAME FAMILY TOGETHER" in the inset.

key: the temple opens 100 numbered queues
name: ch06_temple_split_queues
alt: A festival temple splits one huge crowd into many numbered queues, and at day end someone must empty every donation box.
scene: A festive temple courtyard in the evening, strings of marigolds and oil lamps everywhere, the temple gopuram glowing in the background. In the centre-left, a volunteer in a saffron kurta stands at a fork and points devotees into many parallel railed queues, each with a small numbered board ("1", "2", "3"... trailing off into the distance), so the huge crowd is spread thin and each line moves briskly. At the far end of every queue sits a small steel donation box. On the right side, in the late night after the crowd has gone, a tired temple accountant with rolled-up sleeves and a pencil behind his ear kneels on the floor surrounded by a semicircle of opened donation boxes, counting coins and notes from each box into one big brass plate, with a long tally sheet curling to the floor. Near him on a pillar hangs a small slate listing only a few dates with a tick, meaning only festival days are split. Warm lamp light, joyful crowd on the left and a weary but diligent mood on the right. Labels: "SPLIT HOT KEY" over the many queues, and "READ ALL 100" above the accountant's pile of boxes.

key: stores books on shelves by accession
name: ch06_library_catalogue_buildings
alt: A librarian walks straight to a shelf by number, while a student asks for books by one author and needs a separate catalogue across buildings.
scene: An old public library interior with tall wooden shelves, each shelf end carrying a brass plate with number ranges. On the left, a calm librarian in a cardigan and half-moon spectacles holds a slip with a number and walks straight down one aisle to exactly the right shelf, a dotted line marking her direct path. In the centre at the issue desk, a college student with a backpack and a notebook asks a question, and a speech bubble above shows a closed book cover with an author silhouette and a question mark, meaning "all books by this author". Beside the desk stands a wooden card-catalogue cabinet with many small drawers, one drawer pulled out, its cards sorted by author names, glowing softly as the key extra tool. Through a large window in the background, three more library buildings are visible across a courtyard, each with its own shelves, and a question mark hovers over the courtyard asking where the catalogue cabinet should live when books are spread across all these buildings. Soft late-afternoon light, dust in the air, quiet and studious mood. Labels: "PRIMARY KEY" over the numbered shelves, and "SECONDARY INDEX" on the catalogue cabinet.

key: old telephone directory for a big city
name: ch06_phone_directory_volumes
alt: Two thick telephone directory volumes split by surname letters, while a newly moved family is not printed in them yet.
scene: A warm living room scene split into foreground and background. In the foreground on a coffee table lie two thick old telephone directories with yellowed edges, one spine marked "A-M" and the other "N-Z". An elderly man in a cardigan sits in an armchair with one volume open on his lap, his finger running down a long column of identical surnames, finding them quickly. Behind him through the window, a moving truck is parked outside a neighbouring house and a young family is carrying boxes and a potted plant inside. Between the two scenes a dotted path leads from the new family to a small printing press in a distant building, where a printer in an apron is slowly setting type, a large wall calendar beside him showing several weeks crossed out. In a thought bubble above the old man, a page of the directory shows an empty gap where the new family's line should be, with a small "not in the book yet" feel conveyed by a blank line and a question mark. Late afternoon golden light, nostalgic and patient mood. Labels: "GLOBAL INDEX" on a ribbon across the two directories, and "UPDATED LATER" above the distant printing press.

key: A chain of kirana shops delivers to
name: ch06_kirana_new_shop_rebalance
alt: A new kirana shop opens and takes just a few customers from each existing shop while milk deliveries continue.
scene: A bird's-eye illustration of a residential colony with neat rows of houses and three existing kirana shops placed around it, each with a colourful awning and a delivery boy on a bicycle with milk packets in a basket. A brand-new fourth shop with a fresh ribbon across its door has just opened in the middle of the colony. From each of the three old shops, one or two thin dashed arrows curve towards the new shop, each arrow ending at a single house that is now its customer, while most houses keep solid lines to their old shop, showing that only a few customers move. In the foreground, the owner of one old shop, a portly man in a white vest and lungi, is crossing out two names in a thick delivery register while handing a short list to the young new shopkeeper in a checked shirt. Meanwhile the early-morning milk deliveries are still happening on every street, cycles in motion, a rooster on a wall, the sky pink with dawn. The overall feeling is of a calm handover where nobody misses their milk. Labels: "REBALANCING" across the top, and "FEW MOVE" beside the dashed arrows.

key: Students sit at desk number = roll
name: ch06_desk_mod_vs_benches
alt: Left: adding one desk per row makes almost every student change seat; right: a new row only takes a few whole benches.
scene: A split-panel classroom illustration divided by a vertical chalk line, the same classroom with green chalkboard and ceiling fans in both halves. LEFT panel: total chaos, almost every student in a white shirt and navy shorts or pinafore is standing up and carrying a school bag to a different desk, bumping into each other, because one extra desk has just been added at the end of each row; a teacher at the board has written a formula with a percent sign and holds her head in dismay. Many curved arrows criss-cross the room. RIGHT panel: calm order, students sit on long wooden benches, each bench carrying a small numbered tag; a new row has been added at the side and two janitors are carrying just two whole benches, with the students still seated on them smiling, into the new row. All other students sit still, reading. The teacher here smiles with arms folded. Morning light through tall windows. Labels: "HASH MOD N" at the top of the left panel, and "FIXED PARTITIONS" at the top of the right panel.

key: A school starts with one section of
name: ch06_class_section_split
alt: One crowded class splits into two sections by surname, one moving upstairs, while a principal pre-splits on day one.
scene: A two-storey school building shown in cross-section like a doll's house. On the ground floor, a single classroom labelled "6" on the door is packed with sixty-plus students, benches crammed, children squeezed three to a seat. A line of students with surname cards beginning with later letters of the alphabet is filing out of this room and up a staircase to an empty classroom on the first floor, where a fresh door sign reads "6-B" and a teacher waits with a register. The ground-floor door now has a new sign "6-A" being hung by a peon on a stool. Next to the staircase a tall cut line on the wall, like a big pair of scissors cutting a strip of paper with letters A to Z, shows the split point between K and L. In a small inset at the top left, on the very first morning of the year, a thoughtful principal in a sari and shawl stands with a seating chart she has divided into four parts in advance, pointing new children to four different rooms. Bright school-day light, lively bustle. Labels: "SPLIT" beside the scissors, and "PRE-SPLIT" in the principal's inset.

key: split a big round pizza by each making
name: ch06_pizza_random_cuts
alt: Four friends cut a pizza at random and get very unequal slices, compared with cutting it into many small pieces dealt out fairly.
scene: A split-panel table-top view of a round wooden dining table, four young friends seated around it in both halves (a girl in a hoodie, a boy in glasses, a girl with braids, a boy in a cricket jersey), plus a fifth friend arriving at the door with a backpack. LEFT panel: a large pizza on a board has been cut by four random knife strokes from the centre, so one friend has a huge half-pizza wedge and looks smug, another has a sliver and looks indignant; the newcomer stands waiting while one friend reluctantly saws his own slice in half. RIGHT panel: the same pizza is cut into a neat grid of many small square pieces, and the friends are dealing them out like playing cards into equal little piles on their plates; the newcomer happily receives a few squares passed from each of the four friends, arrows showing one piece coming from every plate. Warm evening lamp light, a bottle of water and glasses on the table, playful mood. Labels: "RANDOM CUTS" at the top of the left panel, and "MANY SMALL PIECES" at the top of the right panel.

key: close it and send its queue to the other
name: ch06_counter_cascade_closure
alt: An automatic rule shuts one slow reservation counter, its queue floods the others, and they close too until the station master steps in.
scene: A long railway reservation hall seen from the side, five ticket counters in a row with glass windows and brass grilles. At the leftmost counter, one difficult passenger in a bright shirt is arguing and waving several forms while the clerk holds his head. A large automatic signal box on the wall above, like a robotic timer, has flipped a red "closed" shutter down over that window. Thick arrows show its long queue of passengers with suitcases spilling sideways into the next counters, which are now overloaded; further along, the next two shutters are also crashing down one after another like dominoes, each with a small spark, and anxious passengers bunch up in the middle of the hall. On the far right, a calm station master in a white uniform and peaked cap walks in from a side door holding up a hand, looking at the original counter and saying in a speech bubble "just one slow passenger". The hall has ceiling fans, departure boards and a clock reading quarter past six. Tense, comic-chaotic mood. Labels: "CASCADING FAILURE" across the top of the hall, and "HUMAN CHECK" beside the station master.

key: A wedding caterer must make 2,000 plates
name: ch06_caterer_parallel_query
alt: Four cooks each prepare part of a wedding meal at once, dishes are passed between stations, and a head cook plates the final meal.
scene: A large open-air wedding kitchen behind a marriage hall, seen from slightly above, with tarpaulin roofs and huge steel vessels on gas burners. On the left, four cooks in white vests and checked lungis each sit at their own chopping station with a heap of vegetables, all chopping at the same time, each heap a different mix of onions, potatoes, beans and paneer. In the middle, helpers carry steel buckets between stations along curved arrows that cross each other, so that each station on the right ends up with all of one dish: one huge kadai of dal, one of paneer curry, one of rice. At these right-hand stations, cooks stir and finish their single dish. At the far right, a head cook with a grey moustache and a chef's cap stands at a long serving table assembling a perfect steel thali from a ladle of each dish, with a mountain of empty plates waiting behind him and the lit wedding hall visible beyond. Steam, firelight and evening fairy lights, busy but organised mood. Labels: "SCAN" above the chopping stations, "SHUFFLE" over the crossing buckets, and "COMBINE" above the head cook.

key: money must leave your account and arrive
name: ch07_payment_all_or_nothing
alt: A phone payment where the app crashes after the debit, and a big all-or-nothing button rolls the whole transfer back.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a jagged lightning-shaped line, the same young woman (mid 20s, kurti, sling bag) in both halves holding her phone. LEFT panel: on a phone screen blown up as an inset, money coins leave her wallet icon and fly along an arrow towards her friend's wallet icon, but halfway the phone shows a cracked "app stopped" screen; the coins hang frozen in mid-air over a gap, and her friend standing at a tea stall across the road shrugs with an empty palm. The woman looks horrified, one hand on her forehead. RIGHT panel: the same moment with a giant round red button on a pedestal beside her, like a game-show buzzer; when the app dies, a curved rewind arrow pulls the coins neatly back into her own wallet, and both friends look relaxed, ready to try again. The background is a busy Indian street market with a vegetable cart and a scooter. Bright daylight, clear cause-and-effect mood. Labels: "HALF DONE" at the top of the left panel, "ALL OR NOTHING" on the red button, and "ROLLED BACK" at the top of the right panel.

key: booking for a family of four
name: ch07_family_booking_abort
alt: A family of four books train berths; the server crashes after two, and instead of half a booking everything is cancelled and refunded.
scene: A railway booking scene in a family living room, a father in his 40s with spectacles at a laptop on the dining table, his wife and two children (a teenage girl and a small boy hugging a toy train) crowding behind him watching the screen. Above the laptop a large floating thought cloud shows a railway coach with four berths: two berths glow with green ticks and two have red question marks, and the father's face shows panic at this half-booked picture, crossed out with a big red X. Beside it a second cloud shows the clean outcome: all four berths empty and grey, a small coin stack sliding back into the father's wallet with a curved arrow, and a "try again" circular arrow, with the family relaxed. Through the window behind them a distant server building has a small puff of smoke, showing the crash. Warm evening lamp light, an old wall clock and a calendar with a marked holiday date. On the table sit a steel tumbler of tea, a printed itinerary and the mother's reading glasses; the small boy points at the half-booked cloud while the girl reads the screen over her father's shoulder. Labels: "ABORT" on the clean outcome cloud, and "NO HALF BOOKING" under the crossed-out cloud.

key: total udhaar written = sum of all
name: ch07_khata_consistency_rule
alt: A shopkeeper enforces his own totals rule in a credit notebook that will accept any entry, wrong or right.
scene: A close, warm scene inside a small kirana shop at dusk, shelves of biscuit packets, rice sacks and a hanging bunch of bananas behind the counter. The shopkeeper, a man in his 50s with a white vest, reading glasses on his nose and a pencil behind his ear, leans over a fat red cloth-bound credit notebook. The open pages show a column of customer names with amounts and, at the bottom, a boxed total line. A thought bubble over his head shows a balance scale with the individual dues on one pan and the total on the other, perfectly level: this is his rule. In the notebook itself a small pencil is happily writing an obviously wrong number with a smile, showing the notebook does not care. On the counter a little brass bell and a stack of coins. In a tiny inset at the lower right, the notebook's first page has a printed column heading with a little padlock icon next to the phone numbers, suggesting the one simple rule a database could enforce on its own. Soft tube-light glow, homely mood. Labels: "APPLICATION RULE" over the thought bubble, and "DATABASE" on the cover of the notebook.

key: keep the original in a drawer (disk)
name: ch07_id_card_copies_durability
alt: An identity card kept in four places: a drawer, a phone photo, an online locker and a photocopy at the parents' house, each lost to a different accident.
scene: A four-part grid illustration, each square showing one copy of the same plain government identity card (a generic card with a photo silhouette and a few lines, no real logos). Top left: the original card in a wooden drawer in a bedroom, but small flames lick at the edge of the room. Top right: a photo of the card on a smartphone lying on a train seat, the owner walking away without it. Bottom left: the card as an icon in a cloud-shaped online locker on a laptop screen, safe and glowing. Bottom right: a photocopy of the card pinned to a fridge in an old couple's kitchen in another town, the grandmother smiling and waving. Thin golden threads connect all four squares to a calm young man standing in the centre with arms folded and a slight smile, showing that losing one copy still leaves others. A small shield icon hovers over him with a crack in one corner, meaning very safe but never perfect. Evenly lit, clear and orderly mood. Labels: "REPLICAS" across the top of the grid, and "NEVER 100%" on the cracked shield.

key: Replacing a page in a bound register
name: ch07_register_page_swap
alt: A clerk writes a whole new page on a fresh sheet and swaps it into a bound register in one move while a reader waits briefly.
scene: An old government office desk with a heavy bound register lying open, its spine stitched and pages slightly yellowed. On the left, a careful clerk in a half-sleeve white shirt and a pen in his pocket has written the complete new version of one page on a crisp fresh sheet, every line filled, and is lifting it with both hands to slot it into the binding in a single motion, a curved arrow showing the instant swap, while the old page is pulled out at the same moment. On the right, a visitor in a checked shirt holding a token stands at the desk's edge, briefly waiting with a small hourglass floating above his head. A large inset bubble at the top shows what never happens: a page torn horizontally with the top half in old faded ink and the bottom half in fresh blue ink, crossed out with a big red X. Background: steel cupboards, files tied with red tape, a ceiling fan and afternoon light through slatted windows. Calm, precise mood. Labels: "ATOMIC WRITE" above the clerk's hands, and "NEVER HALF" beside the crossed-out torn page.

key: A school register and the class photo
name: ch07_register_photo_list_mismatch
alt: The office updates the attendance register with a new student but not the class photo list, so the teacher calls a name with no photo.
scene: A primary school classroom scene with a split focus. On the left at the school office counter, a busy office clerk in a sari has just written a new student's name into the big attendance register, while the separate class photo list, a board with small passport photos pinned in rows, sits untouched on a shelf behind her with a dusty look. A new girl in a fresh uniform with two ribbons stands shyly near the office door. On the right, in the classroom, the teacher in a cotton sari and spectacles holds the register and calls out a name, while looking at the photo board on the wall where one slot is empty, a white rectangle with a question mark. Rows of children turn around in confusion; one boy shrugs. A dotted line runs from the office register to the classroom register (updated) and a broken dotted line runs to the photo board (not updated). Bright morning light, gentle comic confusion. In the classroom, the photo board has neat rows of smiling passport photos in two-tone uniforms, and the new girl's name tag hangs from the register on a thin string, making the gap on the board obvious even from the back row. Labels: "UPDATED" on the register, and "NOT UPDATED" over the photo board's empty slot.

key: Paying at a shop by UPI and the app
name: ch07_payment_retry_double
alt: A customer's payment app spins and says failed though the money went, and the shopkeeper checks by transaction number before a retry.
scene: A small mobile-phone accessories shop in a bazaar, glass display cabinet with chargers and covers, a QR code stand on the counter (plain, no logos). On the left a young man in a college hoodie stares at his phone, where an enlarged inset shows a spinning loading circle followed by a red cross "failed" screen; his thumb hovers over a "pay again" button with a worried face. Behind the screen, a faint dotted arrow shows the money actually leaving and arriving at the shopkeeper's side, unseen by him. On the right the shopkeeper, a calm middle-aged woman in a cardigan, holds up her own phone showing a received payment and points to a reference number on it, saying in a speech bubble "check if it reached". Between them a ghostly second coin with a red X shows the double payment that would happen if he pressed again. Afternoon market light, mild tension resolved by the shopkeeper's calm. Other shoppers pass in the background carrying cloth bags, and a cycle-rickshaw waits at the kerb; the young man's thumb casts a small shadow over the pay-again button to show the risky moment. Labels: "ACK LOST" over the young man's failed screen, and "DEDUPLICATE" beside the reference number.

key: the teacher is still marking papers
name: ch07_peek_half_marked_sheet
alt: A student peeks at a half-marked answer sheet in the staff room and spreads a wrong score, while others wait for the notice board.
scene: A school corridor and staff room scene. On the left, inside the staff room through a half-open door, a teacher in a grey shawl is marking a two-page answer sheet with a red pen; page one shows a circled "40" and page two is still unmarked under her hand. A mischievous boy in a uniform peeks through the gap in the door at the sheet. In the middle of the corridor, the same boy excitedly tells a cluster of friends, a speech bubble showing "40", and they react with gasps. On the right, a wooden glass-fronted notice board on the wall has a pinned official results list where the same student's row shows "75", and a calm girl stands in front of it reading, finger on the line. A dotted arrow from the teacher's finished sheet leads to the notice board, while the peek path is drawn in a dashed red line with a small warning sign. Mid-morning light, lively school bustle. Stacks of unmarked sheets tied with string sit on the staff room table next to a tumbler of tea, and a peon with a bell walks past in the corridor, unaware of the rumour spreading behind him. The gossiping friends lean in eagerly, one already writing the wrong number in his notebook. Labels: "DIRTY READ" above the peeking boy, and "COMMITTED" on the notice board.

key: the other overwrites it, then they each
name: ch07_shared_form_overwrite
alt: Two salespeople edit the same online sale form at once and produce a mixed-up record, versus a lock banner that makes one wait.
scene: A split-panel illustration inside a car showroom with shiny generic hatchbacks in the background. LEFT panel: two salespeople at two desks back to back, a young man in a tie and a young woman in a blazer, both typing into the same sale form shown as one big floating form between them; the buyer name box contains half of one name scribbled over another, the colour box and the price box each carry different handwriting, and the result looks like a patchwork monster form stitched together, with a comic stitched-creature feel. Both look puzzled. RIGHT panel: the same two desks, but the woman's screen shows a bright yellow banner across the form with a padlock icon, and she leans back sipping tea, waiting, while the man finishes his edit; a small clock icon shows a short wait. Showroom lighting, glossy floor, mild comedy. A customer couple waits on a sofa between the desks holding a car brochure and a set of keys, glancing at each other with raised eyebrows at the confusion. Big glass windows behind show traffic outside, and a potted plant and a coffee machine stand near the reception. Labels: "DIRTY WRITE" at the top of the left panel, and "ROW LOCK" on the yellow banner in the right panel.

key: A restaurant menu board being repainted
name: ch07_menu_board_repaint
alt: A restaurant owner paints a new menu board in the back while customers keep reading the old one, then swaps it at once.
scene: A cutaway of a small South Indian restaurant. In the front dining area, customers at steel tables look up at a chalk-style menu board on the wall showing dish names with old prices, happily ordering; a waiter writes on a pad. Through an open doorway at the back, in a storeroom with rice sacks, the owner, a cheerful moustached man in a striped shirt and apron, kneels and paints a brand-new menu board with fresh prices, a single paintbrush and one small paint tin, a sign on the storeroom door saying one painter at a time with a single-person icon. A large curved arrow above shows the planned instant swap of the new board onto the wall hook. In a small inset at the top right, the rejected alternative: the wall covered with a white sheet and customers standing confused with nothing to read, crossed out. Warm restaurant lighting, steam from idli plates, friendly mood. A family of four in the dining room points at the old board while the waiter nods; in the storeroom the owner hums to himself, the new board propped on two crates, a rag over his shoulder and a small bucket of water for his brush. A cat sleeps on a rice sack beside him. Labels: "OLD VERSION" under the wall board, and "NEW VERSION" under the board being painted.

key: attendance register written in pen
name: ch07_pen_register_versions
alt: An attendance register where entries are struck through and rewritten with teacher numbers instead of erased, and a clerk later recopies it.
scene: A close-up of an open attendance register on a wooden teacher's desk, ruled in blue lines with a red margin, everything written in fountain-pen ink. One student's name is struck through with a single neat line and a tiny note in the margin "struck by #13", and on the next line the corrected name with "written by #13". Above the desk, two teachers appear: on the left, an older teacher in a cardigan who opened the register earlier holds a clear plastic overlay that hides teacher 13's marks, so through it she sees the old line still intact; on the right, teacher 13, a young man with a number badge "13" on his lanyard, holds the pen. In the background corner, a clerk with a fresh register and a ruler sits at a side table recopying only the current lines cleanly, a wastebasket of crossed-out pages beside him. Soft morning light, quiet and methodical mood. The ink colours make each version easy to tell apart: old lines in faded black, new lines in bright blue. A pile of earlier registers with frayed spines sits on a steel almirah, and a bell and a wooden ruler lie next to the open book. A wall chart of the school timetable hangs behind the desk. Labels: "MVCC" above the register, and "VACUUM" over the recopying clerk.

key: each photographs their copy and sends it
name: ch07_shopping_list_last_photo
alt: Mom and Dad each photograph their own copy of a shopping list and send it; the shop keeps only the last photo and one item is lost.
scene: A three-zone horizontal illustration. On the left, in a home kitchen, a mother in a cotton nightie and dupatta writes a new line on her paper shopping list and photographs it with her phone. In the centre, in the living room, a father in a kurta pyjama writes a different new line on his own paper copy of the same list and photographs it too. Two arrows, one from each phone, travel to the right, the father's arrow arriving a fraction later. On the right, at a kirana shop counter, the shopkeeper holds up his phone showing only the father's photo, while the mother's photo fades and drops into a small dustbin under the counter; the shopkeeper packs a bag with milk but no atta. A small floating inset shows two lists side by side, each with a different extra item highlighted, and a red dashed circle around the lost one. Cheerful morning light, domestic comedy. The two parents never see each other's copy: a closed door stands between kitchen and living room, and a small child sits on the floor between them playing with blocks, oblivious. The shop's shelves are full of rice sacks and soap bars. Labels: "LOST UPDATE" over the dustbin, and "LAST WRITE WINS" above the shopkeeper's phone.

key: The bank does the read and the write
name: ch07_bank_add_atomic
alt: A customer at a bank counter says add five hundred instead of calculating a new balance, and the teller does the read and write together.
scene: A split-panel bank counter scene with polished wooden counters and glass partitions. LEFT panel: an elderly man in a white kurta and cap leans on the counter, scribbling a long subtraction and addition on a scrap paper with a stub pencil, saying in a speech bubble "set it to this number"; meanwhile behind him, a second customer at the next window is also changing the same passbook, shown by a faint ghost of the same account card in both windows, and a lightning bolt between them. RIGHT panel: the same man simply hands over a deposit slip with a big plus sign and a stack of notes, saying "add this"; the teller, a young woman with a bun and an ID lanyard, reaches into a single closed cabinet behind her counter where the reading of the balance and the writing of the new one happen inside one box, shown by a closed lid with two small arrows looping inside. Calm daylight, ceiling fans, a token display. Labels: "READ-MODIFY-WRITE" at the top of the left panel, and "ATOMIC INCREMENT" on the cabinet in the right panel.

key: A carrom board where a player puts
name: ch07_carrom_hand_on_striker
alt: A carrom player keeps a hand on the striker while thinking, so nobody else can take it until the hand is lifted.
scene: A top-down, slightly tilted view of a wooden carrom board on a low stool on a veranda, coins arranged near the centre, powder sprinkled on the surface. Four players sit around: a teenage boy in a vest, his grandfather in a dhoti, a girl in a frock and an uncle in a checked shirt. The teenage boy has placed his flat palm firmly over the striker, fingers spread, while he looks thoughtfully at the board and a small floating rulebook icon above him shows he is checking a rule. The girl's hand reaches towards the striker but stops in mid-air, politely blocked by a faint glowing outline around the boy's hand. A small speech bubble from the boy says "my turn". In the corner, a tiny inset shows the same hand lifting and the girl's hand then taking the striker, with a numbered sequence 1 and 2. Late afternoon sun, a hanging bird cage, relaxed family mood. A plate of murukku and four glasses of lime juice sit on a side stool, and the uncle leans back with his arms crossed, patiently waiting. The grandfather watches over his spectacles with an amused smile, as if he has seen this rule enforced many times. Coins glint in the low sunlight. Labels: "SELECT FOR UPDATE" in a banner above the board, and "LOCK" beside the boy's hand.

key: A bank cheque clearing desk that notices
name: ch07_cheque_bounced_recheck
alt: A cheque clearing clerk spots that the balance changed after the cheque was written and returns it for re-issue.
scene: A bank back-office desk with sorting trays, a rubber stamp rack and a computer screen. A bespectacled clearing clerk in a blue shirt holds a cheque up to the light, and beside him the account ledger on screen shows a balance figure that has been crossed and changed, a small clock icon marking that the change happened after the cheque's date. He presses a red "returned" stamp onto the cheque. On the right, a young woman customer with a handbag receives the cheque back at the window with a shrug and immediately starts writing a fresh one at the side counter, a circular arrow drawn around her indicating a retry. In the background, other customers walk freely past the window without any queue, showing that no one was made to wait up front. A small inset at the top left shows the alternative: a long queue roped off at the door, crossed out. Cool office lighting, efficient mood. The clerk's desk holds a tray of sorted cheques, a bottle of glue, a box of rubber bands and a small table fan, and a wall poster about cheque rules hangs behind him. Through the glass, the bank's main hall is bright and mostly empty. Labels: "CONFLICT DETECTED" above the clerk, and "RETRY" near the customer rewriting the cheque.

key: move me from F7 to F8 only if F8
name: ch07_cinema_seat_swap_cas
alt: A moviegoer asks to move to seat F8 only if it is still empty, but someone just took it, so nothing happens and he picks again.
scene: A cinema hall interior before the show, red velvet seats in rows, the screen glowing blank. In row F, a young man in a denim jacket stands at seat F7 holding a popcorn tub, looking at his phone, where an enlarged inset shows a seat map with F8 and a condition arrow: move only if empty. But in F8 a woman with a shawl has just sat down a second ago, her bag still mid-air as she settles. On his phone, the seat map flashes a gentle red with a small "pick again" icon and the man's seat F7 is unchanged, a small padlock on it. In a second smaller inset at the top right, a stale seat map image shows F8 still green, with a faded timestamp, to show the danger of checking an old picture. Row letter "F" painted on the end of the aisle. Dim cinema lighting with the warm glow of the phone. Around them, other moviegoers settle into their seats with snacks and soft drinks, an usher in a waistcoat holds a torch near the aisle, and the green exit sign glows at the side wall. The young man's expression is mildly disappointed but calm, already scrolling for another seat; the woman in F8 has no idea she just won the race. Labels: "COMPARE-AND-SET" above the phone inset, and "STALE MAP" beside the faded small inset.

key: Two branches of a shop each count
name: ch07_footfall_clickers_merge
alt: Two shop branches each tally visitors on a clicker and add the totals at night, versus phoning head office where the last call wins.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: two small clothing shop entrances side by side at night, each with a security guard holding a hand clicker counter showing a number; dotted arrows from both clickers lead into a calculator held by a smiling accountant at a head-office desk, who adds them with a plus sign and writes the correct total on a sheet. RIGHT panel: the same two guards are each on a mobile phone calling head office; at the head office desk, the accountant holds one ringing landline to her ear while a second call fades out, and she writes only the number from the last call, crossing out the other; a small ghost figure of a shopper with a question mark floats away from the sheet as the lost visitor. Evening market lights, neon reflections, slightly comic mood in the right panel. Shop windows show mannequins in kurtas and saris, a few late shoppers carry bags, and the head office in both panels is a small room with a wall calendar, a steel cupboard and a ledger. In the left panel the accountant smiles at a correct total; in the right she frowns at a smaller number. Labels: "COMMUTATIVE MERGE" at the top of the left panel, and "LAST WRITE WINS" at the top of the right panel.

key: Booking the society clubhouse through
name: ch07_clubhouse_double_booking
alt: Two residents in different flats both see Saturday free in the group chat and both post that they booked it.
scene: A housing society scene in cross-section: two apartments on different floors, each with a resident on a sofa holding a phone. On the upper floor, a woman in her 30s in a kurta with a laptop beside her; on the lower floor, a retired man in a vest with reading glasses. Each phone is shown as an enlarged inset: both show the same group chat scrolled up to an older message saying the clubhouse is free on Saturday, and both are typing a new message at the same moment, two little pencil icons. Between the two flats a wall separates them so neither sees the other's screen. At the bottom of the picture, the clubhouse hall has a calendar on its door where Saturday has two overlapping name stickers, one on top of the other, with party balloons and a cricket bat both leaning against the door, showing two events clashing. Evening light, comic clash mood. The upper flat has potted plants on the balcony and a child doing homework beside the woman; the lower flat has a cricket match on the television and a cup of tea on a side table. The two phones glow in the dim rooms, and a society notice board in the lobby between them shows the clubhouse rules. Labels: "CHECK THEN ACT" over the two phones, and "WRITE SKEW" on the clubhouse calendar.

key: someone else also saw the empty corner
name: ch07_phantom_empty_corner
alt: Two people see an empty corner and each go to fetch a chair; there was no chair to put a reserved cloth on.
scene: A wedding reception hall with rows of chairs, white cloths and marigold garlands. In the foreground, an existing chair has a red cloth draped over it with a small reserved card, a contented aunt nearby. In the right-hand corner of the hall there is a bare patch of floor with no chair. From the left, a young man in a kurta carries a folding plastic chair towards the corner; from a door on the right, a young woman in a lehenga carries another chair towards the same empty spot. Each has a thought bubble showing the empty corner. Floating above the empty floor is a red reserved cloth hanging in mid-air with no chair under it, drooping comically, with a question mark, to show you cannot reserve empty air. A small dotted circle on the floor marks where the clash will happen. Bright festive lighting, fairy lights, light comedy mood. Guests mingle in the background around a buffet, children chase each other between the chairs, and a photographer with a big camera kneels near the stage. The two chair carriers are both smiling and confident, neither noticing the other, their paths drawn as dotted arrows meeting at the bare spot. Labels: "PHANTOM" over the empty corner, and "NOTHING TO LOCK" beside the floating cloth.

key: A badminton court sign-up sheet printed
name: ch07_badminton_slot_sheet
alt: A clipboard sign-up sheet with every half-hour slot pre-printed, so players write names in boxes that two people cannot share.
scene: An indoor badminton court with green flooring and a net, shuttlecocks scattered. On a pillar beside the court hangs a large clipboard with a printed grid: rows of half-hour time slots down the side and days across the top, every box pre-printed and mostly empty. A woman in a sports tracksuit writes her name into one box with a marker. A young man in shorts reaches for the same box with his pen, but a small glowing outline around her box blocks him and he moves to the next one. Beside the pillar, a stack of many more printed sheets, months' worth, sits on a bench, mostly blank, showing the cost of printing boxes in advance. Above the grid, a small inset shows a blank page with no boxes and a hand trying to write on empty space, crossed out. Bright sports-hall lighting, energetic mood. A shuttle is frozen mid-flight over the net between two players in the background, and a water bottle, a racquet bag and a towel lie on the bench. The woman writing her name is smiling, and the young man shrugs good-naturedly as he picks the next box. A ceiling of bright floodlights casts crisp shadows. Labels: "MATERIALIZE CONFLICTS" across the top of the clipboard, and "EMPTY ROWS" on the stack of blank sheets.

key: Three ways to run a single ATM safely
name: ch07_three_ways_atm
alt: Three panels of the same ATM: one person at a time, waiting only on shared accounts, and cancelling clashes at the end.
scene: A three-panel illustration of the same roadside ATM kiosk with a glass door and a guard's stool, separated by thin vertical lines. PANEL ONE: a single straight queue outside, one customer inside at a time, a stopwatch above showing each person is quick; the guard waves the next in. PANEL TWO: several customers inside at once at multiple screens, but two of them reaching for the same account card icon, and one stands back with a small padlock and hourglass over her head while the other finishes. PANEL THREE: everyone inside working at once freely, and at the exit a bank officer with a clipboard checks receipts, tearing up one receipt where two withdrawals clashed and handing it back with a circular retry arrow. Night-time street with a sodium street lamp and a stray dog asleep nearby, clear and comparative mood. Each panel shows the same kiosk from the same angle so the differences stand out: the number of people inside, the padlock in panel two, and the torn receipt in panel three. A small stopwatch in the corner of each panel hints at how fast people get through. Labels: "SERIAL" at the top of panel one, "LOCKING" at the top of panel two, and "OPTIMISTIC" at the top of panel three.

key: A busy dosa tawa with one expert cook
name: ch07_dosa_single_cook
alt: One expert dosa cook serves orders one after another very fast with everything within reach, until one order needs a storeroom trip.
scene: A bustling street-side dosa stall at night, one large black iron tawa sizzling, steam rising. A single expert cook, a wiry man in a white vest and a towel over his shoulder, spreads batter in a perfect spiral with a ladle. Within arm's reach around him are steel bowls of batter, chutney, sambar, potato masala and ghee, all neatly arranged in a semicircle. A tidy line of order slips hangs on a string in front of him and finished dosas slide one after another onto plates in a continuous stream, shown with motion lines. Customers at the counter smile. On the far right, one customer holds a slip for an unusual dish, and a dotted arrow leads to a dark storeroom door at the back with a ladder and dusty sacks, the cook's glance towards it worried; behind this customer a small queue begins to bunch up with impatient faces. Warm orange streetlight and tawa glow, energetic mood. A hand-painted price board hangs from the stall's canopy, a bright bulb dangles on a wire above the tawa, and steel tumblers of filter coffee wait on the counter. The customers at the front look delighted, while those at the back of the bunching line start checking their phones. Labels: "SINGLE THREAD" above the cook, and "ALL IN MEMORY" over the semicircle of bowls.

key: calling the waiter for each dish
name: ch07_order_all_at_once
alt: A diner calls the waiter back for every dish, versus handing a complete written order to the single cook at once.
scene: A split-panel restaurant illustration. LEFT panel: a family at a table in a busy dining room, the father calling a waiter for one dosa; the waiter's path is drawn as a long zigzag dotted line running back and forth between the table and the kitchen hatch many times, the waiter sweating with a towel on his shoulder; in the kitchen hatch, the only cook stands idle with folded arms waiting for the next instruction. RIGHT panel: the same father hands the waiter one long written order slip with several lines and a small conditional note, the waiter carries it once to the kitchen in a single straight arrow, and the cook works smoothly through the whole list with plates lined up. Warm restaurant lighting, ceiling fan, a wall menu without brand names. In the left panel the waiter's footprints are drawn on the floor to show how many trips he made, and the family's plates are empty while they wait. In the right panel the family is already eating, a little boy reaching for a crispy dosa, and the cook wipes his hands contentedly. The order slip shows a small if-arrow icon beside one line. Labels: "INTERACTIVE" at the top of the left panel, and "STORED PROCEDURE" at the top of the right panel.

key: Two branches of a sweet shop that both
name: ch07_recipe_card_replication
alt: Two sweet shop branches follow the same exact recipe card instead of shipping finished laddoos, with the date taken from head office.
scene: A wide illustration of two identical sweet shop kitchens on either side of a road, connected by a postman on a bicycle carrying a laminated recipe card in a pouch, not boxes of sweets. In each kitchen a cook in a white cap stirs a large karahi and rolls laddoos, the trays on both sides looking exactly alike. The recipe card, shown enlarged in the centre, lists precise quantities with a little weighing scale icon and a date written by the head office stamp. On the left kitchen wall, a clock shows one time and on the right wall a different time, both crossed out lightly, with an arrow pointing to the stamped date on the card instead. In a small inset at the bottom, a recipe line reading "to taste" with a pinch of sugar falling is crossed out in red, showing what is not allowed. Bright morning light, aroma swirls, tidy and precise mood. Shop customers in both branches queue at glass counters filled with sweets, and both shopkeepers wear the same striped aprons. The postman on the bicycle pedals cheerfully, his pouch only holding the thin card, while a heavy crate of laddoos sits unused at the roadside, crossed out to show it is not shipped. Labels: "SAME RECIPE" on the card, and "DETERMINISTIC" under the two matching trays.

key: A big railway station with one ticket
name: ch07_zone_windows_cross_partition
alt: Eight zone ticket windows serve single-zone travellers quickly, but a three-zone ticket needs three clerks to stop and stamp it together.
scene: A long station concourse with a row of eight ticket windows, each with a small zone board above it, and short brisk queues moving quickly, passengers walking away with tickets. In the middle of the row, one elderly traveller with a big tin trunk and a long multi-part ticket stands frozen, and three clerks from three neighbouring windows have leaned out together to stamp his ticket in unison, three stamps descending at once; their own queues behind them have stalled, with passengers checking watches and tapping feet. Dotted lines tie the three clerks together like a chain. On the far right, a ninth window has just been opened with a ribbon, but the traveller still has to wait for the same three clerks, shown by a small shrug icon over the new window. Bright station lighting, departure board above, busy crowd. Coolies in red shirts carry luggage on their heads across the concourse, and a station announcer's horn speaker hangs from a pillar. The elderly traveller looks apologetic, holding his spectacles and the long ticket, while the three clerks concentrate on synchronising their stamps. Labels: "SINGLE PARTITION" above the fast windows, and "CROSS-PARTITION" over the three stamping clerks.

key: One customer with a full trolley
name: ch07_express_counter_trolley
alt: An express supermarket counter blocked by one full trolley and one forgotten item, and the cashier sending that customer aside to fetch it.
scene: A supermarket with bright aisles and a single express checkout counter at the front. A queue of customers each with a small basket of two or three items waits; at the counter, a man with an overflowing trolley is unloading item after item, while behind him a woman realises she forgot something and points back down an aisle. The cashier, a young woman with a ponytail and a name badge, makes a kindly sweeping gesture to the side, guiding the forgetful customer to step out of the line to a small waiting spot marked with footprints, while the next customer moves forward. A dotted arrow loops from the waiting spot into a far aisle labelled with a storage shelf icon and back to the front of the queue. Fluorescent store lighting, shelves of colourful packets without brands, mildly busy mood. Customers in the queue hold small baskets with a loaf of bread, a packet of tea or a bar of soap, and a little girl on her father's shoulders points at a sweets rack. The trolley man looks oblivious, piling up rice bags, cooking oil and detergent. The forgetful woman is shown again faintly in the far aisle, reaching for a packet, and once more at the front of the line with it in her hand. Labels: "EXPRESS ONLY" on the sign above the counter, and "ANTI-CACHING" beside the step-aside spot.

key: A library reference book: many people
name: ch07_reference_book_shared_lock
alt: Many students read one reference book together, but an editor wanting to rewrite a chapter makes everyone hand it back first.
scene: A library reading room with a long wooden table and green-shaded lamps. LEFT half: one thick reference book lies open in the middle of the table and five students lean over it reading together, each with a small green key token beside their notebook. RIGHT half: an editor in a waistcoat with a red pen and a stack of new pages stands at the table's end holding a single large red key, and the students are handing the book back one by one; the last student still reading has a small hourglass over the editor's head. Then, while the editor rewrites the chapter, the book sits under a glass dome with a padlock and the students wait in chairs, idle, one yawning. Warm lamplight, wooden shelves, studious mood. The students are a mix of ages: a girl with a braid taking notes, a boy in glasses copying a diagram, an older man with a newspaper tucked under his arm, and two friends sharing one notebook. The editor looks polite but firm. Tall shelves rise behind them with ladders, and a librarian at a desk in the distance stamps cards. Clock on the wall shows time passing in the right half. Labels: "SHARED LOCK" over the reading students, and "EXCLUSIVE LOCK" beside the editor's red key.

key: A single toll booth where one truck
name: ch07_toll_booth_lock_queue
alt: One truck driver argues at a single toll booth while a long line of cars waits behind him, the twentieth car waiting longest.
scene: A highway toll booth with one open lane and a striped barrier, seen from a slightly raised angle behind the queue. At the booth, a truck driver in a vest leans out of his colourful decorated truck arguing with the toll operator, both gesturing, a small pile of coins and a receipt between them. Behind the truck stretches a long line of cars, autos and a scooter, numbered by tiny floating tags from 1 up to 20, with the last car's driver resting his head on the steering wheel and a large clock face above him showing a long wait. Above the queue, a simple bar of small coloured blocks shows that most cars waited a little but the last ones waited a lot. The neighbouring lanes are closed with cones, so nobody can switch. Hot afternoon sun, heat haze, mild frustration. The truck is painted with bright patterns and tassels, the toll operator wears a reflective vest and a cap, and roadside hawkers sell water bottles and cucumbers to the waiting drivers. A family in car number 7 plays a card game on the dashboard, and an auto driver in the middle naps with his feet up. Dust rises behind the queue on the shoulder of the road. Labels: "LOCK HOLDER" above the arguing truck, and "TAIL LATENCY" over the twentieth car.

key: Telling the wedding hall manager
name: ch07_hall_manager_predicate_hold
alt: A wedding hall manager holds any booking request matching one hall, date and evening, even requests that have not been made yet.
scene: A wedding hall booking office with an old wooden desk, a big register and framed photos of decorated halls on the wall. The manager, a portly man with a moustache and a gold watch, listens to a young couple seated across the desk. Above them a glowing condition bubble shows three tiles combined: a hall icon with the number 1, a calendar page with 12 December and a moon for evening. In the doorway behind, two more customers arrive with their own request slips; one slip matches the three tiles and is held up by a raised palm from the manager, while the other slip for a different hall is waved through. A ghostly third customer outline in the corridor, still deciding to come, also has a faint raised palm over him, showing even future requests are held. Warm office light, ceiling fan, calm authority. The couple across the desk holds a wedding card sample and a folder of photos, the bride-to-be pointing at a picture of the lit hall. A peon waits at the door with a tray of tea. The register on the desk is open to a page with a few existing bookings, none of them for the matched evening yet. Labels: "PREDICATE LOCK" over the condition bubble, and "HELD" near the blocked slip.

key: the manager simply puts a sticky note
name: ch07_register_page_sticky_note
alt: The hall manager puts a sticky note on a whole register page, quick to check but also blocking some unrelated customers.
scene: A close view of the same kind of wedding hall booking office: a thick bound register lies open on the desk, and the manager with a moustache slaps a bright yellow sticky note over the whole page headed with a hall number, while another tab sticks out from the page for a December date. On the left, a customer whose request clashes is stopped, and on the right a different customer who only wanted a morning slot is also waiting on a bench looking at his watch, a small annoyed cloud over him, showing over-blocking. In a corner inset, the whole register is wrapped in a ribbon with a big padlock, for the case where there are no pages to stick notes on. Afternoon light, tidy office, quick and practical mood. The manager wears a cream safari suit and holds a pen between his teeth while flattening the sticky note with his palm. A wall calendar behind him shows December with several dates circled. The waiting man on the bench holds a box of sweets and a booking form for a different event, glancing at the clock. A tea glass steams on the desk, and a small brass idol sits on a shelf. The clashing customer at the left looks resigned but understanding. Labels: "INDEX-RANGE LOCK" on the sticky note, and "OVER-BLOCKING" over the waiting customer.

key: An exam hall where students sit wherever
name: ch07_exam_check_copying_end
alt: Students sit anywhere and write freely, and at the end the invigilator cancels only the sheets that were copied.
scene: A large exam hall with rows of desks, students in uniforms writing busily, no queue at the open door, a few students still wandering in to pick any free seat. At the front, a wall clock shows the end of the exam. On the right, an invigilator in a sari with spectacles on a chain sits at a long table, comparing answer sheets side by side with a magnifying glass. Two sheets that are suspiciously identical have red cancel stamps on them, and the two students who wrote them stand nearby looking sheepish, holding blank fresh sheets for a retake. All other sheets are stacked neatly with green ticks. A small inset at the top left shows the same hall packed shoulder to shoulder, with many cancel stamps flying, showing high contention. Bright daylight, calm overall mood. Ceiling fans turn slowly, a blackboard at the front shows the start and end time drawn as two clock faces, and a peon collects sheets from the last row. Most students look relieved and stretch their arms after the exam, a few chatting quietly by the door. A tall stack of completed, ticked papers sits at the invigilator's elbow. Labels: "OPTIMISTIC" above the open door, and "ABORTED" over the red-stamped sheets.

key: calling a friend before visiting
name: ch07_call_first_vs_just_go
alt: One person phones a friend before every visit while another just goes and sometimes finds the door locked.
scene: A split-panel illustration showing two neighbourhood streets with similar houses. LEFT panel: a young woman in a kurti stands at her own gate holding a phone to her ear with a patient face, a speech bubble asking if the friend is home, and a small clock showing time passing before she even sets off; a dotted path to the friend's house is not yet walked. RIGHT panel: a young man in a T-shirt and sneakers has already walked to the friend's door; in most frames of a small strip above him the door is open and he is welcomed with chai, but in one frame the door has a padlock and he turns back with a shrug and a circular arrow. A small dial gauge in each panel shows contention: low on the right panel's main scene, with a note of what happens when it is high. Sunny afternoon, cheerful mood. Both streets have colourful houses with potted tulsi plants, scooters parked by the gates and a vegetable vendor pushing his cart. The friend's house is the same in both panels, a blue door with a brass knocker. The woman in the left panel looks a bit bored, tapping her foot, while the man on the right whistles as he walks. Labels: "PESSIMISTIC" at the top of the left panel, and "OPTIMISTIC" at the top of the right panel.

key: and place an order based on that
name: ch07_food_app_stale_premise
alt: A customer orders food because the app showed the restaurant open, but it closed a minute ago so the order is cancelled.
scene: A split-scene illustration. On the left, a young man in a hoodie lies on his bed at night scrolling a food delivery app (generic, no logos) on his phone; an enlarged inset shows a restaurant card with a green open badge and he taps order with a hungry smile. On the right, across the street, the restaurant's shutter is being pulled down by a staff member in an apron, the lights going off, a wall clock showing one minute past closing time. Between the two, a dotted arrow carries the order from his phone towards the shutter, and a referee-like figure, a small robot with a whistle standing on the arrow, raises a red card and points back, as the phone inset changes to a cancelled notice. Night city lighting, neon reflections, gentle comedy. His room has a study table piled with books, a desk lamp, and a poster of a mountain on the wall. The restaurant on the right has a hand-painted signboard without any brand, plastic chairs stacked inside, and the staff member yawning as he pulls the shutter. A stray cat sits on the step outside. The young man's face changes from eager to disappointed across a small two-frame strip at the corner of his phone inset. Labels: "PREMISE CHANGED" above the closing shutter, and "SSI ABORT" beside the robot referee.

key: You check the hostel room chart at 9:00
name: ch07_hostel_chart_pencil_note
alt: A student reads a hostel room chart at nine, ignoring a pencil note, and at nine-five the warden says the note became ink.
scene: A college hostel corridor with a notice board showing a room allotment chart. A two-part scene left to right. LEFT: a student with a duffel bag reads the chart at a wall clock showing 9:00; on Room 4's row a faint pencil note sits next to the word free, and the student's eyes skip it, shown by a dotted gaze line passing over it. RIGHT: the same student stands at the warden's office door at a clock showing 9:05 holding a move-in form; the warden, a stern but kind older man in a sweater and muffler, holds up the chart where the pencil note has become bold ink, a small clock icon beside it reading 9:02, and he points back to the board. In a tiny inset, another student just glancing at the chart without a form passes by without being stopped. Morning light through corridor windows, mild suspense. The corridor has rows of numbered doors, a water cooler, and a cricket bat leaning against a wall, with another student in a towel heading to the bathroom in the background. The warden's office has a desk with a key rack, a register and a framed rules list. The student holding the form scratches his head, slightly embarrassed but nodding. Labels: "STALE READ" over the left scene, and "CHECK AT COMMIT" above the warden.

key: A shared office fridge with a sign-in
name: ch07_office_fridge_sticky_note
alt: Priya takes the last milk from the office fridge and leaves a note on Arjun's desk, so Arjun must re-plan before he finalises.
scene: An office pantry with a tall fridge, a coffee machine and a sign-in sheet clipped to the fridge door listing who looked at the milk and when. On the left, a young woman in a blazer pours the last of the milk from a carton into her mug, the fridge open and the shelf empty. In the centre, she places a bright pink sticky note on a colleague's desk in an open-plan office, the note showing a little empty milk carton drawing, without stopping to wait. On the right, the colleague, a young man in a sweater holding a plan for a tea party on a clipboard, sees the note and sighs, crossing out the plan with a red pen and starting again. A dotted line connects the sign-in sheet entry to his desk, showing how she knew whom to notify. Bright office daylight, light comedy. The pantry has a microwave, a kettle, a jar of biscuits and a notice reminding people to wash their mugs. The young woman walks on quickly to her own desk carrying her mug, not waiting for any reply, while the colleague behind her reads the note with a slow sigh. Other colleagues in the open office type at laptops, unaware. Labels: "READ TRACKING" on the sign-in sheet, and "RE-PLAN" beside the crossed-out clipboard.

key: Planning a family wedding across three
name: ch08_wedding_calls_three_cities
alt: A woman planning a wedding by phone from home can see everyone at home but cannot tell why a cousin in another city does not answer.
scene: A wide illustration split into a central house and three distant city vignettes connected by long wavy phone lines. In the centre, inside a warm living room cluttered with wedding cards, sweet boxes and a half-sewn garland, a woman in her 40s in a cotton sari sits on a sofa with a phone to her ear and a notebook of to-do lists on her lap; everyone in her house is visible and accounted for: a husband counting envelopes, a grandmother threading marigolds, a teenage son on a laptop. The three phone lines lead out to three small round vignettes: top left, a cousin asleep in a dark bedroom with his phone face-down; top right, a cousin on a hill road with a phone showing no signal bars; bottom right, a cousin on a moving train with luggage, phone in his bag. Each line ends near the woman in an identical silent dotted segment with a question mark, because from her side all three look the same. Warm evening light inside, cooler tones in the vignettes. Labels: "ONE COMPUTER" over the bright living room, and "UNKNOWN" beside the three silent question marks.

key: Your home inverter vs your city
name: ch08_inverter_vs_grid
alt: At home an inverter failure darkens everything at once; in the city grid one street is dark while the next is lit and the office cannot tell why.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a vertical line. LEFT panel: a single flat at night with a home inverter and battery under the staircase; the inverter shows a red fault light and the entire flat is uniformly dark, the family sitting together with a candle, clear and simple, a single big switch icon in the off position. RIGHT panel: an aerial night view of a city neighbourhood where one street is pitch dark while the very next street glows with lit windows and street lamps; a feeder line on a pole has a small spark. Far away, in an electricity board office, a tired engineer sits at a desk with a big wall panel of meters, one meter showing a blank reading, and a thought bubble above him splits into two pictures: a burnt transformer and a cut wire to his meter, with a question mark between them. A lineman with a ladder is still far off, walking. Night colours with sodium lamps, puzzled mood on the right. Labels: "TOTAL FAILURE" at the top of the left panel, and "PARTIAL FAILURE" at the top of the right panel.

key: A supercomputer is like a board exam
name: ch08_exam_hall_vs_railway_system
alt: A board exam hall stops entirely during a power cut, while a nationwide railway booking network keeps selling tickets though one counter is jammed.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a large board exam hall plunged into darkness by a power cut, hundreds of desks with answer sheets, an invigilator on a stool holding up a hand to stop everyone, and a big wall poster showing a rewind arrow back to the last collected answer sheets in a sealed bundle; students sit with pens down, waiting. RIGHT panel: a map-like collage of several railway reservation counters scattered across a stylised map of India, each counter with a clerk and a short queue; at one counter a dot-matrix printer has jammed and the clerk is pulling out crumpled paper with a sigh, but all other counters keep printing tickets, passengers leaving happily with tickets in hand. Thin glowing lines connect all counters into one network that stays lit. Contrasting lighting: gloomy hall on the left, bright daylight counters on the right. In the left panel a single emergency lamp throws a pale beam over the rows, and a peon carries the sealed bundle to a steel cupboard. In the right panel a few passengers at the jammed counter simply walk to the next window, smiling. Labels: "STOP AND RESTART" at the top of the left panel, and "KEEP RUNNING" at the top of the right panel.

key: Registered post (TCP) keeps asking
name: ch08_registered_post_tcp
alt: Ordinary letters get lost or delayed, while registered post keeps re-sending until acknowledged, though it still cannot beat a stuck van.
scene: A post office scene split into top and bottom bands. TOP band: a postman in khaki on a bicycle with a sack of ordinary letters rides along a bumpy road; a few letters flutter out of the sack and blow into a ditch, and one letter is caught in a tree. BOTTOM band: the same route with registered letters in numbered envelopes 1, 2, 3, each tied to a pink acknowledgement card; at the receiving house an old man signs card 1 and 2, and a returning arrow carries the signed cards back to the post office counter, where a clerk ticks them off; for envelope 3 no card returns, so the clerk sends a fresh copy, shown by a circular arrow and a duplicate envelope. On the far right of the bottom band, a red mail van is stuck in a monsoon traffic jam with water up to its wheels, and the clerk looks at a wall clock, unable to speed it up. Overcast monsoon light with puddles. The post office counter has a brass weighing scale, a pot of glue, a rack of pink cards and a clerk in a half-sleeve shirt with spectacles; the receiving house has a tulsi plant and a blue door. Small numbers on each envelope keep the order clear. Labels: "IP" on the top band, "TCP" on the bottom band, and "STILL DELAYED" over the stuck van.

key: Some months the wire to one flat breaks
name: ch08_society_intercom_faults
alt: A housing society intercom with one broken wire, a whole wing silent, two wrongly wired lines, and a flat that can call out but not hear.
scene: A cutaway illustration of an apartment building with two wings and a gatehouse, intercom handsets drawn on the wall inside each flat and thin wires running down to a panel in the gatehouse where a guard in a beret sits. In wing A, one flat's wire is visibly snapped with frayed ends and a small spark. All the flats in wing B are greyed out and silent, little mute icons over each handset. At the gate panel, an electrician on a stool holds two cables crossed into the wrong sockets with a confident grin, while a second backup line next to it is also crossed the same wrong way. In a top-right flat, a woman in a nightie presses her handset and speaks, her voice drawn as a line reaching the guard, but the guard's reply line stops halfway and droops, so she hears nothing and frowns at the receiver. Evening light, a few lit windows, stray cat on the boundary wall. The guard at the gate holds a handset to each ear in confusion, a register and a torch on his desk. A small sign near the electrician shows two lines for backup, which are no help when both are wired the same wrong way. Labels: "NETWORK FAULTS" across the top of the building, and "ONE-WAY" beside the drooping reply line.

key: Sending a courier to an office
name: ch08_courier_delivered_vs_signed
alt: A courier's delivered message only means the parcel reached reception; whether the manager signed it is known only when he replies.
scene: A three-stage left-to-right illustration. LEFT: a young woman in a work blouse at her home desk receives an SMS on her phone with a tick and the word delivered, looking relieved. CENTRE: an office reception with a glass door and a potted plant, where the courier boy in a cap hands a brown envelope to a receptionist who stamps a receipt; the envelope is then placed on a growing pile on the reception counter. RIGHT: a closed manager's cabin behind frosted glass, the manager's chair empty and a jacket on it, the envelope not yet inside; a dotted line from the cabin back to the woman's phone is still empty with no reply. A small side inset shows the rarer case, the receptionist pointing at a shutter with a closed sign, and a quick reply arrow going back. Bright daytime office lighting, calm but uncertain mood. The courier boy rides away on a motorbike with a bag of other parcels, already on to the next delivery. The woman at home taps her pen on the desk, glancing between her phone and a wall clock, and a cup of tea cools beside her laptop, its steam fading as time passes. Labels: "TCP ACK" over the delivered SMS, "PROCESSED?" above the empty cabin, and "RST" in the small inset.

key: Waiting for a friend at the metro
name: ch08_metro_friend_timeout
alt: A man waiting for a friend at a metro station either leaves too early, stranding the friend, or waits for hours for someone who cancelled.
scene: A split-panel illustration at the same elevated metro station with a platform, digital board and turnstiles. LEFT panel: a young man in a T-shirt glances at his watch showing two minutes and walks away down the stairs; just behind him a train pulls in and his friend, a young woman with a tote bag, steps out looking around, alone, with a sigh and a heavy bag of shopping that she now carries by herself. RIGHT panel: the same young man sits on a platform bench as the sky outside goes from sunset to dark night, the wall clock behind him showing two hours later, empty chai cups beside him, yawning; in a thought bubble, the friend is at home in pyjamas watching TV, having cancelled. A small inset at the top centre shows a train timetable board with a guaranteed maximum delay stamp, which does not exist here, crossed out lightly. Evening city lights, gentle comedy. In both panels the metro board above the platform shows train times, and other commuters in office wear and school uniforms flow past. The friend's face in the left panel is mildly hurt, and the young man's face in the right panel is bored and sleepy. Labels: "SHORT TIMEOUT" at the top of the left panel, and "LONG TIMEOUT" at the top of the right panel.

key: three highways merge into one plaza
name: ch08_toll_plaza_congestion
alt: Three highways merge into one toll plaza at rush hour and cars are turned away, while a radio commentator never repeats words lost to static.
scene: An aerial evening illustration. In the main area, three highways from the left, top and bottom curve and merge into one toll plaza on the right side, each road busy with cars, buses and trucks with headlights on. At the plaza a long queue backs up past the merge point, and a traffic police officer in a white shirt and cap with a whistle waves some cars off onto a side road, those cars marked with small red crosses, though every road surface is fine and green. In a round inset at the top right corner, an old transistor radio on a windowsill crackles with static lines, a cricket commentary bubble coming out with a couple of words broken into fragments and falling away, while the commentator in a tiny picture inside the bubble is already describing the next ball. Golden-hour sky with orange glow, busy energy. A row of booths with striped barriers and overhead lights stands across the plaza, and an electronic sign shows a jam. A few drivers lean out of their windows to look ahead; a family in an auto shares snacks while waiting. Dust and exhaust haze hang in the warm air. Labels: "QUEUEING" over the backed-up plaza, "DROPPED" beside the turned-away cars, and "UDP" on the radio inset.

key: A reserved seat on a Rajdhani Express
name: ch08_reserved_vs_general_coach
alt: A reserved berth on a premium train stays empty for its owner, while the packed general coach takes whoever fits.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same long-distance train at a station platform. LEFT panel: inside a clean air-conditioned coach with curtains, an empty reserved berth has a printed name card and a folded blanket, a passenger in a business shirt arriving calmly with a wheeled suitcase and checking a ticket; a big clock icon above shows exact departure and arrival times. A second reserved berth in the same bay stays empty because its owner never came, a little cobweb drawn on it for humour. RIGHT panel: a general compartment at the rear of the train packed with people, some standing, some on luggage racks, a family with bundles squeezing in, a vendor selling peanuts; on the platform a few passengers are left behind waving at the train with resignation, waiting for the next one. Bright station daylight, crowded energy on the right. The two panels share the same platform with a tea stall, a book cart and a station clock, so the contrast is only inside the coaches. A railway attendant in the left panel hands a pillow to the calm passenger, while in the right panel a man squeezes in through the door with a tiffin held high. Labels: "CIRCUIT" at the top of the left panel, and "PACKETS" at the top of the right panel.

key: A private cab you pay for by the day
name: ch08_cab_vs_bus_capacity
alt: A private cab waits idle all day for one person at great cost, while a shared city bus is cheap but crowded at rush hour.
scene: A split-panel street illustration. LEFT panel: a shiny white private cab is parked outside an office building with its driver dozing behind the wheel, a newspaper over his face; a meter on the dashboard shows a large rising number, and a clock shows most of the day passing while a single passenger in a suit finally walks out at evening, alone in the back seat. Coins drain from the passenger's wallet in a small inset.
