RIGHT panel: a bus stop with a crowd of office workers, students and a vegetable seller; a red city bus pulls in full of people, some hanging on the footboard during rush hour, and a young woman checks her watch while waiting, but each passenger hands only a small coin to the conductor. A timetable board at the stop is blank with a question mark. Afternoon light changing to evening. The office building in the left panel has a glass front and a security guard, and the cab sits under a tree all day, leaves falling on its roof as the sun moves. In the right panel a small boy holds his mother's hand and a cyclist rings past the stop. The bus conductor wears a khaki uniform with a leather bag and a ticket punch. Labels: "STATIC" at the top of the left panel, and "DYNAMIC" at the top of the right panel.

key: Every house in your colony has a wall
name: ch08_colony_clocks_drift
alt: Five neighbours each show slightly different wall clock times, correcting them now and then from the TV news, which takes its time from a satellite.
scene: A row of five small colourful houses in a residential colony, drawn with their front walls cut away to show each family's living room. Each room has a wall clock showing a slightly different time: a few minutes apart, hands visibly misaligned. In each room a resident turns to answer a neighbour leaning over the boundary wall asking the time, and their speech bubbles show five different times. In the middle house, a TV on a cabinet shows a news anchor with a clock in the corner of the screen, and an elderly man stands on a stool adjusting his wall clock to match it. A thin line runs from the TV up into the sky to a small satellite with a tiny precise clock, glowing. Morning light, gentle humour. The houses are painted in pastel colours with potted plants, rangoli at the doorsteps and clotheslines on the roofs. In the first house a young mother answers with a baby on her hip, in the second a student with headphones, in the fourth an old woman with a newspaper, and in the fifth a man shaving with foam on his face. Each speech bubble is a small clock face rather than written numbers, the hands slightly different in each. Labels: "CLOCK DRIFT" across the five houses, "NTP" beside the man on the stool, and "GPS" beside the satellite.

key: Your old wind-up wristwatch gains
name: ch08_windup_watch_drift
alt: A wind-up watch gains time faster in hot Chennai than in cold Shimla, is set daily from the radio, and a child cheats a game by changing the phone date.
scene: A three-part illustration. LEFT: a man in a white half-sleeve shirt on a sweltering Chennai street, sweat on his brow, looking at his wind-up wristwatch, whose hands are drawn with a small fast-forward arrow and a thermometer icon showing heat. CENTRE: the same man in a woollen cap and shawl on a snowy Shimla mall road, his watch with a smaller arrow and a cold thermometer. Above both, a small transistor radio broadcasting time beeps, and the man sets his watch each morning, a tiny calendar showing daily ticks. Further along, a faded calendar with a month of no ticks leads to a picture of him running onto a platform as a train pulls away. RIGHT: a boy on a sofa secretly changing the date on a phone's settings screen with a grin while a game screen behind shows extra lives. Mixed lighting, playful mood. The man is the same office clerk in all scenes, with a moustache and a leather bag, so the viewer sees one watch behaving differently by place and over time. The boy's mother calls from the kitchen doorway, not noticing his trick. Labels: "DRIFT" above the two watch scenes, and "UNTRUSTED DEVICE" over the boy.

key: A slightly wrong weighing scale at a
name: ch08_wrong_weighing_scale
alt: A dead weighing scale gets fixed at once, while a scale that reads five percent light quietly loses money for months until checked against a known weight.
scene: A split-panel kirana shop illustration with sacks of rice and dal, a brass bell and a calendar on the wall. LEFT panel: a shopkeeper in a white vest taps a digital scale with a blank dark display, frowning, and a repairman with a toolbox is already walking in through the door, a wall calendar showing today's date circled. RIGHT panel: the same shopkeeper happily weighs onions on a scale whose needle reads a little light, a tiny downward arrow; behind him a calendar flips through many months and a cash box slowly leaks coins out of a small hole into a growing pile on the floor. In the foreground of the right panel, an inspector in a cap places a shiny standard weight on the scale with a magnifying glass, and a red tag saying stop using is being tied to it. Warm shop light, quiet worry on the right. Customers wait at the counter in both panels with cloth bags, one holding a toddler; in the right panel the shopkeeper smiles unaware as each customer leaves with slightly more onions than paid for. Labels: "OBVIOUS FAULT" at the top of the left panel, and "SILENT DRIFT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Two cashiers at a bank, each with a
name: ch08_bank_slips_clock_skew
alt: Two bank counters with wrong clocks stamp deposit slips, and head office throws away the later deposit because its stamp looks earlier.
scene: A bank branch hall drawn left to right. At counter 1, a cashier in a striped shirt stamps a deposit slip from a man in a blue kurta, the wall clock above the counter a little fast; an enlarged slip shows a time stamp. At counter 3 on the right, a cashier in a sari stamps a second slip from the man's wife in a yellow sari, whose slip has a small arrow pointing back to the first slip, but the clock above this counter is visibly slow, its hands behind. Both slips travel by a peon's tray to a head office desk in the background, where a clerk sorts them strictly by stamp time, keeps the first slip and drops the wife's slip into a wastebasket labelled superseded, with a faint coin outline vanishing above the bin. Nobody notices; the couple walks out smiling. Bright bank interior, ceiling fans, quiet mishap mood. The two clocks are drawn large and prominent, side by side if the viewer's eye traces across the hall, so the difference in their hands is easy to see. The wife's slip has a small note linking it to the first deposit, which the sorting clerk ignores. Labels: "CLOCK SKEW" between the two clocks, and "LAST WRITE WINS" over the head office desk.

key: (false precision). An honest conductor
name: ch08_bus_conductor_interval
alt: At a bus stop, a phone app gives a to-the-second arrival time while an honest conductor gives a range of a few minutes.
scene: A roadside bus stop with a tin shelter, a timetable board and a few people waiting: a schoolgirl with a heavy bag, an elderly man with an umbrella and a young professional with earphones. On the left, the young professional holds his phone where an enlarged inset shows a precise time down to seconds next to a bus icon, with a small decorative row of decimal digits floating off like confetti to show false precision. On the right, a bus conductor in a khaki uniform with a leather cash bag and a whistle leans out of a parked bus and holds his hands apart, as if showing a width, with a speech bubble showing a short time range on a ruler-like bar from one time to another. The elderly man nods trustingly at the conductor. In the distance, a road curves away with a bus just appearing over a hill. Morning light, calm humour. The bus shelter has a faded advertisement panel with no brand, a dog asleep under the bench and a tea vendor with a kettle nearby. The schoolgirl looks between the two sources, unsure which to believe. Labels: "FALSE PRECISION" above the phone inset, and "CONFIDENCE INTERVAL" above the conductor's spread hands.

key: Two exam invigilators with slightly
name: ch08_invigilators_wait_uncertainty
alt: Two invigilators with uncertain watches draw overlapping time ranges, so the first waits extra minutes before declaring submission.
scene: An exam centre courtyard with two separate exam rooms. In the left room, invigilator one, a woman in a blue sari with spectacles, collects the last answer sheet; above her a horizontal translucent band shows her time as a fuzzy range around a clock face. In the right room, invigilator two, a man in a sweater, holds a sealed envelope of answer keys about to open it; above him another fuzzy band. The two bands overlap in the middle, coloured with a striped hatch and a question mark. Below, a second version of the scene: invigilator one sits on a chair with a small hourglass, deliberately waiting before she announces, and her band has now moved fully to the left of his band, a clear gap between them with a green tick. Notice boards, a bell on a pole, morning sun across the courtyard. Each invigilator's wristwatch is drawn enlarged in a circle, with a soft blur around the hands to show the uncertainty. Students in the rooms sit at desks, some finishing, some handing in papers. Labels: "UNCERTAINTY" on the overlapping hatch, and "COMMIT WAIT" beside the waiting invigilator with the hourglass.

key: An ambulance vs a food-delivery rider
name: ch08_ambulance_vs_delivery_rider
alt: An ambulance with a cleared green corridor arrives on time for one patient, while a cheap delivery rider is usually on time but sometimes stuck for an hour.
scene: A split-panel city street illustration. LEFT panel: an ambulance with flashing lights races down an empty lane bordered by traffic police holding back cars on both sides, green signals all along the route, a stretcher with one patient inside visible through the rear window; a small price tag icon with many coins floats above. RIGHT panel: a delivery rider on a scooter with a big insulated box on the back, wearing a helmet and a rain jacket, threads through ordinary traffic; most of the frame shows him dropping bags at doors with smiling customers, but on one side he is stuck in a dense jam behind a bus and a cow, checking a phone showing a late order, and another tiny vignette shows him waiting at a restaurant counter while the cook is busy. Busy evening traffic, honest everyday mood on the right. Onlookers on the left pavement watch the ambulance with folded hands, and a small sign on a post shows it took a lot of planning. In the right panel the customers waiting at doors are mostly satisfied, and only one checks his watch at the late order. Labels: "REAL-TIME" at the top of the left panel, and "BEST EFFORT" at the top of the right panel.

key: A restaurant with three cooks. Instead
name: ch08_cook_planned_washup
alt: A head chef tells one cook to finish current plates and wash up while the other two take new orders, so customers never wait.
scene: A busy restaurant kitchen viewed through a wide service hatch. Three cooks in white jackets stand at a long range of burners. The head chef, a bearded man in a tall cap, points at cook two and says in a speech bubble to finish current plates then wash up. Cook two is plating his last two dishes, and a dotted arrow leads from him to a deep sink with a pile of dirty pots, where a ghosted future version of him scrubs. Meanwhile order tickets on a rail are being re-routed with small arrows only to cooks one and three, who are happily cooking. In a small inset in the corner, the bad alternative: a cook suddenly abandoning a sizzling pan mid-order to wash dishes, with smoke rising and customers glaring, crossed out. The dining room beyond the hatch shows customers being served without delay. Warm kitchen light, organised bustle. Copper pans hang above the range, steam curls from a pot of rice, and a waiter in a white uniform waits at the hatch with an empty tray. Labels: "GC PAUSE" in the crossed-out inset, and "PLANNED BREAK" above cook two.

key: Studying a faraway star: the light you
name: ch08_faraway_star_light
alt: A girl looks at a star through a telescope, but the light she sees left it long ago and the star may have already changed.
scene: A rooftop at night in a small town, water tanks and a TV antenna silhouetted, a girl of about 12 in a sweater kneeling at a small telescope on a tripod, her father beside her holding a star chart and a torch. Overhead, a vast starry sky; one bright star in the far upper right is shown in two forms: the star as she sees it, small and steady, and next to it a faint ghost of the same star as it is now, already changed and swollen red. A long ray of light runs from the star down to the telescope with tiny calendar pages drifting along it, showing many years of travel. In a small inset at the bottom left, two servers on a desk are joined by a long dashed message arrow carrying an old snapshot photo of the other server's state, with a clock showing it is already out of date. Deep blue night, peaceful wonder. Fairy lights from a neighbouring rooftop twinkle, and the father points up with his torch while the girl adjusts the focus with excitement. A cat sits on the parapet watching them. Labels: "OLD NEWS" along the ray of light, and "PAST STATE" beside the inset snapshot.

key: A token number at a government office
name: ch08_token_counter_fencing
alt: At a government office counter, the clerk has served token 34 and refuses token 33 who wanders back from the canteen.
scene: A government office hall with wooden benches, an overhead token display, and a clerk's window with a grille. The display shows the number 34 glowing. At the window, a middle-aged clerk in a beige cardigan with a pen in hand has just finished stamping a file for token 34, a woman with a folder walking away. A man in a crumpled shirt, holding a paper token with 33 on it and a glass of tea from the canteen, insists at the window with a raised finger; the clerk holds up a firm palm and taps the display. A small rubber stamp on the counter shows a big red rejected mark. Behind, other people on benches hold higher tokens and watch. A counter rule sign beside the window shows an upward arrow of numbers. Afternoon light through tall windows, bureaucratic but fair mood. A ceiling fan turns slowly above the benches, a stack of files tied with red tape sits on a shelf behind the clerk, and a notice board lists office hours. The man with token 33 looks indignant, still holding his tea. Labels: "FENCING TOKEN" on the overhead display, and "REJECTED" above token 33's paper slip.

key: some umpires might be fixing the match
name: ch08_umpires_byzantine
alt: A third umpire panel with some broken cameras, a hidden crooked umpire, and all umpires watching the same buggy replay software.
scene: A cricket stadium's third-umpire room high above the ground, a glass window overlooking the pitch. A row of five umpires in white shirts and black blazers sit at monitors. On the wall, a bank of camera feeds: most show the batter clearly, two feeds are fuzzy static, labelled by a small broken-camera icon. One umpire at the end of the row has a slight sly smirk and a hidden wad of cash peeking from his pocket, which the others cannot see, drawn with a subtle shadow over his face. Above the row, every monitor runs the same replay software window with an identical glitch, a pixelated ball, and a red bug icon on all screens at once. Down below, players and fans wait under floodlights for the decision. Evening floodlit stadium, tense mood. The umpires wear headsets and take notes on clipboards, a coffee cup at each station. Through the window, the giant stadium screen shows a big question mark while the decision is pending, and the crowd holds flags. Labels: "CRASH FAULTS" over the static feeds, "BYZANTINE" over the smirking umpire, and "SAME BUG" over the glitching screens.

key: Counting cash at a bank: the cashier
name: ch08_bank_sanity_checks
alt: A bank cashier recounts a bundle, refuses an absurd cheque amount and trusts the two clocks that agree out of three.
scene: A bank teller's cabin from inside, a glass partition with a small slot, a cash-counting machine and a stack of rubber-banded notes. The cashier, a sharp-eyed woman in her 40s in a sari with her hair in a bun, recounts a bundle by hand with a rubber thimble on her finger, a small tick mark appearing over the bundle. On the counter, a cheque pushed through the slot shows an absurdly long row of nines in the amount box, and she slides it back with a firm shake of the head. On the wall above her, three clocks: two show the same time, one is clearly off, and a small finger points at the two matching clocks with a majority sign. In the background, a masked robber silhouette is drawn faintly on a poster as a reminder that these simple checks do not stop serious crime. Bright bank lighting, competent mood. A queue of customers waits patiently outside the glass with passbooks, and a security guard with a rifle sits on a stool at the door. Labels: "CHECKSUM" over the recounted bundle, "SANITY CHECK" over the rejected cheque, and "MAJORITY" beside the two matching clocks.

key: never two customers with the same number
name: ch08_bakery_token_machine
alt: A bakery token machine gives unique, increasing numbers and always gives a slip to whoever presses the button.
scene: A cosy neighbourhood bakery with glass cases of puffs, cakes and buns, a warm oven glowing at the back. Near the door stands a red token dispenser on a pole; a little girl in a frock presses its big button and a paper slip curls out, while her mother waits behind. Customers on a bench hold slips with consecutive numbers, and above them a display shows the current number being served. Three small icons float near the dispenser in a row: a fingerprint symbol for unique numbers, an upward staircase for increasing numbers and a hand receiving a slip for always getting one. The baker, a jolly man in a white cap and apron, calls out the next number while holding a tray of fresh buns. Golden morning light, sweet aroma swirls, cheerful mood. Shelves behind the counter hold loaves wrapped in paper, a tray of nankhatai cookies and a glass jar of rusks. An old man on the bench reads a newspaper while waiting with his slip. The display number and the slips in people's hands are plain round numbers so the order is easy to follow. Labels: "UNIQUE" by the fingerprint, "MONOTONIC" by the staircase, and "AVAILABLE" by the hand.

key: will stop the train in a storm
name: ch08_train_safety_liveness
alt: A train halted by staff in a storm stays safe and will still reach Mumbai later; safety is kept by giving up speed.
scene: A dramatic illustration of a long passenger train halted on a bridge over a swollen river during a monsoon storm, rain slashing diagonally and lightning in the dark clouds. A guard in a raincoat with a red lamp stands beside the engine, signalling stop, and the driver leans out of the cab nodding. Inside the lit windows, passengers look out patiently, a child pressing her nose to the glass. At the far right end of the track, beyond the storm, the skyline of a city is visible in sunshine with a station signboard reading Mumbai, a dotted line showing the train will still get there. In a small inset at the bottom left, a crossed-out scene of the train speeding through the storm and tilting off the track, showing what must never happen. Stormy blue-grey light with warm window glow. The river below churns brown and fast, and a signal post on the bridge glows red. A tea vendor inside the coach keeps serving passengers, who sit calmly with blankets. Labels: "SAFETY" over the guard with the red lamp, and "LIVENESS" beside the distant city.

key: earthquake design assumes
name: ch08_earthquake_model_fire_exits
alt: Engineers prove a building survives a modelled earthquake but still add fire exits for when reality goes beyond the model.
scene: A tall modern apartment tower under construction, shown in a cutaway. On the left, two structural engineers in hard hats, one woman with a tablet and one older man with rolled blueprints, stand beside a seismograph chart with a dashed maximum line, and a big green tick shows the building passes under the modelled shaking. Inside the building, braces and dampers are drawn in the walls. On the right side of the tower, bright red emergency staircases spiral down the outside, glowing exit signs above each door, a fire extinguisher on each landing, and an evacuation map on the wall of one floor. Above the building, a dramatic seismograph line rises beyond the dashed maximum, showing reality exceeding the model, with the exits highlighted. Clear daylight with dust clouds, serious but reassuring mood. Workers on scaffolding wave from the upper floors, and a crane stands beside the tower. A safety notice board at the site entrance shows a building icon with an exit arrow. Labels: "SYSTEM MODEL" above the engineers' chart, and "FALLBACK" beside the red emergency exits.

key: electricity voltage stabiliser at home
name: ch09_voltage_stabiliser
alt: A home voltage stabiliser turns a wildly swinging grid supply into a steady output for the fridge.
scene: A clean kitchen corner in an Indian flat, seen from the front. On the left wall, a power socket is fed by a thick cable coming from outside the window, where a zigzag, wildly jumping voltage line is drawn like a lightning-shaped graph, with small storm clouds and a flickering street lamp on a pole behind. The cable enters a grey metal voltage stabiliser box mounted on the wall, with a needle dial and a small green light, and out of the other side flows a perfectly flat, calm, straight line into a tall fridge decorated with fridge magnets and a child's drawing. The fridge hums happily, a painted smile on a magnet. A middle-aged woman in a cotton nightie opens the fridge door to take out milk, completely unbothered. In a small inset in the top right corner, a dark house during a total blackout shows the stabiliser light off, a tiny candle on the counter, to show what the box cannot fix. Morning light through a window with a mosquito net. Labels: "MESSY FAULTS" above the jagged line outside, and "CLEAN PROMISE" above the flat line entering the fridge.

key: A school notice gets photocopied to 5
name: ch09_peon_notice_boards
alt: A peon walks around a school pinning photocopies of the principal's notice on five classroom boards, so some boards are briefly out of date.
scene: A cutaway view of a single-storey school building with five classrooms in a row along a veranda, each with a small notice board beside its door. On the far left, in the principal's office, a stern principal in a white sari and spectacles hands a freshly signed notice to an elderly peon in a khaki uniform with a cloth bag full of photocopies. A dotted footpath shows the peon walking slowly along the veranda in a loop, past classrooms one to five. Boards one and two already show the new notice with a bright yellow paper; boards three, four and five still show yesterday's notice in pale blue. Outside room five, a curious girl in a pinafore reads the old blue notice and shares it with a friend, while the principal at the far end has just changed it. A wall clock and a hand bell hang on a pillar. Bright mid-morning sunlight, slow and gentle mood, a crow on the veranda railing. The peon walks with a slight limp and a cheerful face, a pot of glue and a brush in his other hand. Labels: "EVENTUALLY CONSISTENT" above the veranda, and "STALE" beside the old blue notices.

key: A railway platform display switching
name: ch09_platform_display_no_flipback
alt: A platform board changes a train from on time to delayed, and once one passenger has seen delayed, everyone after must see delayed too.
scene: A railway platform under a tin canopy with an overhead electronic display board, amber letters on black. The board is caught mid-change: the left half of the scene shows the board reading on time with a green dot, the right half shows the same board reading delayed forty minutes with a red dot, a smooth transition line between them like a page turning. Below, a row of passengers stand in time order from left to right, each with a small numbered tag. The passenger in the middle, a young man with a backpack, looks up and sees delayed; a bright arrow runs from him to every passenger standing to his right, who all see delayed too. A ghostly crossed-out speech bubble above a passenger further right shows on time with a red X, the forbidden flip back. On the left, before the change, a grandmother calmly reads on time. Morning light, tea vendor with a kettle, pigeons on the rafters. Each passenger's line of sight to the board is drawn as a thin dotted line. Labels: "LINEARIZABLE" across the top of the display, and "NO GOING BACK" beside the crossed-out bubble.

key: A bank passbook printed by one clerk
name: ch09_one_clerk_passbook
alt: Customers queue at many windows but a single clerk prints every entry into one passbook in one order.
scene: A bank hall with three customer windows on the left, each with a short queue: an elderly man with a cloth bag, a college student with a backpack, a woman in a sari with a toddler. All their slips travel along little conveyor-belt arrows that merge into one single desk on the right, where one clerk in a striped shirt and arm sleeves sits at a dot-matrix passbook printer. The passbook in the printer shows a single column of entries, each line numbered, printed one after another, with the latest balance at the bottom. A small floating inset above shows a ghost of an older balance line trying to reappear at the bottom and being stopped by a raised palm. Wall clock, ceiling fan and a rubber stamp rack complete the hall. Bright daylight through tall windows, orderly mood. The clerk wears reading glasses on a cord and works with steady concentration, a stack of passbooks waiting at his elbow. Customers at the windows chat or check their phones, unaware that everything they hand in ends up in the same single line of print. A small brass bell and a calendar sit on the clerk's desk. Labels: "ONE ORDER" above the printer, and "NO OLD VALUE" beside the stopped ghost line.

key: terrace water-tank room, kept with the
name: ch09_water_tank_key_split_brain
alt: Two watchmen at two gates each think the terrace key is still on their hook, so two people get the key: split brain.
scene: A housing society seen from the side with a staircase going up to a rooftop where a padlocked door leads to the water tank room. Two security cabins stand at two different gates at the bottom: the north gate on the left and the south gate on the right. In each cabin a watchman in a uniform and beret points at a key hook on his wall with a confident grin, and each hook holds what looks like the very same brass key with a red tag, drawn identically. From each cabin, a resident walks up the staircase holding a key: a plumber with a wrench from the left, an electrician with a coil of wire from the right. They meet face to face at the terrace door, both holding up identical keys, with a big lightning bolt between them. In a small inset at the top left corner, a single key on a single hook with a lock icon shows the correct state. Late afternoon sun, comic tension. The building is painted cream with green window grilles and potted plants on balconies, and a few residents peer over the railings curiously. Labels: "SPLIT BRAIN" at the terrace door, and "ONE LOCK" in the corner inset.

key: one berth left, thousands clicking
name: ch09_last_berth_vs_overbooking
alt: At ten sharp thousands click for one last berth and exactly one gets it, while an airline overbooks and later pays a volunteer to fly later.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a big wall clock at exactly ten, below it a sea of hands clicking on phones and laptops in many homes and cyber cafes, drawn as a fan of tiny windows; at the centre, a single railway berth glows and one lucky young woman in a hoodie jumps with joy holding her phone with a confirmed tick, while every other screen around her shows a waitlisted icon instantly. RIGHT panel: an airport gate with a large plane outside the window; more passengers than seats stand around, and a gate agent in a blazer holds up an envelope of cash and a voucher, offering it to a relaxed traveller in a cap who smiles and raises his hand to volunteer for the next flight. A small inset under the right panel shows two trains facing each other on the same track with a stop sign, the case that can never be fixed afterwards. Bright daylight, energetic mood. The left panel's tiny windows include a cyber cafe with rows of PCs, a family huddled over one phone, and a student in a library. Labels: "STRICT" at the top of the left panel, and "COMPENSATE LATER" at the top of the right panel.

key: You pay a shopkeeper by UPI and say
name: ch09_payment_shout_beats_bank
alt: A customer pays by phone and shouts done, but the shopkeeper's phone has not buzzed yet because the bank's message is slower.
scene: A small sweet shop counter with glass jars of laddoos and a hanging bell. On the left, a young man in a checked shirt holds up his phone and calls out cheerfully, a big speech bubble flying quickly across the counter in a short straight arrow. On the right, the shopkeeper, a plump woman in an apron with reading glasses, looks at her own phone lying on the counter, blank and silent, and shakes her head. Overhead, a long winding dotted line with a slow-moving snail icon travels from the young man's phone up through a bank building in the sky and back down to her phone, still on its way. A second customer, an old man in a cap, pays quietly beside them without saying anything, unaffected. Warm shop light, gentle comedy. Shelves of sweets in steel trays line the walls behind the shopkeeper, a ceiling fan turns lazily, and a small framed picture of a deity hangs above the cash box. The young man's grin and the shopkeeper's sceptical frown face each other across the glass counter, while the old man in the cap simply waits for his packet of jalebi, unbothered by any delay. Labels: "FAST CHANNEL" on the speech bubble arrow, and "SLOW CHANNEL" along the winding bank route.

key: A school with one official register kept
name: ch09_class_register_substitute
alt: The class teacher keeps the official register with copies to the office, until a substitute starts her own register and there are two truths.
scene: A classroom scene with a split focus. At the front, the class teacher, a woman in a crisp cotton sari with a pen in her hair, writes in a thick official register with a gold star sticker on its cover, and dotted arrows carry photocopied pages out of the door to a school office where a clerk files them in a steel cabinet. In the next room, visible through a connecting door, a young substitute teacher in a cardigan has started her own separate register with a different coloured cover and is confidently marking attendance too; a child is marked present in one book and absent in the other, shown by a tick and a cross on two floating mini-pages. Children in both rooms look confused. In the corridor, the principal with a walking stick approaches to settle it. Morning light, gentle confusion. Rows of children sit on benches with slates and school bags, a blackboard behind each teacher, and the school bell hangs in the corridor. The two registers look almost identical except for the cover colour, which makes the danger easy to see. Labels: "LEADER" on the gold-star register, and "TWO TRUTHS" between the two conflicting mini-pages.

key: Three newspaper stalls in your colony
name: ch09_newspaper_stalls_quorum
alt: Three newspaper stalls get the morning edition at different times, so one reader asking two stalls sees the result and another asking two others does not.
scene: A colony street corner with three small wooden newspaper stalls in a row, each with magazines clipped on a string. A delivery van on the right has just dropped a fresh bundle of morning papers only at stall three, which now displays the new edition with a big headline picture of a garlanded winner. Stalls one and two still display yesterday's paper with a faded look. A young man in a tracksuit stands between stalls two and three holding both papers, smiling. Ten minutes later, drawn on the left with a small clock icon, his neighbour in a lungi and vest asks stalls one and two, holding two copies of yesterday's paper and looking puzzled. Overhead, little coloured arcs show which two stalls each reader asked. Early morning light, milk packets on doorsteps. Each stall has a different owner: a young boy on a stool, an old man with a cap and a woman with a flask of tea. The van's driver tosses the bundle with a thud, papers fanning out. Small dates printed on the papers are drawn as two different calendar icons so the viewer can tell old from new without reading text. Labels: "QUORUM READ" above the young man, and "STILL STALE" above the puzzled neighbour.

key: is like a restaurant menu saying
name: ch09_cap_flooded_kitchen
alt: A restaurant in a monsoon flood must either close the kitchen or serve only what is in the fridge, since nobody chooses the flood.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same small restaurant during a monsoon flood, water knee-deep in the street outside, a supply truck stuck at the end of the road with its driver waving helplessly. LEFT panel: the owner in a white shirt pulls down the shutter and hangs a closed sign, the menu board behind him still showing every dish neatly; customers in raincoats turn away. RIGHT panel: the shutter is open, and the cook serves plates from a half-empty fridge, the menu board has several dishes crossed out with chalk, and customers happily eat whatever is available. Between the panels at the top, a humorous chalkboard reads choose two with three icons, a plate of food, a stack of plates and a raincloud, the raincloud circled as not a choice. Rainy grey light, puddle reflections. An auto-rickshaw is stuck in the water beside the truck, and a child floats a paper boat in the street. Labels: "CONSISTENT" at the top of the left panel, "AVAILABLE" at the top of the right panel, and "PARTITION" over the stuck truck.

key: Office staff sharing one whiteboard vs
name: ch09_whiteboard_vs_notebooks
alt: Office staff write in their own notebooks for speed and sync up at stand-up, instead of walking to one shared whiteboard each time.
scene: An open-plan office drawn in a wide shot. At the far end of a long corridor stands one big shared whiteboard covered in tasks. In the foreground, four colleagues at their desks each write quickly in their own spiral notebooks, pens flying, a small speed-line effect showing how fast this is. A long dotted path with footprints shows how far one would have to walk to the whiteboard each time, with a tired stick figure halfway along it. In the centre right, the same four colleagues stand in a circle at a stand-up meeting next to the whiteboard holding their notebooks, copying entries onto it, with a little sync icon of two circular arrows above them. A coffee machine, plants and laptops fill the office. Bright morning light, productive mood. The four colleagues are a young woman in a kurta with a pen behind her ear, a man in a hoodie, an older woman with reading glasses and a man in a formal shirt. The whiteboard's coloured sticky notes match the entries in their notebooks after the meeting. Labels: "CPU CACHE" above the notebooks, "MAIN MEMORY" on the whiteboard, and "MEMORY FENCE" over the stand-up circle.

key: A hospital OPD token system. The token
name: ch09_opd_token_leader
alt: A hospital token machine sets the order for doctors, while without it two receptionists might hand out the same token number.
scene: A hospital outpatient waiting hall with rows of steel chairs and patients waiting: a pregnant woman, an old man with a cane, a mother with a feverish child. On the left wall, a single token machine on a stand dispenses numbered slips, with a small crown icon above it, and a digital display above the doctors' cabins shows the current number. Three doctors' cabins on the right each have a doctor in a white coat calling the next number in order, arrows from the machine to each cabin. In a small inset at the bottom right, the bad alternative: two receptionists at two separate desks both handing out paper slips with the same number, two patients holding identical slips looking at each other in confusion, crossed out. Clean fluorescent hospital light, calm mood. Nurses in white walk past with files, a ceiling fan turns overhead, and a water cooler stands in the corner. The numbers on the display and on the slips are simple and large, and each doctor's door has a small light that turns green when it is the next patient's turn, so the single source of order is easy to follow. Labels: "SINGLE LEADER" above the token machine, and "DUPLICATE" in the crossed-out inset.

key: A WhatsApp group where Mom asks
name: ch09_cake_reply_before_question
alt: A cousin's phone shows a reply saying me before the mother's question about who brings the cake, which looks absurd.
scene: Three people in three locations connected by curved message lines. Top left: a mother in a kitchen with flour on her hands types a question on her phone, a speech bubble with a cake icon and a question mark. Top right: her son on a college bench types a quick reply bubble with a raised hand and a smiling face. Bottom centre: a cousin on a sofa holding a phone, the phone screen enlarged showing a group chat (no logos) where the son's raised-hand reply appears ABOVE the mother's cake question, with a confused frown on the cousin's face and a big question mark. Thin dotted arrows show the question leaving first but arriving late to the cousin, tangled behind the reply. A tiny inset shows the correct order with the question first and a green tick. Warm evening light, comic confusion. The three people are drawn at different scales on a soft blue background, and the tangled arrows look like a ball of string, emphasising how the network mixed up the order. Labels: "CAUSALITY VIOLATED" over the cousin's phone, and "CORRECT ORDER" in the small inset.

key: A family tree vs a queue at a ration
name: ch09_family_tree_vs_ration_queue
alt: A ration shop queue where everyone has a definite place, next to a family tree where cousins on different branches have no order between them.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a ration shop with a wooden counter, sacks of rice and wheat, and a weighing scale; in front of it a single straight queue of people with numbered tags 1 to 6 painted on the ground under their feet: a woman with a cloth bag, a boy holding a ration card, an elderly man, all in a clear line. RIGHT panel: a large hand-drawn family tree on a wall chart with small framed portraits: a grandfather at the top, two sons below, and their children branching further; an arrow chain runs down from grandfather to father to a young man, but between the young man and his cousin on the other branch there is a double-headed dashed line with a question mark showing neither comes first. Bright daylight in the left panel, a cosy home wall in the right. In the left panel the shopkeeper weighs rice on a balance while a poster on the wall shows grain prices without words. In the right panel the portraits are simple warm faces of different ages in oval frames, a garlanded photo of the grandfather at the top, and a child points at the double-headed arrow, puzzled. Labels: "TOTAL ORDER" at the top of the left panel, and "PARTIAL ORDER" at the top of the right panel.

key: carton of your new almirah before
name: ch09_almirah_cartons_order
alt: A courier delivers part two of a flat-pack almirah before part one, and the owner sets it aside until part one arrives.
scene: A flat's front door with a courier boy in a uniform and cap handing over a large cardboard carton marked with a big printed 2 of 2 on the side. The flat owner, a young man in shorts and a T-shirt, signs the receipt and points to a corner where he places the carton aside under a sticky note with a clock drawing. A second scene to the right, a little later, shows another courier arriving with carton 1 of 2; the young man now has both cartons open on the floor, with steel shelves and screws laid out, an instruction sheet with numbered steps, and he assembles the almirah in order with a screwdriver, a numbered sequence of 1 then 2 drawn as arrows. Afternoon light through a balcony door, a ceiling fan, practical calm mood. The flat has a shoe rack by the door and a calendar on the wall. The first scene shows the young man pausing thoughtfully rather than opening the box, a hand on his chin, and the second scene shows him whistling as he tightens the last screw, a cat watching from the sofa. The almirah's grey steel doors stand finished at the end, with a small mirror on the inside. Labels: "HOLD BACK" over the set-aside carton, and "CAUSAL ORDER" above the assembly scene.

key: Two bank branches issuing token numbers
name: ch09_branch_token_ranges
alt: A customer takes token 1005 at one branch then token 7 at another for a follow-up, so sorting tokens wrongly puts the follow-up first.
scene: Two bank branches on either side of a busy road. The left branch has a sign showing a low number range on its token machine; the right branch shows a high number range. A man in a white shirt and tie with a file folder is drawn twice: first at the right branch taking a slip with a large high number, then walking across a zebra crossing with a dotted path, and then at the left branch taking a slip with a small single-digit number for a follow-up. In the foreground, a clerk at a sorting table lays the two slips in number order, the small number first, and a timeline arrow beneath shows the real order was the opposite, a red cross linking them. Bright daytime street, scooters, a tea stall. The man looks pleased with himself, unaware of the confusion he causes. Each branch has a glass door, a security guard on a stool and a queue of customers in chairs; the token machines are red stands with a single big button. The sorting clerk wears a cardigan and spectacles and works methodically, trusting only the numbers on the slips, so the viewer sees how sorting by token number puts the follow-up visit before the first visit. Labels: "REAL ORDER" along the timeline arrow, and "WRONG ORDER" over the sorting clerk's slips.

key: Village gossip with numbered notes
name: ch09_village_gossip_lamport
alt: Villagers pass numbered gossip notes, and each new note gets a number one higher than the highest number its writer has seen.
scene: A village scene with mud houses, a banyan tree with a platform, and a well. Notes on small paper slips pass between houses carried by children running barefoot. On the left, a moustached man in a dhoti writes a note numbered 5. A child carries it to a woman in a red sari outside her house on the right, whose last note on her wall pin was numbered 1; she reads the 5 and writes her next note numbered 6, a thought bubble showing the calculation of the higher number plus one. Further right, a third house has also written a 6 independently, and a tie-break sign shows the two sixes ordered by house number painted on the doors. In the foreground on the banyan platform, an old man sorts all the notes in number order with a satisfied nod. Golden evening light, chickens and a goat. The children carrying notes are barefoot and laughing, one balancing a note on his head. Each house has a nail on its front wall where the latest note number is pinned, making each person's counter visible. Smoke rises from a chulha and a bullock cart rests under the tree. Labels: "LAMPORT TIMESTAMP" above the woman writing 6, and "TIE-BREAK" beside the two sixes.

key: Two exam centres in different cities
name: ch09_exam_centres_earliest_stamp
alt: An invigilator in Pune cannot announce the earliest sheet as winner because a sheet from Nagpur with an earlier stamp may still be in the post.
scene: A wide illustration with two exam centres on the left and right and a head office in the centre background. In the left centre, an invigilator in a blue sari stamps an entry time on an answer sheet and starts to raise a hand to announce a winner, but freezes. In the right centre, another invigilator in a sweater stamps an earlier time on another sheet, which is put into an envelope and handed to a postman on a scooter riding along a long winding road towards the head office. At the head office, a clerk sits waiting at a desk with an in-tray, only able to decide when all envelopes arrive, and a small checklist shows one centre still missing. Midday light, dusty roads, patient tension. The two centres are labelled by small city skylines above them, one with a fort and one with orange trees, without written names. Students in both centres hand in sheets and leave, chatting. The postman's road is long and curving, passing fields and a level crossing where a train makes him wait, showing how late a sheet can arrive. The head office clerk sips tea, watching a wall clock. Labels: "CANNOT DECIDE YET" above the frozen invigilator, and "STILL IN TRANSIT" over the postman.

key: The Sensex ticker on every TV channel
name: ch09_market_ticker_channels
alt: Several TV channels show the same stock ticker in the same order, one channel a few seconds behind but never out of order.
scene: An electronics shop window with a wall of four televisions, each tuned to a different news channel (generic, no logos), each with a scrolling market ticker band at the bottom showing small coloured blocks with arrows up and down. The blocks appear in the exact same sequence on all four screens, drawn with matching colours so the order is obvious; on the fourth screen the ticker is slightly behind, the same sequence shifted a little to the right. A cable bundle from all four TVs leads to a single source building on the far right, a stock exchange tower with a big clock. Passers-by on the pavement watch: an office worker with a briefcase, an auto driver leaning out, a student with a cycle. Evening street light, neon reflections. Each television shows a different anchor in a studio: a woman in a blazer, a man with a beard, an older man in spectacles and a young reporter, but the moving band at the bottom of every screen is identical. A shopkeeper inside the glass leans on the counter watching the screens. The fourth TV's band has a tiny clock icon showing it is a few seconds late, yet the same blocks follow in exactly the same order. Labels: "TOTAL ORDER BROADCAST" above the TVs, and "SINGLE SOURCE" on the exchange tower.

key: A cricket ball-by-ball commentary log
name: ch09_ball_by_ball_log
alt: A ball-by-ball log that is only ever appended to, replayed by scorers in different stadiums who all reach the same score.
scene: A long paper scroll unrolls across the top of the image like a ribbon, each segment a ball of an over with a small icon: a dot, a four, a six, a wicket. The latest ball is being added at the right end by a scorer's hand with a pen, and an earlier gap in the scroll has a red slash over a hand trying to squeeze in an extra ball, rejected. Below the scroll, three small stadium scorer boxes in different cities, each with a scorer at a manual scoreboard flipping number plates, all reading the scroll from left to right and arriving at the same total on their boards. A third umpire's review appears as a new correction ball at the end of the scroll, not an edit. Bright afternoon light, stadium flags. The scorers are diverse: an older man in a cap, a young woman with a notebook, and a teenager on a stool. Each scoreboard has big painted numbers and a small hut roof. The three stadiums are drawn as small round vignettes with green grounds and floodlight towers, linked to the scroll by thin arrows, and all three totals show the same number plates. Labels: "APPEND ONLY" on the scroll, and "SAME STATE" above the three matching scoreboards.

key: single register book at the gate for
name: ch09_gate_register_first_line
alt: Residents write their names in one gate register for the Diwali clubhouse booking, and whoever wrote the first line for that slot gets it.
scene: A housing society gate with a security cabin, decorated with Diwali lamps and a hanging lantern. On the cabin's counter lies a single thick register book, open, with a guard in uniform holding it steady. Three residents lean over it: a young woman in a festive kurti, an older man in a shawl, and a teenager with headphones around his neck. On the page, a heading with a small lamp icon is followed by several lines with names; the first line is highlighted with a soft glow, and the young woman whose name is on it points to it with a delighted smile, while the others nod in agreement. A small inset in the top corner shows three identical copies of the register in three different gates with arrows between them and a question mark, hinting at the hard part. Warm diya light, evening festival mood. The guard steadies the register with one hand and holds a pen on a string with the other, and a sweet box from a resident sits on his counter. Labels: "FIRST WRITE WINS" above the glowing first line, and "REPLICATED?" in the inset.

key: Chapters of a serialised novel in a
name: ch09_serialised_novel_gaps
alt: A reader receives magazine issue 6 before issue 5 and knows to wait, but with jumpy numbers she could never tell whether something is missing.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a cosy reading nook with a cane chair and a cup of tea. LEFT panel: an elderly woman in a shawl holds a weekly magazine with a big 6 on the cover and looks at a small shelf where issues 1 to 4 sit neatly, with a clearly empty labelled gap for 5 between 4 and 6; she smiles knowingly and waits, a postman visible through the window carrying issue 5. RIGHT panel: the same woman holding magazines numbered with irregular big numbers, and the shelf shows uneven gaps with question marks between them; she scratches her head, unsure whether anything is missing. Soft afternoon light, homely mood. The magazines have colourful covers with simple drawings of characters, a different illustration each week. On a side table sit a pair of spectacles, a tumbler of filter coffee and a small radio. In the left panel the gap on the shelf is drawn with a dotted outline the exact size of one magazine, and a little calendar shows the expected day for issue 5. In the right panel the uneven gaps between irregularly numbered magazines are drawn with question marks in them, and a cat on the windowsill tilts its head in sympathy. Her expression changes from serene on the left to perplexed on the right. Labels: "GAP-FREE" at the top of the left panel, and "GAPS UNKNOWN" at the top of the right panel.

key: A joint family deciding whether to sell
name: ch09_joint_family_land_sale
alt: A joint family needs every sibling's signature to sell ancestral land, and separately chooses one head for the year.
scene: A large ancestral house courtyard with a tulsi plant, a swing and a brass lamp. LEFT side: five siblings of different ages sit on a durrie around a low table with a land sale deed, each with a signature line; four have signed, and the fifth line is empty while a video call on a tablet shows a sibling abroad in a winter coat, still thinking. A lawyer in a black coat waits with a closed briefcase. RIGHT side: the same family gathers around a wooden chair with a shawl draped over it, placing a turban and a big key bunch on the chair for the head of the family this year, an elderly uncle being gently guided to it with folded hands. A banana tree and a parked scooter fill the background. Warm late-afternoon light. The siblings include a brother in a formal shirt, a sister in a cotton sari, a younger brother in jeans and an elder sister in a shawl, all looking at the tablet. A dotted line links the empty signature line to the tablet to show the deal waits for him. On the right, children watch from the swing, and a grandmother in white blesses the uncle with a raised hand. The two halves of the courtyard are divided by a pillar to show these are separate decisions. Labels: "ATOMIC COMMIT" over the deed table, and "LEADER ELECTION" over the chair.

key: Friends deciding a movie on a group call
name: ch09_movie_vote_timeout
alt: Friends voting on a movie on a group call cannot tell if a silent friend is thinking or gone, so they agree a two-minute timeout.
scene: A grid of video call tiles shown on a laptop screen in a college hostel room, with four friends in their tiles: a girl with popcorn, a boy in a cap, a girl with curly hair holding up a movie poster, and one tile frozen with a spinning circle where the friend's face is blurred and still. Above the screen, a small row of movie poster icons with tally marks under each. In front of the laptop on the desk sits an hourglass that has just finished running out, a sticky note beside it with a simple rule drawn as a clock with a two and an arrow. The girl with the poster points at the hourglass and the others nod and decide. A tiny thought bubble above the frozen tile shows the friend actually just thinking with a hand on his chin. Evening hostel lighting, posters on the wall. The hostel room has a bunk bed, a study table with books and instant noodles, and a string of fairy lights. The friend whose tile is frozen is drawn larger in the thought bubble, chin on his hand, eyes on a movie list, showing that the silence might just mean he is slow. The remaining friends look relieved once the rule lets them decide. Labels: "TIMEOUT" on the sticky note, and "SLOW OR GONE?" above the frozen tile.

key: sign the register in different towns
name: ch09_half_marriage_two_towns
alt: The bride's and groom's families sign marriage registers in two different towns without checking each other, and one side refuses.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a winding road between two small towns. LEFT town: in a decorated hall, the groom's family in festive clothes and turbans proudly sign a marriage register at a registrar's desk, a garland on the table and a priest smiling. RIGHT town: in another decorated hall, the bride's family stand around a similar register, but the bride's father, a stern man in a white kurta, firmly closes the register and shakes his head, while relatives look shocked. In the middle of the road, a small figure of a couple is split down the middle, half of them glowing as married and half grey, with a big question mark. Bright festive colours, comic drama. The road between the towns has a milestone and a bus going past, emphasising the distance and the lack of communication. Neither family can see the other; a mobile tower on a hill between them has no signal bars. Guests in both halls are dressed in bright silks, garlands and turbans. The registrar on the left looks pleased and the one on the right looks embarrassed. Labels: "COMMITTED" over the left register, "ABORTED" over the right register, and "HALF DONE" over the split couple.

key: Booking a group trip: each friend first
name: ch09_group_trip_holding_account
alt: Friends each transfer money to a holding account and vote yes, then the organiser books and writes booked in his diary, even if one friend's phone dies.
scene: A wide illustration with four friends in their own homes around the edges and an organiser in the centre. Each friend holds a phone sending a coin along an arrow into a central glass piggy bank with a lock, and each has a green tick speech bubble saying they are in. In the centre, the organiser, a young man with a cap and a travel backpack, sits at a desk with a laptop showing train tickets and writes in a small leather diary a big underlined word, with a stamp beside it. In the bottom right corner, one friend's phone lies on a bed with a dead battery icon, while she sleeps; a dotted arrow shows the news waiting for her when she wakes. Cheerful daylight, travel maps on the wall. The four friends are a girl in a hostel room, a boy at a cricket ground, a young man in an office and the sleeping girl. Each green tick is drawn like a raised hand. The organiser's laptop shows a train and four seats, the diary is open on a table next to a mug of tea, and the moment of writing is highlighted with a soft glow, the single point after which the trip is definitely on. Labels: "PREPARED" above the piggy bank, and "COMMIT POINT" over the organiser's diary entry.

key: who collapses after telling only the
name: ch09_pandit_collapses_in_doubt
alt: The pandit faints after telling only the groom they are married, and the bride must wait, unsure, until he recovers and checks his notebook.
scene: A wedding mandap decorated with marigolds, banana leaves and a small sacred fire. The pandit, an elderly man in a white dhoti and a shawl, has fainted on a cushion, a small notebook slipping from his hand, while two relatives fan him. On the left, the groom in a cream sherwani and turban beams, having just heard he is married, a small speech bubble with a ring icon near him. On the right, the bride in a red lehenga stands frozen with a confused face, looking from the groom to the pandit, a big question mark above her head; she holds her dupatta tightly and does not move. In the background, guests whisper. A small inset in the corner shows the pandit later sitting up with spectacles and reading his notebook, the answer revealed. Warm firelight and festive colours, tense moment. Musicians with a shehnai and a dhol pause mid-tune at the side, and the bride's mother reaches out a hand but stops, unsure whether to celebrate. The groom's family has already started throwing rice, while the bride's side stands still, waiting for word. Labels: "IN DOUBT" above the bride, and "COORDINATOR DOWN" beside the fainted pandit.

key: 3PC is like a plan that says
name: ch09_monsoon_timeout_lies
alt: A group waits for the organiser's call; after ten minutes some go ahead and some stay, because a weak monsoon signal made the silence lie.
scene: A monsoon street scene with heavy rain, a tilted mobile tower on a rooftop with weak signal bars, and puddles everywhere. A group of five friends under a bus stop shelter in raincoats is split: three walk off to the left with umbrellas, having decided the organiser must be gone, a clock icon above them showing ten minutes passed; two stay on the right, phones to their ears, waiting. Far away in the background, the organiser sits in a cafe frantically pressing call on his phone, which shows one weak bar, his call drawn as a broken dotted line that never reaches them. Grey rain light, a sense of splitting. The friends are in their early twenties, one in a yellow raincoat, one with a broken umbrella, one carrying a backpack. The two who stay hold their phones up hoping for signal, while the three walking away wave goodbye. A bus splashes past, and the cafe in the background has steamed windows and a warm yellow glow. The viewer can see that the organiser is alive and trying, while the friends cannot. Labels: "TIMEOUTS LIE" over the broken call line, and "SPLIT GROUP" above the separating friends.

key: Splitting a restaurant bill inside one
name: ch09_bill_split_three_systems
alt: Splitting a bill inside one shared app is easy, but paying one bill all-or-nothing across a wallet, a card and a gift voucher is hard.
scene: A split-panel restaurant table scene. LEFT panel: four friends at a table with empty plates each look at the same bill splitting app on their phones (generic), each screen showing the same neat split pie chart, and they smile and give a high five. RIGHT panel: a single customer at the cash counter tries to pay one bill using three things at once: a phone wallet, a bank card and a paper gift voucher; three little machines and clerks behind the counter each speak in a different shaped speech bubble (square, round, zigzag) and none look at each other, wires tangled between them, while the cashier scratches her head. Warm restaurant lighting, comic contrast. In the left panel the table has empty thali plates, glasses of lassi and a small bowl of saunf, and the friends' phones are all the same simple shape. In the right panel the cashier counter has a cash drawer, a card machine and a voucher stamp, each machine with a tiny clerk who looks only at his own machine. A queue forms behind the customer, and one man in the queue checks his watch, showing how hard it is to make three separate systems all agree before money moves. Labels: "ONE SYSTEM" at the top of the left panel, and "HETEROGENEOUS" at the top of the right panel.

key: a retry sends a second SMS, because
name: ch09_duplicate_payment_sms
alt: Marking an order paid and removing it from the queue happen together so a retry is harmless, but the SMS sent on a retry goes out twice.
scene: A food delivery company's back office drawn as a clean flow diagram with characters. On the left, a clerk at a desk stamps an order card as paid and slides it out of a pending tray in one smooth motion, both actions inside one dotted box with a small rewind arrow showing they can be undone together. On the right, a separate SMS tower sends a message bubble to a customer's phone; because the step was retried, two identical message bubbles arrive on the phone and the customer, a young woman on a sofa, raises an eyebrow at the duplicate. A small cannot-undo icon, a closed padlock over the tower, shows that the SMS cannot be taken back. Bright clean colours, light humour. The back office has a wall of order tickets, a cork board and a coffee mug. The order card shows a simple plate icon and a coin icon. The SMS tower is drawn as a tall antenna with radio waves, and the duplicate messages arrive a second apart, each with a small coin icon and a tick. The customer's sofa has cushions and a bowl of biryani beside her, the order already delivered. Labels: "EXACTLY ONCE" over the dotted box, and "SENT TWICE" above the customer's phone.

key: A wedding planner who keeps the only
name: ch09_planner_diary_in_pocket
alt: A wedding planner keeps the only record of confirmations in his pocket diary and is hospitalised, leaving the caterer and decorator stuck.
scene: A split illustration. LEFT: a hospital bed where a wedding planner in a hospital gown lies asleep with a drip, and a small leather diary peeks out of the pocket of his jacket hanging on a chair. RIGHT: outside a decorated wedding hall, the caterer in an apron next to huge cooking vessels and the decorator on a ladder holding marigold garlands both stare at their phones, waiting for a call that does not come; their own phones cannot call him, shown by a crossed-out arrow pointing from their phones to him, and an arrow pointing the other way that is dashed and empty. Piles of half-prepared food and half-hung decorations sit frozen. A calendar shows the wedding date approaching. Contrasting cool hospital light and warm hall light. A nurse checks the drip and a get-well card stands on the bedside table. The decorator's ladder leans against an arch half covered in flowers, and the caterer's helpers sit idle on upturned vessels, playing cards. The bride's family stands in the hall doorway looking worried. The diary is drawn slightly glowing to show it holds the only copy of the decisions. Labels: "COORDINATOR LOG" on the diary, and "IN DOUBT" over the waiting caterer and decorator.

key: A car parked across the society gate
name: ch09_car_blocking_gate_lock
alt: A car parked across a society gate by someone who said two minutes blocks everyone, because the owner fell asleep.
scene: A housing society entrance with a sliding iron gate and a security cabin. A small hatchback is parked diagonally across the gate, hazard lights blinking. Behind it inside the society, a school van with children, a delivery scooter and a resident's car queue up honking; outside, an ambulance and a vegetable cart wait. A note on the car's windscreen shows a clock with two minutes drawn. In a thought bubble above, the car owner is shown asleep on a sofa in a nearby flat with a newspaper on his chest. The watchman in a beret stands next to a tow truck with his hand on his chin, deciding whether to tow. Midday heat, frustrated mood. The school van driver leans out with his arm waving, children's faces pressed to the windows; the scooter rider holds a pizza-style delivery box with no brand; and the ambulance's light flashes blue. A small crowd of residents gathers on the inner side holding shopping bags and briefcases. The car itself is ordinary and grey, doing nothing, which is exactly the point. The watchman's whistle hangs from his neck, and his face shows he is unsure if he is allowed to move the car. Labels: "HELD LOCK" on the car, and "BLOCKED" over the waiting vehicles.

key: A court case where the only file was
name: ch09_court_file_lost_flood
alt: A court's only case file is lost in an office flood, freezing the parties until a judge reconstructs it, while a clerk decides one thing alone.
scene: A district court record room partly flooded, water covering the floor, soggy files floating, a clerk in a white shirt holding an empty folder with a worried face. In the next room, two parties to the case sit on opposite benches with frozen expressions: a man next to a padlocked house drawing and a woman holding a bank passbook with a chain around it. On the right, a judge in a black robe at a raised bench questions witnesses one by one, writing notes to reconstruct the case. In a corner, a junior clerk secretly cuts the chain off the woman's passbook with scissors, an anxious look over his shoulder at the judge. Monsoon rain outside the barred windows, grey light, serious mood. The two parties look anxious and powerless, unable to sell or spend, and an old wall clock shows weeks passing. The court building has tall pillars and a peeling notice board, lawyers in black coats crowd the corridor holding umbrellas, and a typist sits outside under a tin shade with a typewriter. Labels: "IN DOUBT" over the frozen parties, and "HEURISTIC DECISION" above the junior clerk.

key: needs signatures from 7 departments
name: ch09_seven_signatures_vs_quorum
alt: A government file that needs seven signatures stops when one officer is on leave, while a committee needing four of seven keeps working.
scene: A split-panel government office illustration. LEFT panel: a thick file tied with red ribbon sits on a desk with seven signature boxes; six are signed, and the seventh desk is empty with a nameplate and a sign showing a holiday palm tree, a peon sitting on a stool with the file waiting, cobwebs forming. RIGHT panel: a committee room with seven chairs around a table, two empty with leave notes, and five members raising their hands to vote; a vote counter on the wall shows four is enough with a green tick, and a resolution paper is being stamped. Afternoon light through window blinds, ceiling fans. In the left panel each desk has a nameplate and a rubber stamp, and the officers who have signed are leaving for lunch while the file waits on the stool, its ribbon gathering dust; a calendar shows many days crossing off. In the right panel the committee members are a mix of men and women in formal clothes, water glasses and files on the table, and a secretary at the end types the resolution on a laptop. The two empty chairs have small notes with a plane icon and a hospital cross icon, explaining the absence. Labels: "ALL MUST SIGN" at the top of the left panel, and "MAJORITY" at the top of the right panel.

key: A parliament session where each item
name: ch09_assembly_batched_votes
alt: In an assembly the speaker proposes agenda items in batches and members confirm them, building an ordered list of passed motions.
scene: A grand legislative assembly hall (generic, no national emblem) with semicircular benches of members in kurtas and shawls, and a speaker in a high chair at the front with a gavel. Beside the speaker, a long scroll unrolls down the wall listing numbered motions with green ticks, newest at the bottom. The speaker holds up a tray carrying three motion papers at once, and members raise hands in agreement, a single sweep of raised hands drawn across the benches. A clerk at a table writes the three motions onto the scroll in order. Warm chandelier light, formal mood. Members sit at polished wooden desks with microphones and nameplates without readable names. A gallery above holds visitors and reporters with notebooks. The three motion papers on the speaker's tray are drawn with different coloured seals so the viewer sees they are separate items passed together. On the scroll, earlier items show single entries and the newest three appear together in one bracket, but still in a strict numbered order. Ushers in white uniforms stand at the doors, and a large clock above the speaker shows the session running late into the evening. Labels: "LEADER" above the speaker, and "ORDERED LOG" on the scroll.

key: but the president just resigned
name: ch09_club_president_resigned
alt: A college club whose rule says the president conducts elections, but the president has just resigned and nobody knows who should run the vote.
scene: A college club room with posters, a notice board and a long table. At the head of the table, an empty chair has a president's sash draped over it and a resignation letter on the seat. Around the table, club members in casual clothes look at each other with puzzled expressions, one holding a ballot box, another holding the club rulebook open to a page with a circular arrow drawn on it, pointing from the president back to the election. In the doorway, a faculty advisor in a tweed jacket peeks in, but a small crossed-out icon over him shows that machines cannot call such a person. Afternoon light, mild comedy. The members are a girl in a denim jacket, a boy with a guitar, a quiet student with glasses and a girl in a sports jersey; each looks to another as if expecting them to take charge. The notice board behind them is covered with event posters and a sheet with the club's rules, one rule highlighted. A ballot box sits unopened on the table, a pile of blank ballot slips beside it. Through the window, students walk across a green campus lawn. The empty chair is drawn slightly spotlit to emphasise the missing leader who should run the vote. Labels: "WHO RUNS THE ELECTION?" above the empty chair.

key: Society committee elections every year
name: ch09_committee_epoch_circular
alt: An old committee's secretary sends a circular, but residents who know there is a newer committee ignore it, so he cannot collect enough signatures.
scene: A housing society corridor with flat doors on both sides. A secretary in an old-fashioned cardigan carrying a circular and a badge with an older year number knocks on doors. Residents at most doors hold up a newer badge with a higher number, each shaking their head and pointing at a notice on the lobby board that announces the new committee with a group photo. On the secretary's clipboard, the signature list has only one or two signatures out of many lines. At the end of the corridor, the new committee members stand together with their own higher-number badge, smiling. Daylight through a corridor window, light comedy. The corridor has shoe racks, potted plants and name boards beside each door. Residents answer the door in everyday clothes: a woman with a ladle, a man in a towel, a child holding a cricket ball, an elderly couple. The badges are drawn as large round pins with numbers, the newer number clearly higher, so the viewer understands that residents compare numbers and reject the lower one. The secretary looks bewildered, his circular crumpling. Labels: "OLD EPOCH" on the secretary's badge, and "NEW EPOCH" on the notice board.

key: security desk register: it is small
name: ch09_security_register_coordination
alt: A society security desk register lists who is inside, numbers every entry, expires visitor passes, and pings residents when guests arrive.
scene: A housing society security desk at the main gate, with three guards in uniform sharing one compact register that is shown enlarged above them. The register has short numbered entries, each with a small serial number badge, all identical in each guard's view. On the right, a visitor holds a pass with a small clock that is running out, with a gentle reminder bell icon. In the background, a resident on a balcony with a phone has set an alert, and a dotted arrow shows the guard pressing a button to ping her when her guest arrives. On the left, one guard steps away and a second takes over the same register seamlessly. Bright daytime, orderly mood. The gate has a boom barrier, a small garden and a board of flat numbers. The guards are an older man with a moustache, a young man and a woman in uniform, all looking at the same page. The serial number badges on each entry go up one by one. Labels: "SMALL SHARED STATE" above the register, "LEASE" on the visitor's pass, and "WATCH" near the resident's phone.

key: A cricket tournament with hundreds of
name: ch09_selection_committee_team_sheet
alt: A three-member selection committee publishes a team sheet that hundreds of players read, while scores are kept by a separate scoring desk.
scene: A cricket tournament ground with many players in coloured kits practising in the nets. In a small pavilion on the left, three selectors sit at a table, a woman and two men in blazers, writing a team sheet. The sheet is pinned on a large notice board outside, and dozens of players crowd around it reading their positions, nobody voting. On the right side, a separate scoring box with a scorer and a digital scoreboard updates ball by ball, a stream of small balls flowing into it. Bright afternoon sun, flags and tents. The selectors sit with water bottles and a stack of player profiles, and the team sheet is a simple grid with names replaced by small player silhouettes and batting positions. Players at the notice board include a tall bowler, a young wicketkeeper with pads and a batter holding his helmet, some pointing excitedly, others shrugging. A dotted line shows the sheet changing only between matches, with a small calendar beside it, while the scoring box receives a constant flow of tiny ball icons every few seconds. Spectators sit on the grassy bank under umbrellas, and a coach with a whistle walks between the nets. The calm, small committee contrasts with the busy crowd of players and the fast stream of scores. Labels: "COORDINATION SERVICE" over the three selectors, and "DATA" over the scoring box.

key: the directory being up is more important
name: ch09_stale_directory_number
alt: A man calls a shop from a slightly old phone directory and still mostly reaches it, but the shop's ownership must be officially decided.
scene: A split illustration. LEFT: a man in a vest at home thumbs through a thick, slightly worn local business directory, his finger on a listing, and dials a landline; a dotted line runs to a busy hardware shop where a shop assistant answers cheerfully. RIGHT: inside the same shop, a formal handover ceremony: an old owner hands a big key bunch and a signed document to a new owner in front of a lawyer and a witness, a rubber stamp descending. In a small corner inset, a parcel is delivered to the old owner's house by mistake, and the new owner holds up a signed paper to check it. Warm daylight, everyday mood. The directory is thick with tabs and a coffee ring on its cover, and the man ticks off the number with a pencil. The hardware shop has racks of tools, paint tins and coils of rope. The handover ceremony on the right is solemn: the lawyer holds the document flat, the witness signs, and the old owner smiles with relief. In the small inset the delivery boy scratches his head as the new owner shows the stamped paper, establishing who really owns the shop now. Labels: "AVAILABLE" above the phone directory, "AGREED" over the handover, and "FENCING" in the inset.

key: Attendance in a class: if each student
name: ch09_official_attendance_monitor
alt: Students each keep their own attendance lists and pick different monitors, until the teacher announces one official list and everyone agrees.
scene: A classroom split into two moments. LEFT side: several students each hold their own little handwritten attendance list and point to different classmates as the monitor, arguing, with small crowns hovering over three different children at once. RIGHT side: the teacher in a sari at the front holds up one official register, reading it aloud, and a single crown sits above one child, everyone nodding; one student wrongly marked absent raises a hand to protest, a little cloud over his head, but sits down to rejoin later. Blackboard, a globe on the teacher's desk, and morning light through barred windows. On the left side the students' lists are scraps of paper, a notebook page and a hand with names written on it, and the three floating crowns compete for attention. On the right side the register is large with a hard cover and the teacher's finger traces a column of ticks. The protesting boy is drawn with his bag on his back as if he arrived late, accepting he will be marked present tomorrow. Labels: "MANY VIEWS" over the arguing students, and "ONE MEMBERSHIP LIST" above the official register.

key: Wipe the slate and you can recount from
name: ch10_bill_book_slate_derived
alt: A kirana shop's carbon-copy bill book is the source of truth, and the slate total, dues list and best-seller note are all derived from it.
scene: Inside a small kirana shop at closing time, shelves of rice, soap and biscuit packets behind a wooden counter, a single tube light humming. In the centre of the counter lies a fat bill book with pink carbon copies, its pages fanned to show every sale. Three derived things surround it, each linked by a thin arrow from the book: on the left, a black slate with a chalk total for the day; at the top, a small notepad listing customers who owe money with little coin icons; on the right, a sticky note on the shelf with a noodle packet drawing and a Sunday calendar icon, the shop's best-seller hint. The shopkeeper, a cheerful man in his 50s with a white vest and a towel on his shoulder, has just wiped the slate clean with a cloth and is recounting from the bill book with a pencil, unbothered. In a small inset at the top right corner, the opposite disaster: the bill book is gone, only the slate remains, and the shopkeeper stares at a lone number with a question mark, unable to check it. His young son watches from a stool, eating a toffee. Warm yellow light, tidy and reassuring mood. Labels: "SYSTEM OF RECORD" on the bill book, and "DERIVED DATA" beside the slate.

key: The ticket counter is a service: one
name: ch10_station_service_batch_stream
alt: A railway station shows three ways of working: a ticket counter serving one passenger at a time, a night accounts job, and a live departure board.
scene: A three-panel illustration of the same busy railway station, separated by thin vertical pillars. LEFT panel: a ticket counter in daytime with a clerk in a white shirt serving one passenger at a time through a grille, a queue of people with suitcases checking their watches impatiently, a stopwatch icon above showing that response time matters. MIDDLE panel: the same station at night, empty and quiet; in a back office under a single lamp, an accountant in a cardigan sits with a huge pile of the day's ticket stubs going in on one side and a single neat report coming out on the other, no one waiting at the window, a moon visible through the window. RIGHT panel: the main concourse with a large live departure board whose rows are updating as trains move, a train pulling in on one platform and the board changing to arrived, passengers glancing up as they walk. Each panel has a distinct light: bright day, lamp-lit night, and a glowing board.
