Labels: "SERVICE" at the top of the left panel, "BATCH" at the top of the middle panel, and "STREAM" at the top of the right panel.

key: delivery register: one row per parcel
name: ch10_courier_register_rows
alt: A courier office register has one boring row per parcel, but counting across thousands of rows reveals which PIN code gets most parcels.
scene: A courier company back office with steel shelves stacked with parcels, a weighing machine and a ceiling fan. On a long desk lies an enormous ledger opened across two pages, ruled into neat columns with small icons for date, sender, receiver, weight and status, and each row is one parcel, many rows filling the pages. A bored clerk with oiled hair and a pen behind his ear yawns while writing yet another row. On the right, a young analyst in a kurti with a calculator and coloured highlighters has pulled out a stack of old registers and is tallying a single column, and above her a simple bar chart floats like a thought bubble where one bar towers above the others with a little map pin icon on top. Dozens of small dotted lines run from many rows into the tall bar, showing value only emerges when counting across many records. Morning light through dusty windows, parcels with string and stamps. A courier boy drops another sack of parcels by the door. Labels: "ONE ROW PER EVENT" over the ledger, and "AGGREGATE" over the bar chart.

key: line all gift boxes up in alphabetical
name: ch10_gift_count_notebook_vs_lineup
alt: Counting wedding gifts either with a notebook of tally marks per guest or by lining up gift boxes in name order and counting each run.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a wedding hall the morning after the ceremony, marigold garlands still hanging, a stage with two empty chairs in the background. LEFT panel: an uncle in a kurta sits at a table with a notebook, writing one line per guest and adding tally marks every time a gift from that guest is opened; the notebook is overflowing, with extra pages taped on and falling off the edge, and an aunt hands him yet another box with a new name, while he looks stressed. RIGHT panel: a long line of colourful wrapped gift boxes stretches across the hall floor, sorted by the giver's surname with small name tags; a teenage cousin walks along the line with a clicker counter, counting each run of same-tag boxes and writing one number at each run's end. The floor space is generous, with room for many more boxes. Bright morning light, helpful family mood. Children run between the boxes in the right panel, and a bride's younger sister holds a tray of tea for the counters. Labels: "HASH TABLE" at the top of the left panel, and "SORT THEN COUNT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Sorting exam answer sheets for a whole
name: ch10_exam_sheets_external_sort
alt: A clerk sorts answer sheets two hundred at a time into sorted piles on the floor, then merges the piles by taking the smallest top sheet.
scene: A university examination office, the floor covered with neat stacks of answer sheets tied with string. In the centre, a small wooden table holds just a modest pile of sheets, the most it can fit, and a clerk in a beige safari suit with spectacles sorts them by roll number into a single tidy pile. Behind him on the floor stand many such sorted piles in a row, each with a small paper flag. On the right, a second scene: the same clerk sits cross-legged on the floor with several of those piles arranged in a semicircle in front of him, and he repeatedly picks the top sheet with the smallest roll number from whichever pile has it, placing it on one final growing stack beside him; a curved arrow loops from the piles to the final stack. Through a window, a university clock tower is visible. Morning light, dust motes, patient and methodical mood, a cup of tea going cold on a stool. The clerk's spectacles slide down his nose and he wipes his brow with a handkerchief. Labels: "SORTED RUNS" above the row of piles on the floor, and "MERGE" above the final stack.

key: The standard Indian 3-pin plug
name: ch10_three_pin_plug_interface
alt: A mixer, a phone charger and a table fan, all different machines, all fit the same three-pin wall sockets.
scene: A clean kitchen-and-living-room wall with a row of identical white switchboards, each with a standard round three-pin socket and a small red indicator light. Three very different appliances stand below: on the left a mixer-grinder on the kitchen counter, in the middle a phone charger with a phone on a shelf, on the right a table fan on a study table with a stack of books. Each appliance's cable ends in the same standard three-pin plug, drawn large and identical, and dotted arrows show that any plug could go into any socket, crossing over each other. A young woman in a cotton kurta happily plugs the fan into the kitchen socket while her younger brother plugs the mixer into the study socket, laughing. In a small inset at the bottom right corner, a voltage label on the back of the mixer with a small question mark hints that the plug does not say what the machine needs inside. Bright daytime light, playful mood. Labels: "UNIFORM INTERFACE" above the row of sockets, and "ANY TO ANY" beside the crossing arrows.

key: A mixer-grinder motor. The motor
name: ch10_mixer_motor_attachments
alt: A mixer-grinder motor spins the same way whatever jar is attached; the cook chooses the attachment.
scene: A close-up of a kitchen counter with a mixer-grinder motor base in the centre, its dial and power cable visible, and three different jars arranged around it like spokes of a wheel: a small chutney jar with coriander and coconut on the left, a dry-grinding jar with spices on top, and a tall juicer jar with oranges on the right. A woman in her 40s in a printed nightie and an apron is clicking the chutney jar onto the base with a confident twist, while the other jars wait. The motor is drawn with a simple spinning arrow and a calm face, as if it doesn't care which jar is on top. Arrows from the hand to the jar show that the person does the wiring. A small inset at the bottom left shows two pots of different food trying to feed into the single opening of one jar at once, with a puzzled face, hinting at the two-input limit. Morning light through a kitchen window with curry leaves on the sill, cosy domestic mood. Labels: "LOGIC" on the motor base, and "WIRING" beside the hand attaching the jar.

key: Cooking from a recipe while tasting
name: ch10_dal_tasting_steps
alt: A cook tastes dal at each step while the raw ingredients stay untouched in the store room, so she can always start again.
scene: A home kitchen scene with a gas stove, a steel pressure cooker, a kadai of tempering with mustard seeds popping, and a wooden spoon. A young cook in a salwar suit with her hair tied back tastes a spoonful of dal from a small bowl with a thoughtful expression. Along the counter, three small tasting bowls are lined up with tiny step numbers 1, 2 and 3 beside them, each a sample from a different stage: boiled dal, after tempering, before salt. Behind her, through an open door, a store room shelf holds unopened sacks and jars of raw lentils, spices and onions, glowing softly, untouched. A dotted circular arrow runs from the store room back to the stove, showing she could start over any time. A small inset in the corner shows the reverse, a cooked pot with an arrow pointing back to raw lentils, crossed out with a red X. Warm afternoon light, steam rising, calm experimenting mood. A small window shows rain outside. Labels: "INSPECT EACH STEP" above the tasting bowls, and "INPUT UNTOUCHED" on the store room shelf.

key: A joint family storing photo albums
name: ch10_photo_albums_rooms_hdfs
alt: A joint family keeps photocopied photo albums in cupboards across rooms, with grandma's notebook listing which copy is where.
scene: A cutaway view of a large ancestral house with five rooms visible side by side, each room with a small wooden cupboard whose doors are open to show a few photo albums inside. The same album, recognisable by its red cover with a gold border, appears in three different rooms, linked by thin golden threads. Instead of one giant steel almirah, which stands crossed out in a small inset in the corner, the storage is spread out. In the central room, a grandmother in a white sari and spectacles sits on a swing with a notebook on her lap, its pages showing album icons with small room numbers beside them, and she points to where a grandson should look. In the rightmost room, water from a burst pipe floods the floor and a cupboard is soaked, but the red album is safe in two other rooms. Warm afternoon light, family pictures on the walls. Children play carrom in one room and an uncle naps in another, each room with its own character, while the albums in their cupboards stay calm and safe. Labels: "REPLICAS" beside the golden threads, and "NAMENODE" above grandma's notebook.

key: India Post sorting at night
name: ch10_post_night_sorting_shuffle
alt: Local post offices bag letters by destination hub in PIN order at night, trucks collect the bags, and each hub merges them for delivery.
scene: A night-time aerial illustration with four small local post offices on the left side, each lit by a bulb, where postal clerks in khaki sit on the floor sorting letters into canvas bags of different colours, each bag tied with a tag showing a destination hub, the letters inside stacked in order. In the middle, a road network carries small red mail trucks, each truck collecting only its own colour of bag from every post office, with criss-crossing headlights. On the right, two large sorting hubs receive the trucks; inside one, a worker pours all the same-colour bags onto a long table, merging the letters into one ordered stream, and at the end a postman with a bicycle collects a neat bundle for one address. Starry sky, quiet roads, a sleeping dog near a post office. Each bag colour matches a hub roof colour, so the viewer can trace every bag to its destination, and the letters inside are drawn as small envelopes in a neat sequence. Labels: "PARTITION AND SORT" over the local offices, "SHUFFLE" over the trucks, and "MERGE AND REDUCE" over the hub.

key: A school exam result process
name: ch10_exam_result_trays_workflow
alt: Teachers leave graded papers in one tray, the office tabulates them into a second tray, and the principal signs from that tray, each step waiting for the last.
scene: A school's administrative corridor shown as three adjacent rooms from left to right, connected by a long counter. In the first room, four teachers grade papers at desks and drop them in a big wooden tray marked with a pencil icon, one teacher still grading the last paper with a red pen. In the second room, office clerks in cardigans stand idle beside their own empty tray, waiting, while a head clerk with a moustache and a whistle stands in the doorway with a raised hand, holding them back until the last teacher finishes. In the third room, the principal, a dignified woman in a silk sari, signs mark sheets taken from a tray marked with a stamp icon. No one passes papers by hand; dotted arrows only go from tray to tray. Bright morning light, an old clock and portraits on the walls. The trays are large and labelled with simple icons rather than words, and a calendar in the second room shows the results day circled. The waiting clerks drink tea and look at the clock, showing time lost waiting for the slowest teacher. Labels: "JOB OUTPUT" on the first tray, and "SCHEDULER" above the head clerk.

key: you go through the full marks register
name: ch10_full_register_scan
alt: Finding one student means opening the register at a roll number, but making report cards means reading the whole register start to finish.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a school staff room with steel almirahs and a large wall clock. LEFT panel: a teacher in a sari opens a thick marks register at one page held by a ribbon bookmark, finger on a single row, quickly copying one student's marks onto a slip for a waiting parent at the door. RIGHT panel: the same teacher and two colleagues sit with the full marks register and a full student list laid side by side on a long table, both open at page one, and they slide their fingers down both books together in roll-number order, a long arrow showing they go from start to finish without jumping; a tall stack of finished report cards grows at the end of the table. A small inset over the right panel shows a hand flipping pages back and forth randomly with dizzy lines, crossed out. Morning light, chalk dust in the air. The parent at the door in the left panel is a father in a work shirt holding a helmet. Labels: "INDEX LOOKUP" at the top of the left panel, and "FULL SCAN" at the top of the right panel.

key: auditor checking every transaction of
name: ch10_auditor_photocopy_join
alt: A bank auditor either phones branches for every customer file or brings photocopies of all files once and sorts both piles by account number.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a bank audit room with a long table, files and a ceiling fan. LEFT panel: an exhausted auditor in a grey suit holds a landline phone to his ear, with a huge stack of transaction slips beside him and many dotted phone lines going out to tiny branch buildings on a map; a calendar on the wall flips through many days, and empty tea glasses pile up. RIGHT panel: the same auditor, now relaxed, sits between two neat piles on the table, one of transaction slips and one of photocopied customer files, both sorted by account number with small matching tabs, and he walks his fingers down both piles at once. A photocopier in the corner has just finished a big job, and a tiny clock on the photocopied pile shows it is from last week. Bright office lighting, satisfied mood on the right. The auditor's colleagues bring trays of tea and a stapler. The photocopied files are slightly greyer than the originals, hinting they are a snapshot, not live. Labels: "RANDOM LOOKUPS" at the top of the left panel, and "LOCAL COPY" at the top of the right panel.

key: Matching wedding RSVPs to the guest list
name: ch10_rsvp_sort_merge_join
alt: Guest-list cards and RSVP cards are sorted together by surname so one walk down the pile stamps each family's details onto its RSVPs.
scene: A wedding planner's desk at home, covered with invitation cards and envelopes. In the centre, one long merged pile of cards fans across the desk, sorted by surname: each family begins with a gold-bordered guest-list card on top, followed by several plain white RSVP cards belonging to that family. A young planner in a kurta with a pencil behind her ear walks her fingers down the pile, and a thought bubble above her holds a single gold card's details with a small house icon and a number of people, which she stamps with a rubber stamp onto each white RSVP below it until the surname tab changes colour. A dotted path shows she moves only forwards. In the far right corner, a towering stack of white RSVP cards for one celebrity family leans precariously, hinting at the slow case. Warm desk lamp light, marigold strings, cheerful working mood. Coloured tabs separate the families, so each change of surname is easy to spot. Her mother peeks in with a plate of snacks. Labels: "SORT-MERGE JOIN" above the merged pile, and "SKEW" beside the towering stack.

key: Sessionization is collecting every
name: ch10_order_slips_city_boxes
alt: Order slips are collected into one box per city for counting, and one user's screen taps are gathered in time order into her own box.
scene: A large back-office floor of a food delivery company (no logos), with a conveyor belt carrying thousands of paper order slips from many directions. On the left, workers sort slips into a row of open cardboard boxes, each box with a small skyline icon for a different city, and one worker counts the slips in a box with a clicker. On the right, a second row of boxes each has a small portrait of a user; a worker pulls every small tap card belonging to one young woman from scattered places on the belt and lines them up in time order in her box: an app icon, a magnifying glass with a biryani bowl, a cart and an exit door, drawn as a little comic strip of four frames. Bright warehouse lighting, organised bustle. The workers wear caps and gloves and stand on small platforms beside the belt. The city boxes fill to different heights, one overflowing, and a supervisor with a clipboard notes the counts. The user's box at the right is drawn larger, with a small clock beside each tap card, and a dotted line marks where a long gap of idle time would end her session. Labels: "GROUP BY KEY" above the city boxes, and "SESSION" above the user's lined-up tap cards.

key: A reduce-side join is like a big wedding
name: ch10_caterer_reduce_vs_map_join
alt: One caterer sorts all guests into tables at the door, while another, told guests are already seated by family, simply walks table to table.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a large wedding hall entrance and dining area. LEFT panel: a caterer in a white uniform and cap stands at the hall entrance holding a clipboard, sorting a big disorderly crowd of guests into numbered tables, with many arrows directing people to different tables, a few guests looking confused and a long line building outside; it is laborious but works for any crowd. RIGHT panel: a second caterer receives a note from the host showing a small seating chart already done by family, and calmly walks from one table to the next pushing a serving trolley, ladling food, each table already full of one family. A tiny inset in the right panel shows the seating chart being wrong, and a vegetarian family receiving chicken, with a surprised face and a red cross, showing silent wrong results. Festive lights, marigold arches, bustling mood. The host is a beaming uncle in a sherwani. Labels: "REDUCE-SIDE JOIN" at the top of the left panel, and "MAP-SIDE JOIN" at the top of the right panel.

key: Every billing counter in a supermarket
name: ch10_price_list_broadcast_join
alt: Every supermarket billing counter has its own copy of a small price list, so cashiers look up items without sorting customers.
scene: A wide supermarket front with six billing counters in a row, each with a cashier and a short queue of customers with trolleys and baskets. Above each counter hangs an identical small printed price list board, drawn in the same colours, and a set of dotted arrows comes from a single master price list at the manager's desk on the left, copying it to every counter. Customers are spread randomly across counters, not sorted by item. One cashier, a young man in a uniform cap, runs his finger down his own copy of the list to check the price of a packet of tea. In a small inset at the top right, a telephone-directory-sized price list too heavy for a counter has crushed the counter table, with a comic dent, showing when this stops working. Bright fluorescent store light, shelves of colourful unbranded packets. Customers include a mother with a toddler in the trolley seat, an old man with a cloth bag and a college student with instant noodles. Each cashier works independently without consulting the others. Labels: "BROADCAST" over the copying arrows, and "SMALL INPUT" on the master price list.

key: both the answer sheets and the question
name: ch10_exam_rooms_partitioned_join
alt: Answer sheets and question packets are both sorted into rooms by the same last digit, so each invigilator finds everything in their room.
scene: A school exam building with a row of ten classrooms, each door marked with a single large digit from 0 to 9. In the foreground, two peons push trolleys: one carries answer-sheet bundles and the other carries sealed question-paper packets, and each bundle and packet is tagged with the same coloured digit and delivered to the matching door. Inside room 3, an invigilator in a sweater opens a matching bundle and packet and hands them out, everything fitting. In a small inset at the bottom right, the mistake case: packets tagged by a different rule arrive at room 3 where students sit without question papers looking puzzled, but no alarm sounds and the invigilator does not notice. Morning sunlight in the corridor, potted plants, an orderly mood. The peons are an older man with a towel on his shoulder and a younger one whistling as he pushes. The digit tags are bright coloured circles, and each classroom door has a matching circle, so the pairing is obvious at a glance. Through the window of room 3, students sit in rows with pens ready. Labels: "SAME PARTITIONING" above the two trolleys, and "SILENTLY WRONG" in the inset.

key: A library catalogue card saying not
name: ch10_catalogue_card_metadata
alt: A catalogue card records not just where books are but how they are sorted and split, so the next librarian need not re-sort.
scene: A quiet library aisle with ten tall shelves marked by alphabet ranges on small brass plates, books neatly arranged by author. In the foreground, an old wooden card catalogue drawer is pulled out, and an index card is shown enlarged: it has small icons of a book, a sorting arrow from A to Z and a split icon into ten parts, telling exactly how the shelves are organised. A young librarian in a cardigan reads the card and nods, putting down a pile of books without re-sorting, while a ghostly crossed-out version of her in the background struggles to re-sort everything by hand. In a corner, someone has moved a few books to the wrong shelf without updating the card, shown with a small warning triangle. Soft afternoon light through tall windows. The library has a high ceiling with fans, a long reading table where students study, and a ladder leaning on a shelf. The new librarian carries a trolley of returned books and looks relieved because the card tells her exactly where each book belongs. The crossed-out version of her is surrounded by toppled stacks, sweating. Labels: "METADATA" on the enlarged card, and "STALE" beside the warning triangle.

key: Batch output is the overnight job
name: ch10_newspaper_back_office_plates
alt: A newspaper back office shows a clerk answering one reader's call, an editor reading a monthly report, and an overnight job making printing plates.
scene: A three-zone illustration of a newspaper office at night. LEFT zone: a customer service clerk in a headset answers a call from a single reader, a small speech bubble with a newspaper and a calendar icon about a subscription. MIDDLE zone: the editor, an older man with rolled sleeves and spectacles, reads a monthly circulation report full of bar charts on his desk under a green lamp. RIGHT zone: a big printing room where a machine produces shiny metal printing plates overnight, a technician in overalls sliding a finished plate into the giant printing press that will run at dawn; nobody reads the plate, the press uses it. Arrows show data flowing from a central archive into each zone. Night city skyline through windows. Stacks of yesterday's papers sit tied with string, a coffee machine hums in a corner, and a night watchman walks between the zones with a torch. The plates on the right are drawn shiny and reversed, clearly not meant for human reading. Labels: "OLTP" above the left zone, "ANALYTICS" above the middle, and "BATCH OUTPUT" above the printing plates.

key: The index at the back of a textbook
name: ch10_textbook_index_mapreduce
alt: Making a textbook's back index by noting each important word with its page, then gathering all pages for each word.
scene: A student's desk with a thick school science textbook open, a lamp and a pile of index cards. On the left, a student volunteer in a school uniform flips through pages and writes small cards, each with a leaf icon or a planet icon and a page number, dropping them into a box. On the right, a second student sorts the cards into alphabetical piles on the table, and then writes one line per word at the back of the book listing several page numbers together, a curved arrow from each pile to its line. A small ribbon at the bottom shows the finished index page with neat rows. Evening lamp light, cosy study mood, a cup of tea and a pencil sharpener. The first student is a girl with two plaits and a yellow ribbon, and the second is a boy with round glasses and a pencil behind his ear. The cards are small rectangles with a word icon on top and a page number below. In the middle of the table, a shoebox overflows with cards waiting to be sorted. On the finished index page, each word icon is followed by several numbers in a row. A bookshelf, a globe and a wall map fill the background. Labels: "MAP" above the student writing cards, and "REDUCE" above the student building the index lines.

key: A school changing its timetable
name: ch10_timetable_swap_atomic
alt: Changing a timetable class by class during the day causes chaos; printing the full new timetable and swapping the notice board at four is clean.
scene: A split-panel school illustration. LEFT panel: during the school day, a harried clerk walks from classroom to classroom with a marker, changing entries one by one on each room's timetable chart; through open doors, some classes have a maths teacher arriving while others have a music teacher, two teachers arguing in a doorway, children confused, a half-done trail of changes behind the clerk. RIGHT panel: in a quiet staff room, a teacher checks a fully printed new timetable on a table with a ruler; then at a wall clock showing four o'clock, two teachers lift down the old board from the notice wall and hang the new one in a single swap, with a curved arrow; the old board leans against the wall, ready to be re-hung if needed. Afternoon light, calm on the right. In the right panel, the peon holds a hammer and a nail ready, and students walk past the new board reading it calmly at the end of the day. Labels: "IN-PLACE UPDATES" at the top of the left panel, and "ATOMIC SWAP" at the top of the right panel.

key: Writing an exam answer in pencil on a
name: ch10_pencil_photocopy_vs_pen
alt: A student writing in pencil on a photocopy can redo a mistake on a fresh copy, while one writing in pen on the only original cannot.
scene: A split-panel illustration of two exam desks. LEFT panel: a girl in a school uniform writes in pencil on a photocopied answer sheet; when she spots a mistake, she smiles, crumples it and takes a fresh photocopy from a stack beside her, the clean original sheet safe in a plastic sleeve on the desk, a circular arrow showing she can start over. RIGHT panel: a boy writes in pen on the only original sheet; an ink blot spreads over a wrong answer, he stares in dismay, and a speech bubble over him shows a hand making a promise to be careful next time, which cannot fix the ruined page. Classroom background with a clock and a blackboard. A small hourglass in the left panel hints that rewriting still takes time. Soft daylight. Both students are the same age and in the same uniform, sitting at identical wooden desks with an invigilator walking between the rows. The girl's stack of fresh photocopies is drawn tall and generous; the boy has only his one sheet and a bottle of blue ink. A wall clock shows the exam time. Labels: "IMMUTABLE INPUT" at the top of the left panel, and "IN-PLACE WRITE" at the top of the right panel.

key: An MPP database is a fully equipped
name: ch10_restaurant_vs_community_kitchen
alt: A specialised restaurant kitchen is very fast at its fixed menu, while a rented community kitchen lets anyone cook anything.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a gleaming restaurant kitchen with matching stainless steel stations, each built for one dish on a fixed menu board, cooks in identical uniforms moving with precision, plates flying out on a conveyor at high speed. RIGHT panel: a big community kitchen hall with rows of rented gas stoves, mixed cooks bringing their own ingredients: a grandmother making biryani in a huge pot, a teenager decorating a birthday cake, a man frying samosas and a woman steaming idlis, shared shelves and fridges along the walls. It is slower and messier but full of variety. A small arrow at the bottom between the panels shows each side borrowing ideas from the other, a recipe card going right and a custom-order slip going left. Warm lighting in both, bustling mood. A head chef in a tall hat oversees the left kitchen with a stopwatch. In the right hall, a notice board lists booking slots and a caretaker with a broom chats with the cooks. A delivery van unloads mixed ingredients at the right-hand door. Labels: "MPP DATABASE" at the top of the left panel, and "GENERAL CLUSTER" at the top of the right panel.

key: The sushi principle, Indian version
name: ch10_raw_vegetables_data_lake
alt: Keeping raw vegetables in the fridge lets different cooks make salad, curry and pakoras, rather than one fixed dish cooked on day one.
scene: A family kitchen with an open fridge full of fresh raw vegetables in clear bags: tomatoes, onions, spinach, cauliflower, carrots. In front of it three cooks each take what they need: a teenage girl making a salad in a glass bowl, the mother stirring a curry in a kadai, and the grandfather dipping onion rings into batter for pakoras, steam and sizzle around them. In a small inset at the top left, a single pot of mixed sabzi cooked on day one sits alone on the stove, and three family members with plates all get the same dish, looking bored. In another small inset at the bottom right, a messy fridge with unlabelled bags tumbling out and a confused cook, a hint of chaos. Morning light, lively family mood. The kitchen has steel utensils on a rack, a calendar on the wall and a radio playing. The three cooks work side by side without getting in each other's way, each with a different knife and pan, and each dish is drawn colourfully and distinctly. The fridge light shines brightly on the raw vegetables, emphasising that the raw form is what everyone starts from. Labels: "RAW DATA" on the fridge door, and "MANY VIEWS" above the three cooks.

key: A food court sharing one central cold
name: ch10_food_court_shared_storage
alt: A dosa stall, a noodle stall and a juice bar all take ingredients from one shared cold storage room instead of trucking food between restaurants.
scene: A mall food court seen from slightly above. Three stalls stand in a semicircle: a dosa stall with a tawa, a noodle stall with a wok and flames, and a juice bar with a blender and fruit baskets, each with a cook in a different uniform. Behind them, a single big walk-in cold storage room with a heavy steel door stands open, its shelves full of crates of vegetables, rice sacks, fruit and milk. Helpers from each stall walk in and out carrying what they need, dotted lines from the storage to each stall. In the far background, a crossed-out delivery truck shows the old way of moving food between separate restaurants. Two helpers bump into each other at the storage door, hinting at competition for shared space. Bright mall lighting, busy lunch-hour crowd at tables. Customers at tables eat dosas, noodles and fresh juice, and a cleaner wipes a table. The cold room breathes a small cloud of cool mist, and a storage manager with a clipboard tracks who takes what. Labels: "SHARED STORAGE" above the cold room door, and "MANY ENGINES" above the three stalls.

key: A wedding hall that rents out empty
name: ch10_hall_tuition_preemption
alt: A tuition class uses an empty wedding hall cheaply but must leave when a wedding arrives, so the tutor notes progress on the board after each chapter.
scene: A large wedding hall with a stage and folded chairs. In the middle of the hall, a tuition teacher in a kurta and spectacles teaches a group of students on plastic chairs, a portable whiteboard beside him where he writes a chapter number with a tick after finishing each chapter. At the entrance on the right, a wedding party in bright clothes arrives with a dhol player and decorations, and the hall manager waves the tuition class towards the side door. The students pack their bags while the teacher snaps a photo of the board to resume later. A small inset at the bottom left shows the next day, the class in a different room, starting from the last ticked chapter instead of chapter one. Daylight through tall windows, festive colours arriving on the right. The students are teenagers with notebooks and calculators; one girl erases her notes reluctantly. A stack of plastic chairs leans against a wall, and a caterer's team begins unloading vessels behind the wedding party. The whiteboard's ticks are big and clear, so it is obvious where to resume. Labels: "PREEMPTED" above the arriving wedding party, and "CHECKPOINT" on the whiteboard.

key: A relay race where every runner must
name: ch10_relay_baton_locker
alt: Relay runners must put their baton in a locker and wait for all teams before the next runner starts, compared with a normal hand-to-hand relay.
scene: A split-panel athletics track illustration. LEFT panel: a row of metal lockers stands at the handover point; three teams' runners have locked their batons inside and the next runners stand waiting with hands on knees, while one slow runner from the fourth team is still far back on the track; a referee holds up a hand to stop everyone until all four lockers are shut. RIGHT panel: a normal relay handover, one runner in a red vest passing the baton directly into the next runner's hand, who is already sprinting, motion lines behind them. A small inset in the left panel shows a runner who fainted, and a teammate calmly opening the locker to fetch the baton safely. Stadium seats, bright sunny day. Spectators in the stands wave flags, and a scoreboard shows the times. The waiting runners in the left panel look restless, one checking her watch, another stretching. In the right panel the crowd cheers as the baton moves without a pause. Labels: "MATERIALIZE" over the lockers, "STRAGGLER" over the slow runner, and "PIPE" at the top of the right panel.

key: MapReduce is a factory where every
name: ch10_factory_warehouse_vs_conveyor
alt: In one factory every half-finished part goes back to a central warehouse between machines; in another, parts flow straight down a conveyor.
scene: A split-panel factory illustration. LEFT panel: a factory floor with machines in a row; between every two machines, workers on forklifts carry crates of half-finished parts into a big central warehouse with three identical copies on three shelves, and back out again to the next machine, which sits idle waiting for the whole batch to return; a lot of back-and-forth arrows. RIGHT panel: a modern assembly line with a single conveyor belt carrying parts directly from station to station, workers in overalls fitting pieces as they pass, and only one station in the middle where parts pause briefly to be sorted into order on a rotating table. Industrial lighting, steam and sparks. The left factory's warehouse is huge and dusty with stacked crates and a manager with a clipboard checking the three copies. The machines in the left panel have small clocks showing idle time. The right panel's workers are smiling, and finished products pop out at the end of the belt into a box. Small spark effects show the welding at each station. Labels: "MATERIALIZED STATE" at the top of the left panel, and "DATAFLOW" at the top of the right panel.

key: A recipe card instead of leftovers in
name: ch10_recipe_lineage_recompute
alt: When a pot of gravy spills, the cook simply remakes it from the recipe card and the raw ingredients in the store.
scene: A kitchen scene with a spilled pot of red gravy on the floor and a startled cat jumping back. The cook, a cheerful middle- aged man in an apron and a kerchief, is not worried: he holds up a recipe card with icons for onions, tomatoes, masala and a small timer, and points to a store room shelf where the raw ingredients are lined up. A dotted arrow shows him quickly remaking the gravy in a fresh pot. A small inset in the corner shows a different recipe card with a vague pinch-of-salt symbol and a question mark, next to two plates of food whose colours differ slightly, showing the risk of a non-exact recipe. Warm lighting, comic relief. The kitchen has tiled walls, a gas stove with two burners, a rack of steel plates and a calendar. The store room door is open, revealing shelves with labelled jars and baskets of onions and tomatoes. The recipe card is laminated and pinned to the wall with a magnet, slightly stained from use. A second pot already simmers on the stove, the cook stirring with a wooden spoon, a relaxed whistle drawn as musical notes. Labels: "LINEAGE" on the recipe card, and "RECOMPUTE" over the fresh pot.

key: Announcing exam toppers vs checking
name: ch10_toppers_vs_attendance_pipeline
alt: An attendance clerk ticks each student as they enter, but the person announcing toppers must wait until every paper is marked.
scene: A school entrance and staff room illustration. LEFT side: at the gate, an attendance clerk with a clipboard ticks each student the moment they walk in, a steady stream of students in uniforms passing her, each tick appearing instantly. RIGHT side: in the staff room, the principal stands near a podium with a microphone and a sealed envelope, but a teacher behind her still marks a tall pile of answer sheets, and the principal waits, looking at her watch; a podium stand with first, second and third place steps sits empty. A small arrow from the last unmarked paper to the top step shows it might be the best one. Morning light, school bell and flag pole. Students arriving at the gate wave and chat, their bags bouncing. In the staff room, the marking teacher wears glasses and a cardigan, with a red pen and a tall pile, and a fan blows a few loose sheets. A banner with a trophy icon hangs above the empty podium, and parents wait in chairs in the hall behind, fanning themselves with programmes. Labels: "PIPELINED" above the attendance clerk, and "MUST WAIT FOR ALL" above the waiting principal.

key: Spreading news in a joint family by
name: ch10_news_forwards_iteration
alt: News spreads round by round through a family's phone forwards, versus reprinting the whole family phone book every round.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a family network drawn as many small portraits connected by lines, like a web; in round one, a single aunt holding a phone glows, and in successive rings outward more relatives light up as the news is forwarded to their direct contacts, little message icons travelling along the lines; the rings stop when no new people light up. RIGHT panel: a tired printer operator at an old printing press prints an entire thick family phone book again and again, one copy per round, with just a few names ticked in each new copy, a tall pile of nearly identical books growing beside him. Bright colours on the left, dim workshop light on the right. The portraits in the left panel include grandparents, uncles, cousins and a baby, each in a small circle, and the rings of lit-up circles are numbered by round with small badges. In the right panel, the printer operator wears an ink-stained apron, a calendar above him shows rounds, and the pile of near-identical books is drawn very tall and wobbly. Labels: "ITERATION" at the top of the left panel, and "REWRITE EVERYTHING" at the top of the right panel.

key: Saving a long video game at checkpoints
name: ch10_game_checkpoints
alt: A gamer saves at checkpoints every five levels, so dying at level thirteen means replaying only levels eleven to thirteen.
scene: A teenage boy sits cross-legged on a bedroom floor with a game controller, a big TV in front of him showing a winding game map with numbered levels along a path. Flags with save icons stand at levels 5 and 10, glowing. His character has just fallen at level 13, a small skull icon there, and a curved arrow loops back to the flag at level 10, with levels 11, 12 and 13 highlighted for replay. On the floor next to him, a younger sister and a friend hold their own controllers and wait patiently, one of them eating chips. A small inset at the top corner shows a save bar loading slowly, hinting that saving costs time. Evening room lighting with posters and fairy lights. The game map is colourful with forests, castles and rivers, and the character is a small knight with a shield. The boy groans but keeps playing, a bowl of popcorn spilled beside him. On the TV, levels 1 to 10 are drawn as greyed-out completed steps, and the replayed levels glow orange. A mother peeks in from the doorway with a cup of milk. Labels: "CHECKPOINT" on the flags, and "REPLAY" along the looping arrow.

key: Seating 400 wedding guests across 4
name: ch10_wedding_guests_graph_partition
alt: Wedding guests seated randomly across four halls keep walking between halls, while seating families together keeps nearly everyone in place.
scene: A split-panel illustration of four connected wedding halls seen from above like a floor plan. LEFT panel: guests in colourful clothes are scattered randomly, and many dotted walking paths criss-cross between the halls as relatives try to find each other; a grandmother crosses three halls to meet her son, people bump in corridors. RIGHT panel: families are seated together in clusters within a hall, almost no paths cross between halls, just one or two connector guests (a social uncle in a bright turban) walking between them. A small inset at the bottom shows a single small hall with forty guests happily chatting, no walking at all. Festive lights, flower decorations. Each hall is drawn as a square with round tables, and families are coloured groups of small figures. In the left panel, the corridors are crowded and a waiter with a tray squeezes through. In the right panel the corridors are almost empty and people dance inside their own halls. The connector uncle waves cheerfully as he crosses between two halls. Labels: "RANDOM PLACEMENT" at the top of the left panel, and "GRAPH PARTITIONING" at the top of the right panel.

key: instructing a cook step by step
name: ch10_menu_order_vs_cook_steps
alt: Ordering a dish by name versus standing in the kitchen telling the cook every step, while the kitchen still does all the steps either way.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same restaurant. LEFT panel: a woman at a table points at a menu card and says one short line to a waiter with a notepad, a small chilli icon with a minus sign beside the dish picture; through a hatch, the kitchen busily cooks with many steps happening on its own. RIGHT panel: a man in a shirt and tie stands right next to the cook at the stove, reading from a long scroll of detailed instructions with icons for oil, cumin, a stopwatch and stirring, while the cook follows each step with a resigned face. In a small inset on the right panel, a dish not on the menu is being explained step by step, showing when detailed instructions are still needed. Warm restaurant lighting. The woman in the left panel relaxes with a glass of water, chatting with a friend, while the man in the right panel sweats from the kitchen heat, holding his scroll. The cook in the left panel works with fluid motion, moving between several pans. A wall clock in each panel shows the left order finishing faster in effort for the customer. Labels: "DECLARATIVE" at the top of the left panel, and "IMPERATIVE" at the top of the right panel.

key: picks the best way (join algorithm)
name: ch10_cab_driver_declarative
alt: A passenger tells a cab driver just the destination and the driver picks the best route using today's traffic.
scene: A city street at evening rush hour seen from above, with a yellow-and-black taxi in the centre. Inside, a passenger with a suitcase says a short sentence with an airplane icon in his speech bubble. The driver, an experienced man with a moustache and a cap, glances at the traffic, and above the car a map shows three possible routes: one red with a jam, one orange, and one green that he chooses, highlighted. In a small inset at the bottom right, another passenger leans forward giving turn-by-turn directions with hand gestures to reach a tiny shop in a narrow lane, showing when exact directions are still needed. Evening glow, headlights and traffic. The city has flyovers, auto-rickshaws, buses and a flower seller at a signal. The driver's dashboard has a small idol and a jasmine garland. The passenger relaxes back in his seat with a newspaper, trusting the driver, while in the inset the other passenger leans forward pointing and talking fast. The green route curves around the jam and reaches an airport tower in the corner. Labels: "DECLARATIVE" above the passenger's bubble, and "OPTIMISER" over the driver's chosen route.

key: thali restaurant that started with only
name: ch10_thali_vs_fastfood_converge
alt: A thali restaurant adds reusable components while the fast-food stall next door adds a thali, until both menus look similar.
scene: Two eateries side by side on a busy street. On the left, a traditional thali restaurant with a big menu board; its owner in a white kurta is adding new small items to the menu: chutney bowls and stacks of rotis that can be reused across dishes. On the right, a fast-food stall with burgers and fries; its young owner in a cap is painting a thali on his own menu board. In the middle, a small arrow from each side shows ideas crossing over, and a passing customer looks from one board to the other, finding them alike. Behind the counters, the kitchens are visibly different: tandoors and brass vessels on the left, fryers and griddles on the right. Lively street with scooters. Customers queue at both counters: a family at the thali restaurant and college students at the fast-food stall. The thali owner's helper carries a stack of steel bowls, and the fast-food owner's helper carries a tray of fries. The two menu boards are drawn with pictures, not words, and by the end they show many of the same pictures. Labels: "CONVERGENCE" between the two menu boards, and "DIFFERENT KITCHENS" under the two counters.

key: Trains (events) keep arriving all day
name: ch11_station_board_log
alt: A railway station where trains keep arriving, each arrival is appended to a board, and porters, taxi drivers and the canteen read it at their own pace.
scene: A wide, busy railway station concourse seen from a balcony. Along the top of the scene runs a huge announcement board like a long paper roll, with each train arrival written as a new line at the bottom and older lines above never erased, the newest line still being written by a clerk on a small ladder with chalk. Below the board, several readers each have a small bookmark clip attached to a different line: a red-shirted porter with a turban near an older line, a taxi driver leaning on his cab with a clip near the middle, a canteen cook in an apron with a ladle reading near the newest line, and a ticket clerk at a window with her own clip. On the left, a trains-per-hour tally board with hourly columns shows a late train arriving just after its hour closed, and a station staff member hesitating with chalk over the closed column. Through the arches, trains keep pulling in endlessly with steam and crowds. In a side office, the station master writes every coach movement into a register, with a dotted line from it to the big board. Morning light, constant motion. Labels: "LOG" on the long board, "OFFSET" beside one bookmark clip, and "LATE EVENT" over the hesitating staff member.

key: Batch is the milkman who collects every
name: ch11_milkman_vs_pipe
alt: A milkman carries a whole day's milk to the dairy at night, while a pipe sends each litre straight from the cow to the dairy as it is milked.
scene: A split-panel rural illustration with the same cowshed, green fields and a dairy building on the far right of both panels. LEFT panel: a milkman in a white kurta and turban milks several cows into large steel cans through the day, shown by a sun moving across the sky in small stages, and at night under a crescent moon he rides a bicycle loaded with full cans to the dairy, where a dairy clerk with a lantern receives everything at once and writes one daily total. RIGHT panel: the same cowshed with a shiny pipe running from each cow's milking station across the field directly into the dairy, small droplets flowing continuously along it, and the dairy clerk watching a meter tick upward all day. The cows keep grazing and being milked without pause, and a small calendar beside the pipe has no clear end, a dotted line trailing off past the frame. A young girl with a school bag walks along the pipe watching the drops. Pastoral morning light, calm countryside. Labels: "BATCH" at the top of the left panel, and "STREAM" at the top of the right panel.

key: Waiting for an online order: you can
name: ch11_polling_vs_notification
alt: A shopper keeps opening a shop app to check if her order shipped, versus getting a message the moment it ships.
scene: A split-panel illustration in the same small apartment living room with a sofa, a potted money plant and a wall clock. LEFT panel: a young woman in a T-shirt and pyjamas sits cross-legged on the sofa, repeatedly opening a shopping app on her phone; a strip of small identical phone screens floats above her like film frames, each showing the same no-change status with a little grey dash, and the wall clock shows many short intervals ticking by; on the far side, the shop's warehouse server shown as a small building groans under a stream of arrows from her phone and from many other customers. RIGHT panel: she relaxes with a book and a cup of chai while her phone lies face down; a single message bubble with a parcel icon flies from the warehouse building into her phone at the exact moment a delivery van pulls away from the warehouse door, and she glances at it with a smile. A small inset at the bottom of the right panel shows a message bubble falling into a gap, hinting that a message can be lost. Soft afternoon light. Labels: "POLLING" at the top of the left panel, and "NOTIFICATION" at the top of the right panel.

key: A cricket commentator on the radio
name: ch11_radio_commentary_webhook
alt: Listeners hear every ball of a radio commentary as it happens, but anyone whose radio was off misses that over forever, and a promised phone call can fail.
scene: A street scene on a hot afternoon. In the centre, an old transistor radio on a paan shop counter blares cricket commentary, drawn as sound waves full of small ball icons; around it, a cobbler, a schoolboy on a cycle and an auto driver lean in listening, all reacting to the same ball at the same moment. On the left, a man in an office shirt walks up holding a radio he had switched off, and a small balloon behind him shows a whole over of six balls drifting away into the sky, gone. On the right side, a separate vignette: a young woman's phone lies switched off on a desk, and a friend at the stadium holds his phone to his ear with a dead battery icon, the promised call line between them broken. A tiny inset in the corner shows a man at a counter asking for a specific numbered packet to be repeated and a clerk handing it from a short shelf of recent packets. Bright sun, festive cricket mood. Labels: "DIRECT MESSAGING" above the radio, "MISSED" over the drifting balls, and "WEBHOOK" over the broken call line.

key: Combined = the announcement is sent to
name: ch11_dispatch_fanout_departments
alt: One dispatcher gives each order to one free rider, a group announcement reaches everyone, and a notice sent to every department is picked up by one person in each.
scene: A three-panel illustration. PANEL ONE: a delivery dispatcher in a headset sits at a desk with a stack of order slips and hands each slip to exactly one waiting rider in a line of riders on scooters, arrows going one slip to one rider. PANEL TWO: a society secretary on a stage with a microphone makes an announcement that reaches every resident in a crowd, small copies of the same message icon appearing above every head. PANEL THREE: the same announcement envelope is copied to three department rooms: security with guards in berets, housekeeping with staff holding brooms, and accounts with clerks at calculators; in each room only one person reaches out and takes the envelope while colleagues carry on with their work. The panels share a single colour code for the message so the viewer sees one message split, copied, or both. Bright, clean lighting. The riders in panel one wear rain jackets and helmets, each ready at a different moment. Labels: "LOAD BALANCING" at the top of panel one, "FAN-OUT" at the top of panel two, and "BOTH" at the top of panel three.

key: Teller 2 is handling token 3 when she
name: ch11_teller_faints_reorder
alt: A bank teller faints while handling token 3, the manager reassigns it to the other teller who already served token 4, so token 3 is served after 4.
scene: A bank hall with two teller windows side by side and a token display above them. At window two, a young teller in a sari has fainted back in her chair, a colleague fanning her with a file, and on her desk an unstamped slip with token 3 lies under her hand. At window one, a brisk teller in a striped shirt has just stamped a slip with token 4 for a man depositing cash into an account. The manager, a tall man in a grey suit, carries the token 3 slip from window two to window one with a curved arrow, the slip showing an account-opening form icon. A small timeline ribbon at the bottom shows 4 served before 3, with an exclamation mark, and the deposit icon appearing before the new-account icon. In a corner inset, an email envelope is drawn twice, showing a repeated side effect when the work is redone. Ceiling fans, a queue on benches, and a calendar on a pillar fill the background. Bright daylight. Labels: "REDELIVERY" along the manager's curved arrow, and "OUT OF ORDER" above the timeline ribbon.

key: reservation chart for each coach is a
name: ch11_coach_chart_partitions_offsets
alt: Each train coach has its own numbered reservation chart, and a ticket checker keeps a pencil mark of the last line checked in each coach.
scene: A railway platform beside a long train, three coaches visible from left to right. On the side of each coach is pasted a reservation chart with numbered lines going down, each chart in a different pastel colour, and a clerk in a white shirt is writing a new line at the bottom of the middle chart while another clerk writes on the first chart at the same time. A travelling ticket examiner in a black coat and white shirt with a clipboard and a pencil stands between the first two coaches; on each chart there is a small pencil tick beside the last line he has checked, at different heights on each chart, and his clipboard shows two small numbers, one per coach. Passengers with luggage check their names on the charts. An arrow between charts with a question mark shows there is no order across coaches. The station's yellow signboard and a tea vendor are visible. Bright morning light, orderly bustle. Labels: "PARTITION" on one chart, "OFFSET" beside a pencil tick, and "TOPIC" above the whole train.

key: Reading a long novel with a bookmark
name: ch11_bookmark_offset
alt: A reader forgets to move her bookmark after reading on the train, so her friend who picks up the book re-reads the same pages.
scene: A two-scene illustration. LEFT scene: inside a crowded local train compartment, a young woman in a kurti and jeans sits by the window reading a thick novel, absorbed, holding it open to a later page while a ribbon bookmark stays tucked far behind at an earlier page; small page-number tabs on the book edge show the gap between the bookmark and where she is reading. RIGHT scene: at home that evening, the book lies on a table and her roommate in a hoodie picks it up, opens it at the ribbon bookmark, and starts reading pages the first woman already read, a curved arrow showing pages being re-read. A small inset above shows a bill with a coin icon being charged twice, with a warning triangle, hinting why re-reading can be dangerous for real work. Soft evening lamp light, a cup of tea, a cat on the sofa. The train compartment is full of commuters holding overhead handles, a vendor selling peanuts walks through, and stations blur past the window. At home, the roommate sits on a bean bag with a bowl of snacks, unaware that she is repeating pages, while the first woman is seen in the kitchen making dinner. Labels: "CONSUMER OFFSET" beside the bookmark, and "REPROCESSED" over the re-read pages.

key: A CCTV recorder in a shop keeps the last
name: ch11_cctv_retention_loop
alt: A shop's CCTV recorder keeps the last thirty days of footage and overwrites the oldest, so footage from two months ago is gone.
scene: A small jewellery-and-watch shop interior with a glass counter, a ceiling-mounted camera, and a back room with a recording box on a shelf. The recording box is drawn as a circular reel of film frames arranged in a ring of thirty segments, like a clock face, with a write head adding a new frame and erasing the oldest one right in front of it, a curved arrow showing the loop. At the front of the shop, a police constable in khaki with a notebook asks the shop owner, a middle-aged man in a cardigan, for old footage; the owner spreads his hands apologetically, and a thought bubble shows a calendar with the requested date beyond the ring, crossed out. On the shelf next to the box, a larger disk drive and a dimmer, lower-detail camera icon sit as alternatives that would keep more days. Fluorescent shop light, glittering display. A wall calendar behind the owner shows the past month highlighted and earlier months greyed out. A customer in the shop tries on a watch, oblivious, and a second camera above the door blinks a small red light. Labels: "RETENTION" above the ring of frames, and "OVERWRITTEN" on the erased oldest frame.

key: A new analyst can rewind to ball 1
name: ch11_match_recording_replay
alt: A recorded cricket broadcast lets a new analyst rewind to ball one and count boundaries a new way while the live commentary team carries on.
scene: A sports broadcast building with two rooms side by side. In the left room, the live commentary team, two commentators in blazers with headsets, talk into microphones in front of a window over a floodlit stadium, a large live feed on their screen. In the right room, a young data analyst in a hoodie sits at a desk with a monitor showing the same match rewound to the very first ball, a rewind arrow icon on the screen, and she taps on a notepad tallying boundary icons with her own new method. Between the rooms, a long film strip runs from the stadium into a recording cabinet, and from the cabinet two arrows branch out, one to each room, neither disturbing the other. At the far end of the film strip, older frames fade away, showing that the recording is kept only for a while. Evening floodlights, focused mood. The analyst has a mug of coffee and sticky notes on her monitor, and the commentators gesture excitedly at a six. The recording cabinet is drawn like a large film archive with labelled reels on shelves. Labels: "REPLAY" over the analyst's screen, and "INDEPENDENT CONSUMERS" between the two rooms.

key: A chess game sent by post: each player
name: ch11_chess_by_post
alt: Two chess players in different cities keep their own boards and send only moves by post, so the boards stay identical.
scene: A split illustration of two homes in different towns. On the left, an elderly retired professor in a shawl sits at a wooden chessboard on a veranda with a hill view; on the right, a young woman in a college sweatshirt sits at an identical chessboard at a desk in a city flat. The boards show exactly the same arrangement of pieces. Between them, a postman on a bicycle carries a small postcard with only a tiny arrow drawing of one piece's move, no board. Each player holds a postcard from the other and moves the matching piece. A ribbon of earlier postcards is pinned on each wall in the same order. A tiny inset at the bottom shows a postcard with a die and a question mark crossed out, meaning moves must not depend on chance. Warm afternoon light on the left, cool evening light on the right. The professor wears round spectacles and has a pipe resting in an ashtray, a cat curled on the chair beside him; the young woman has a laptop closed beside her board and a mug with a pencil in it. The postcards are simple, each with a stamp and a single arrow, and both walls show identical rows of them, proving that the same moves in the same order produce the same board. Labels: "SAME MOVES" on the postcard, and "SAME STATE" between the two identical boards.

key: Two family members update the address
name: ch11_dual_write_address
alt: Mother and father each phone the shop and then the courier with different flat numbers, the calls arrive in different orders, and the parcel goes to the wrong flat.
scene: A four-corner illustration. Top left: a mother in a house dress on a phone at home; top right: a father in office clothes on a phone at a bus stop. Bottom left: an online shop's call-centre desk (generic, no logo) with an operator writing the address; bottom right: a courier office desk with another operator writing. Two coloured call lines leave each parent: the mother's in pink, the father's in blue. At the shop desk, the pink call arrives first and the blue second, so the operator's notepad shows the blue flat number; at the courier desk, the order is reversed, blue first then pink, and that notepad shows the pink number. Both operators say a cheerful OK. In the centre, a delivery boy on a scooter stands confused between two apartment doors with different numbers, holding a parcel. Daylight, comic mix-up mood. The four people at the desks look busy and confident, writing down whatever they heard last. A small clock beside each desk shows the order of arrivals, making the crossing order visible. The two apartment doors in the centre are side by side with similar brass numbers, and a neighbour peeks out of one door holding the wrong parcel. Labels: "DUAL WRITES" above the crossing call lines, and "INCONSISTENT" over the confused delivery boy.

key: In a school, only the class teacher
name: ch11_register_daily_changes
alt: Only the class teacher's register is the truth; the office, canteen and bus coordinator each receive an ordered photocopy of its daily changes.
scene: A school illustrated as a hub-and-spoke diagram with real people. In the centre, a class teacher in a crisp sari marks the official attendance register on her desk, a gold star on its cover. From her desk, a peon carries a stack of photocopied change slips, numbered in order, along three paths to three places: the school office where a clerk files them, the canteen where a cook in an apron updates a meal count chalkboard, and the bus bay where a coordinator with a whistle ticks a route list. None of these three takes attendance on its own. The canteen's path is longer and the peon has stopped to chat there, so the canteen's chalkboard still shows yesterday's number while the others are current, a small clock icon beside it. Morning sunlight, school buses, children with tiffin boxes. The three destinations are spaced around the teacher like points of a triangle, and the slips the peon carries have small sequence numbers so the viewer sees they must be applied in order. Children in uniforms line up at the canteen, one asking for a meal that is not on yesterday's count. Labels: "SYSTEM OF RECORD" on the teacher's register, and "CHANGE DATA CAPTURE" along the peon's paths.

key: Triggers are like asking every cashier
name: ch11_till_roll_vs_triggers
alt: Asking every cashier to copy each sale into a second notebook slows them down, while reading the till's own printed roll at day's end adds nothing for them.
scene: A split-panel supermarket checkout illustration. LEFT panel: a cashier in a uniform scans items and, after every customer, also writes the sale into a second notebook beside the register; she looks harried, sweat on her brow, a queue lengthening behind, and one line in the notebook is left blank where she forgot. RIGHT panel: the cashier works smoothly without any extra notebook, and the till's printer spits out a long paper roll curling to the floor; in the back office at closing time, an accounts clerk in spectacles reads the whole roll with a ruler and copies it out. A small inset on the right shows the same roll with a changed print layout and the clerk squinting, hinting at a schema change. Bright store light. The left panel's second notebook is drawn thick and messy, with smudges and crossed-out lines, and a manager stands behind the cashier with a stopwatch. In the right panel, the till roll curls gracefully like a ribbon across the floor into the back office door. The accounts clerk sips tea, a calculator and a ruler beside him, and he has a small reference card showing the roll's layout. Customers in both panels hold baskets of everyday goods without brands. Labels: "TRIGGERS" at the top of the left panel, and "LOG PARSING" at the top of the right panel.

key: rather than scrolling through 50,000 old
name: ch11_pinned_summary_snapshot
alt: A new member joining a long-running group chat receives a pinned summary as of message one thousand and reads only from the next message on.
scene: A phone screen enlarged in the centre of the picture, held by a young man in a college jacket who has just joined a group chat (generic, no logo). At the top of the screen, a pinned card shows a summary document icon with a small badge marking the exact message number it covers. Below it, messages continue from the very next number downward. To the left of the phone, a tall stack of thousands of tiny message bubbles rises like a skyscraper, crossed out lightly to show he does not need to read them. To the right, a small inset shows a summary card without any number, and the young man shrugs with two arrows, one skipping messages and one repeating them, showing the danger. Background: a hostel common room with friends watching TV. Soft evening light. The friends in the background laugh at a comedy on TV, and one leans over to point at the pinned card. The skyscraper of old messages leans slightly, comically tall, with a tiny window cleaner on it. The first new message under the pinned card is highlighted with a soft glow, so the starting point is unmistakable. Labels: "SNAPSHOT" on the pinned card, and "START FROM HERE" at the first new message.

key: it only needs the latest number per
name: ch11_contacts_compaction
alt: A phone contacts sync log full of edits is compacted to only the latest number per person, keeping a marker that one contact was deleted.
scene: A split illustration. LEFT side: an old phone with a long scrolling log ribbon coming out of it like a receipt, listing many entries over the years, each a small contact card icon with a name initial and a phone icon, several cards for the same person with different numbers, and one card with a trash-can icon. RIGHT side: a brand-new phone receives a much shorter ribbon with just one card per person, the latest number only, and a small grey tombstone card with the deleted person's initial still present. A pair of scissors and a sweeping brush between the two ribbons show the compaction step. A young woman holds both phones, smiling at the short ribbon. A small clock icon on the tombstone card shows it will be kept only for a while. Bright desk-lamp light. The old phone has a cracked screen and a worn case; the new phone is shiny in a box with its charger. The long ribbon on the left curls across a desk and onto the floor, while the short ribbon on the right fits neatly on one card. A desk calendar, a coffee mug and a pen holder fill the scene, and the young woman sits in a home office chair with a relieved smile. Labels: "LOG COMPACTION" over the scissors, and "TOMBSTONE" on the grey card.

key: you stand under the board and watch
name: ch11_platform_change_sms
alt: Instead of standing under the station board waiting for a platform change, a passenger gets a message the moment it changes.
scene: A split-panel railway station illustration. LEFT panel: a tired traveller with a suitcase and a shawl stands craning his neck under a big departure board for a long time, a clock above showing an hour passing, and a man nearby secretly listens to a staff walkie-talkie through a crack in a door. RIGHT panel: the same traveller sits relaxed in the waiting room with a cup of tea, and his phone buzzes with a message bubble showing a train icon and a platform number arrow; at the same moment, far away in the station control room, an operator changes the platform on a panel, and a dotted line connects the panel to his phone. A small note on the right shows that only certain information is shared, with a few other control-room switches greyed out. Evening station lighting. In the left panel, other passengers also stand under the board with luggage and children, all staring upward, necks stiff. In the right panel, the waiting room has ceiling fans, wooden benches and a tea vendor, and the traveller's wife reads a magazine beside him. The control-room operator wears a headset and sits before a panel of switches and track diagrams. Labels: "WATCH THE BOARD" at the top of the left panel, and "CHANGE STREAM" at the top of the right panel.

key: CDC is a security camera filming the
name: ch11_camera_vs_day_book
alt: A security camera records how many boxes are on a shelf without knowing why, while the shopkeeper's day book records each sale and return with its reason.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same small grocery store. LEFT panel: a ceiling camera points at a shelf of biscuit boxes; below it, a monitor shows a series of snapshots of the shelf with the box count changing, two boxes, then three, then two, but no people visible, and a puzzled question mark floating over the screen. RIGHT panel: the shopkeeper, a cheerful woman in a cotton sari with spectacles, writes in a thick day book at the counter while a boy buys a biscuit packet; the open book shows small icons: a sold packet with a coin, then a returned packet with a cracked biscuit and an arrow back, each line with a little clock. A small inset shows a forgotten line in the book with a blank space. Warm shop light. The two panels share the same shelf layout so the viewer can compare: the camera's snapshots are grey and impersonal, while the day book's lines are warm and human. The boy holds his biscuit packet and a coin, and a returned packet sits on the counter with a crack. Shelves of rice, dal, soap and candles fill the background without brand names. Labels: "CDC" at the top of the left panel, and "EVENT SOURCING" at the top of the right panel.

key: Once the ticket is printed
name: ch11_cinema_command_vs_event
alt: At a cinema counter a seat request may be refused, but once a ticket is printed it is a fact; a cancellation is a separate record.
scene: A cinema foyer with a ticket counter, film posters (generic) and a popcorn stand. On the left at the counter, a young man asks for a seat, a speech bubble with a seat icon and a question mark; the clerk checks a seat map on a screen and might say no, shown by a small hand gesture. In the centre, a ticket printer pushes out a printed ticket with a seat icon and a little tick, glowing like a stamped fact. On the right, the usher at the hall door, an older man with a torch, tears the ticket's stub and lets him in without arguing. In a back corner, a separate small cancellation slip is printed for another customer and filed in a tray, while her original ticket stays in the record book, not erased. Warm foyer lighting, red carpet. The young man in a denim jacket holds a phone and a popcorn tub; the clerk wears a waistcoat and a name badge. The record book on a shelf behind the counter is open to show the printed tickets and the cancellation as separate lines one after another. Moviegoers queue behind, and a poster of a generic hero with sunglasses hangs on the wall. Labels: "COMMAND" over the request bubble, "EVENT" on the printed ticket, and "NEW RECORD" on the cancellation slip.

key: odometer is the state (total km)
name: ch11_odometer_speedometer
alt: A car dashboard with a speedometer showing the stream of speed and an odometer showing the accumulated distance.
scene: A close-up of a car's dashboard at night on a highway, seen from the driver's seat, the road and headlights visible through the windscreen. On the left, a round speedometer with a moving needle, small motion lines showing it changing moment to moment. On the right, an odometer with rolling digits slowly counting up. A glowing curved arrow runs from the speedometer to the odometer showing that adding up speed over time gives distance, and a second arrow runs back the other way showing that the change in distance gives speed. The driver's hands on the steering wheel wear a steel bracelet, and a small idol and a jasmine garland hang from the rear-view mirror. Night city lights in the distance. A small inset at the top right shows a graph of speed over time with the area under it shaded, and a second small graph of distance rising steadily, linked by the same arrows. Highway signs glide past outside, a truck's tail lights glow ahead, and the passenger seat holds a water bottle and a road map. The driver's eyes are visible in the rear-view mirror, calm and focused. The whole dashboard glows a soft blue and amber. Labels: "STREAM" above the speedometer, and "STATE" above the odometer.

key: A school answer sheet in pen: if you
name: ch11_strike_out_vs_whitener
alt: A student strikes out a wrong answer with a single line so the examiner can still see it, while whitener that hides history is banned.
scene: A close-up of an exam desk with an answer sheet written in blue ink. One line has a single neat strike-through, and the correct answer is written beside it; the struck words are still readable through the line. A student's hand holds a pen ready, a steel geometry box and a hall ticket on the desk. At the edge of the desk, a small bottle of correction fluid sits inside a red circle with a slash, banned. Behind, an examiner in spectacles leans over and reads both the struck answer and the correction with a nod, a magnifying glass in hand. Classroom background with rows of desks and a clock. Soft daylight. The student is a teenage girl in a school uniform with a braid and a wristwatch, writing carefully, and her rough work in the margin shows small calculations. The examiner's red pen marks a tick next to the correction and a small note acknowledging the first attempt. A rule poster on the classroom wall shows the same banned bottle icon. Other students write quietly at desks in the background, and an invigilator walks slowly down the aisle. The light falls across the desk so the struck line is clearly visible. Labels: "APPEND ONLY" above the struck line, and "NO OVERWRITE" beside the banned bottle.

key: order slips (the log) are written once
name: ch11_order_slips_many_views
alt: A restaurant's order slips are written once and read by the kitchen, cashier and owner to build their own boards, and later re-read for a new chart.
scene: A restaurant back area with a long spike rail holding a growing row of handwritten order slips in time order. From the rail, three dotted arrows lead to three people: the kitchen chef updating a dishes-to-cook board with magnets, the cashier at the counter preparing bills per table on a calculator, and the owner, a confident woman in a salwar kameez, filling a sales-by-dish sheet with tally marks. On the right, the owner is shown again at a desk under a lamp reading through the same slips from the beginning to build a new bar chart of the busiest hour, while the chef and cashier carry on untouched. Warm evening restaurant light. The kitchen chef wears a tall white cap, the cashier is a young man with a pen behind his ear, and the owner wears gold earrings and a watch. The spike rail is long and the slips are numbered by small clock icons, so the viewer sees that the same slips feed every board. The new bar chart has one tall bar for the busy evening hour. Waiters carry plates through the swinging kitchen door, and the dining room beyond is full of families. Labels: "EVENT LOG" above the spike rail, and "DERIVED VIEWS" over the three boards.

key: You post a photo and immediately open
name: ch11_photo_profile_lag
alt: A woman posts a photo and opens her profile, but it is not there yet because a helper reads the post log a second later.
scene: A young woman in a café holds up her phone after posting a photo of her coffee. The phone screen is enlarged, split into two moments: first a posting confirmation with a tick, then her profile page with an empty square where the photo should be and a small question mark. Behind the phone, a conveyor belt carries a single card with a photo icon from a log box to a profile box, a friendly helper figure with a cap reading the card and carrying it a second later, a little clock showing one second. A small inset shows the photo appearing in her profile, feed and a like counter all at once, without any lock. Warm café lighting, plants and a chalkboard menu. The young woman is in her twenties, with curly hair and a denim jacket, and her friend sitting across the table laughs at her puzzled face. The helper on the conveyor walks at a steady pace, and behind him other cards for a feed and a counter move along parallel belts. The second frame of her phone, a moment later, shows the photo in place, drawn as a small strip of two frames. Labels: "ASYNC VIEW" over the conveyor, and "ONE WRITE" on the log box.

key: Deleting a forwarded WhatsApp message
name: ch11_forwarded_message_copies
alt: A man deletes a forwarded message for everyone, but copies survive in a screenshot, a cloud backup and another group.
scene: A young man in a T-shirt holds his phone and presses a delete-for-everyone option, a small trash can icon with a sparkle. Around him, connected by dotted lines, are the surviving copies: a friend's phone showing a screenshot of the message in its gallery; a cloud icon labelled with a backup box holding the message; and another group chat on a third phone where the message has been forwarded again, a small forward arrow icon. Each copy glows faintly. The young man looks hopeful but slightly worried. Bright daytime room. The room is a hostel room with a bunk bed and posters. The friend with the screenshot is a girl in a library chuckling at her phone; the cloud backup is drawn as a fluffy cloud holding a small locked box; the third phone belongs to an uncle in a family group who has already forwarded it further, with tiny forward arrows spreading out like ripples. The dotted lines from the young man's phone to each copy are faint, showing he has no control over them. His expression shifts from relief to realisation in a small two-frame strip beside him. Labels: "DELETED HERE" over his phone, and "COPIES REMAIN" over the three surviving copies.

key: A sugarcane juice line: cane goes in
name: ch11_sugarcane_juice_pipeline
alt: Sugarcane flows into a crusher, juice is filtered, and the result goes either into bottles for a fridge or straight into a customer's glass.
scene: A roadside sugarcane juice stall in bright summer. On the left, a bundle of green sugarcane stalks keeps arriving on a cart pulled by a man in a vest, an endless line of stalks stretching back down the road.
