In the centre, a green-painted crusher with big rollers and a hand wheel squeezes the cane, juice flowing into a steel tray, then through a cloth filter with lemon and ginger into a jug. At the right end, the jug's output splits two ways: a numbered circle 1 points to a row of glass bottles going into a shop fridge, and a numbered circle 2 points to a customer, a sweaty schoolboy, gulping from a tall glass. A small inset shows the crusher jammed with smoke and a calendar with the season's start crossed out. Hot sunlight, flies, bright greens. The stall owner is a cheerful man with a moustache and a towel on his head, turning the wheel, and his helper adds ice and lemon. Customers wait in the shade of a tree, and a scooter is parked nearby. Labels: "OPERATOR" on the crusher, and "DERIVED STREAM" along the filtered juice.

key: a stream processor watching your card
name: ch11_card_fraud_pattern
alt: A bank system spots one card used in two distant cities minutes apart and sends a was-this-you message in real time.
scene: A map of two distant cities connected by a long dashed arc, each city with a small shop icon and a card swipe machine. In the left city, a man in a business shirt swipes his card at a café; three minutes later, according to a little clock icon, the same card is swiped at a jewellery shop in the far city by a shadowy hooded figure. Above the map, a watchful robot with binoculars sits on a stream of card swipe icons flowing past like a ribbon, and it raises a red flag when the two swipes match a pattern drawn as two pins far apart with a small timer. The man's phone buzzes with a message bubble with a question mark. A small inset shows a genuine traveller with a suitcase whose card is blocked, frowning. Clean lighting. The two cities are drawn as small skylines, one with a dome and one with tall glass towers, far apart across the map, and a small plane icon shows that nobody could travel that fast. The ribbon of swipe icons flows like a river beneath the robot, each icon with a tiny clock. The man at the café holds a cup of coffee and looks surprised at his phone. Labels: "PATTERN MATCH" above the robot, and "ALERT" over the man's phone.

key: The instruction (query) stays posted on
name: ch11_cctv_operator_standing_query
alt: A CCTV operator follows an instruction posted on the wall while people stream past the camera, calling when a pattern appears.
scene: A security control room with a wall of CCTV monitors showing a shopping mall entrance and a jewellery counter. A night-shift operator in a uniform sits with a radio, and on the wall beside the screens an instruction card is pinned, drawn as a little comic strip of three icons: a person entering a door three times, then walking towards a ring icon, then a phone. On the screens, a stream of shoppers walks past the camera; one woman in a red scarf is circled faintly on three different screens, and the operator reaches for the phone. A coffee mug and a yawning expression show human fatigue. Dim control room light with screen glow. Behind the operator, a shift chart and a fire extinguisher hang on the wall, and a second operator dozes in a chair with a newspaper. The screens show a mall with escalators, a food court and a jewellery counter with glass cases. The circled woman in the red scarf appears at different times on each screen, each with a small clock, so the pattern builds up over time while the instruction card stays fixed on the wall. The operator's hand is on the phone, ready to call. Labels: "STANDING QUERY" on the instruction card, and "EVENTS" over the stream of shoppers.

key: Your query sits on their server; every
name: ch11_property_alert_index
alt: A property website keeps users' saved alerts on its server and checks each new listing only against alerts for the same city.
scene: A large server room drawn as a sorting office. Saved alert cards from many users hang on racks grouped by city, each rack with a small skyline icon. A new property listing card with a house icon and a city tag drops in from the top, and a robot clerk reads its city tag and walks only to the matching rack, comparing it against those alert cards, ignoring all other racks, which are greyed out. When a card matches, a little bell rings and a message flies to a young couple on a sofa holding a phone, delighted. A crossed-out inset shows the same robot exhausted walking past every rack in the country. Clean modern lighting. The racks look like library shelves with cards clipped on, each card showing a small house icon, a price tag and a bed count. The robot clerk has a friendly face and a tag on its chest. The young couple on the sofa are in their early thirties, the woman pointing at the phone and the man smiling with a cup of tea. Through a window, a city skyline at dusk matches the rack's skyline icon. The crossed-out inset shows the robot sweating with a map of the whole country behind it. Labels: "SAVED QUERIES" above the racks, and "INDEXED BY CITY" over the matching rack.

key: Counting wedding gifts by when they were
name: ch11_gift_envelopes_event_time
alt: Gift envelopes given over a wedding day are opened two days later, so counting by opening time says everyone gave gifts at once.
scene: A split illustration. LEFT: at a wedding reception, guests in silk clothes hand envelopes to the couple at different times, shown by a row of small clocks above them at morning, afternoon and evening. RIGHT: two days later at home late at night, the same couple sit on the floor in pyjamas surrounded by opened envelopes, a single wall clock showing late night, and a tally sheet where all gifts are marked at one time, a single tall bar. A second small tally sheet beside it, built from tiny dates written on some envelopes, shows bars spread across the wedding day. A cat sleeps on a pile of wrapping paper. Warm lamp light. On the left, the bride in a red lehenga and the groom in a cream sherwani stand on a decorated stage receiving envelopes, and the guests include an elderly uncle, a cousin with a baby and a group of college friends. On the right, the couple yawns, pens and a calculator scattered around, and the clock on the wall dominates the room. The two tally sheets are drawn as simple bar charts side by side so the difference is immediately visible. Labels: "EVENT TIME" over the spread tally, and "PROCESSING TIME" over the single tall bar.

key: A toll booth counter clicks each car as
name: ch11_toll_clerk_tea_break
alt: A toll clerk takes a tea break and then counts the backlog quickly, making his cars-per-minute sheet show a gap and a spike though traffic was steady.
scene: A highway toll booth from the side. On the road, cars arrive at a steady, evenly spaced rhythm, drawn as a regular row. The counting clerk, a young man in a reflective vest, is shown away at a tea stall with a glass of tea, his booth empty, and cars bunching up at the barrier. Then he rushes back and waves them through quickly, clicking his counter. Above the booth, his sheet shows a chart with a flat zero and then a tall spike. On the toll gate a small camera with a clock captures each car's arrival time, and a second chart beside it is flat and steady. Afternoon sun, dusty road. The tea stall is a small cart with a kettle and glasses under an umbrella, and the clerk chats with the tea seller while drivers honk at the barrier. Truck drivers lean out of their windows, and a family car waits with children pressing their faces to the glass. The two charts float above the booth like signs, one jagged and one flat, so the viewer can compare them. A highway sign and a line of eucalyptus trees run along the road, heat shimmering above the asphalt. Labels: "PROCESSING TIME" over the spiky chart, and "EVENT TIME" over the flat chart.

key: wristwatch runs 30 minutes slow
name: ch11_slow_watch_diary_offset
alt: A friend's slow watch makes her diary times wrong, so comparing her watch with a correct clock during a phone call lets her correct them.
scene: A two-location illustration. LEFT: a young woman in a kurti sits at a café writing in a small diary, her wristwatch drawn enlarged and showing an earlier time than the café's wall clock, and in the diary a small handshake icon marks meeting a friend. RIGHT: later, she calls a friend at home whose wall clock shows the correct time; a dotted phone line connects them, and an inset bubble shows the two clocks side by side with a bracket measuring the gap. A curved arrow then shifts the diary time forward by that gap to the true meeting time. A tiny inset warns that if the call took long to connect, the correction is off, shown by a slow hourglass on the phone line. Warm café and evening home lighting. The café has wooden tables, a coffee machine and a chalkboard menu, and her friend at home sits on a sofa with a cushion and a TV remote. The diary is open with a pen resting on it, its entries drawn as small icons with clock faces. The bracket between the two clocks is bright and clear, and the arrow moving the diary time is drawn in a different colour so the correction step stands out. Labels: "DEVICE CLOCK" on her watch, and "OFFSET" on the bracket.

key: A restaurant wants to know how many
name: ch11_waiter_two_notepads
alt: A waiter keeps two notepads for the last hour, one for menus given and one for orders, and matches them by table to count who ordered.
scene: A busy restaurant dining room. A waiter in a white uniform holds two small notepads, one in each hand, one marked with a menu icon and one with a plate icon. Above each notepad float little entries with table numbers and small clocks. At table five, a family receives a menu, and later the same family orders, a dotted line connecting the two entries across the notepads. At another table, a couple leaves without ordering, their menu entry with no partner, marked with an empty circle. A large hourglass on the wall shows the one-hour window, and a family arriving back much later is outside the window, faded. Warm lighting, clinking plates. The restaurant has wooden tables with checked cloths, a family at table five with two children reading menus, and a couple at a window table putting on their jackets to leave. The waiter's face is focused, his eyes moving between the two pads, and dotted lines connect matching entries. A kitchen hatch with a bell and a chef's hat is visible in the back. The hourglass is drawn large on the wall like a decorative clock. Labels: "STREAM JOIN" between the two notepads, and "WINDOW" on the hourglass.

key: A delivery app where every order (event)
name: ch11_hub_address_books
alt: Each delivery hub keeps its own address book updated by change slips from head office, so orders are enriched locally instead of phoning head office.
scene: A map illustration with a head office building in the centre and three delivery hubs around it. From head office, a clerk sends small address-change slips along dotted lines to every hub. Inside each hub, a dispatcher keeps a local address book on the desk and copies in each slip, and as order cards arrive on a belt, she quickly writes the address from her local book onto each card and hands it to a rider. A crossed-out inset shows the old way: a dispatcher phoning head office for every order, with a long queue of riders waiting. At one hub, a change slip is still on its way, and one rider leaves with an old address, a small warning icon. Clean daytime colours. Each hub is a small warehouse with roller shutters, scooters parked outside and riders in helmets waiting with insulated bags. The dispatcher at the nearest hub is a young woman with a headset and a pen, and her address book is thick with tabs and freshly glued slips. Head office is a taller glass building with a clerk at a window sending slips like paper aeroplanes. The warned rider looks at his card with a puzzled expression as he rides off. Labels: "LOCAL TABLE" on a hub's address book, and "CHANGELOG" along the slips from head office.

key: A newspaper delivery boy. Every morning
name: ch11_newspaper_boy_timelines
alt: A newspaper boy drops each paper into every subscriber's letterbox, gives new subscribers back issues, and pulls recalled papers from every box.
scene: An early morning residential street with a row of houses, each with a letterbox. A teenage newspaper boy on a bicycle with a canvas bag full of papers drops copies into every letterbox along a dotted route. At one house a new family stands at the gate receiving a small bundle of this week's back issues. At another house a family waves goodbye as the boy takes the unread pile from their box. Further along, he reaches into several boxes to pull out a paper with a red error stamp, collecting them into a recall sack. A follows list on his handlebar shows which houses get papers. Dawn light, milk packets on doorsteps. The houses are colourful with gates, potted plants and dogs sleeping on doorsteps, and the boy wears a cap, shorts and a sweater. His follows list is a small card clipped to the handlebar with house icons and ticks. The recalled papers have a small red stamp and are tucked into a separate sack slung across his chest. A milkman on another cycle passes by, and an old man doing morning exercises waves. Labels: "TIMELINE" on a letterbox, and "MATERIALIZED" over the bundle of back issues.

key: Your salary credit and your EMI debit
name: ch11_salary_emi_order
alt: A salary credit and an EMI debit arrive at the same time, and whether the EMI bounces depends only on which the bank processes first.
scene: A split-panel illustration showing the same bank account as a glass piggy bank. Both panels show two envelopes arriving at nine on the first of the month, a salary envelope with coins and an EMI envelope with a house icon. LEFT panel: the salary envelope goes in first, the piggy bank fills, then the EMI is paid out with a green tick, and the account holder smiles. RIGHT panel: the EMI envelope tries to take money first from the nearly empty piggy bank and bounces back with a red cross and a penalty coin falling, the account holder looking upset, and only then the salary arrives. A bank cut-off rule board between the panels shows a clock with a line. Clean bank colours. The account holder is a young office worker in a shirt and tie, shown at a desk with a laptop and a calendar showing the first of the month circled. The envelopes are drawn with clear icons, coins for salary and a small house for the EMI. A small clock in each panel shows both arriving at nearly the same moment, so the only difference is the order of processing. A bank clerk figure in the background of each panel processes envelopes from a tray, picking a different one first in each panel. Labels: "ORDER MATTERS" between the panels, and "BOUNCED" over the right panel's EMI.

key: Writing an exam in rough first, then
name: ch11_rough_copy_vs_live_anchor
alt: A student tears up a rough page and only hands in a clean copy, while a live TV anchor must correct herself on air.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: an exam desk with a student scribbling on a rough sheet, a crumpled torn page in a bin, and a neat clean answer sheet being handed to the examiner. RIGHT panel: a TV studio with a news anchor in a blazer speaking to a camera with a red on-air light; a small speech bubble shows her correcting a slip mid-sentence with a little correction mark, and viewers at home on a sofa already hearing every word. A small inset shows a short hold timer before airing, a microbatch. Studio lights and classroom daylight. The student is a boy in a white shirt with an ink-stained finger and a wristwatch, and the examiner is a calm woman with a stack of clean answer sheets. The TV studio has a desk with a laptop, bright lights, a camera operator and a teleprompter, and the viewers at home are a family with a grandfather leaning forward to listen. The anchor's expression is composed despite the slip, her hand making a small gesture of correction. The two panels share a central divider with a small clock, and the left side feels relaxed while the right feels live and immediate. Labels: "BATCH" at the top of the left panel, and "STREAM" at the top of the right panel.

key: a bus that leaves the stop every minute
name: ch11_bus_microbatch_double_post
alt: A bus leaves every minute with whoever is waiting, and a gamer who replays from a save posts the same victory twice because the post cannot be undone.
scene: A split illustration. LEFT: a bus stop with a big clock; a small bus departs every minute with whoever happens to be there, a few people boarding, the next bus already approaching. RIGHT: a teenage gamer in a bedroom reaches a level-five victory screen and posts it on a social app, a speech bubble with a trophy icon flying out to friends; then his character dies, the game rewinds to a save flag, he replays level five, and a second identical trophy post flies out, two identical bubbles appearing on a friend's phone with a raised eyebrow. A small undo button on his phone is greyed out. Evening light. The bus stop has a tin roof, a bench and a timetable, and the buses are small and identical. The gamer's room has a poster, a gaming chair and a bowl of chips, and his friend appears in a small circle on the right holding a phone with the two identical trophy bubbles. The save flag in the game is drawn as a glowing banner on a small map, and the rewind arrow loops clearly back to it. The gamer facepalms on noticing the duplicate. Labels: "MICROBATCH" over the bus stop, "CHECKPOINT" on the save flag, and "DUPLICATE" over the two posts.

key: A property registration: money transfer
name: ch11_property_registration_atomic
alt: At a sub-registrar's office, payment, stamp duty, deed and the land record change all count only once one registration entry is made.
scene: A sub-registrar's office with a large wooden counter, a big register book and a rubber stamp. Around the register, four items are tied with a ribbon to a single entry line: a bundle of money, a stamp paper, a sale deed with a house drawing, and a land record card with the new owner's portrait. The sub-registrar, a stern woman in a cotton sari and spectacles, is about to write the single entry. The buyer and seller sit across with a lawyer and witnesses. A small inset shows the same four items greyed out and invisible to a waiting crowd when the entry has not been made. Fluorescent office light, files and fans. The buyer is a young couple in formal clothes holding a folder, and the seller is an elderly man in a white kurta with a walking stick. The lawyer in a black coat points at the register, and the witnesses sign on a side sheet. The ribbon tying the four items to the single entry line is bright red and tight, so the viewer understands they all belong to one moment. Behind the counter, steel cupboards hold old registers, a ceiling fan turns, and a calendar and a clock hang on the wall. Labels: "ONE COMMIT RECORD" on the register line, and "ATOMIC" on the ribbon.

key: Pressing a lift button five times is
name: ch11_lift_button_samosa_slip
alt: Pressing a lift button five times brings one lift, but ordering a samosa five times brings five plates unless the waiter checks the slip number.
scene: A split illustration. LEFT: an office lobby where an impatient man in a suit presses a lift button repeatedly, five tap marks around his finger, and only one lift arrives with doors opening. RIGHT: a restaurant where a hungry college student orders samosas several times; a waiter holds an order slip with a big number and checks a spike of served slips, finding the same number already served, and waves off a duplicate plate. A small inset shows two waiters, not talking, both delivering plates to the same table, with a fence icon between them to show what prevents it. Bright lobby and warm restaurant light. The office lobby has marble floors, a potted palm and a floor indicator above the lift doors with a single arrow. The restaurant has a glass counter of samosas and jalebis, steam rising from a kadai, and the student grins sheepishly at his repeated orders. The order slip is large with a single bold number, and the spike of served slips shows the same number already pinned. The waiter is an older man with a moustache and a towel on his shoulder, calmly raising a hand to refuse the duplicate plate. Labels: "IDEMPOTENT" over the lift, and "DEDUP BY ID" over the slip spike.

key: udhaar (credit) notebook. Options
name: ch11_udhaar_notebook_state
alt: Four ways a shopkeeper keeps a credit notebook safe: at the bank, a nightly photocopy, texting each entry to his brother, or re-adding today's bills.
scene: A four-panel grid around a small kirana shop. Top left: the shopkeeper walks to a bank with the credit notebook for every entry, sweating, the notebook in a bank locker. Top right: at night he photocopies the notebook at a shop with a photocopy machine, a stack of copies piling. Bottom left: after every new entry he sends a text message to his brother, whose phone fills with small entry bubbles. Bottom right: he re-adds only today's bills on a calculator from a small pile of slips, while a tall dusty pile of ten years of slips is crossed out. The same shopkeeper, a middle-aged man in a vest and dhoti, appears in all four panels. Warm everyday light. Each panel has a small clock or calendar icon showing the cost: many trips, a nightly copy, a message per entry, or a quick evening recount. The credit notebook is the same red cloth-bound book in all four panels. His brother in the bottom-left panel is a younger man in a city flat reading the messages with a smile. Labels: "REMOTE STORE" in the top-left panel, "SNAPSHOT" in the top-right panel, and "CHANGELOG" in the bottom-left panel.
